latest.title: Building Trust for Second-Hand Purchase on P2P Resale Platforms: Interactive Effect of Seller-Generated Content and Relationship Norms
latest.abstract: Second-hand consumption on peer-to-peer (P2P) online platforms, as a form of extended product use, is often associated with circular economy initiatives. Yet consumer participation in these markets remains constrained by uncertainty and a lack of trust in sellers. While seller-generated content (SGC) can help build consumer trust, the specific psychological mechanisms through which different SGC types promote second-hand purchase intention remain underexplored. Drawing on relationship norms theory and signaling theory, this study differentiates competence-based trust from benevolence-based trust and explores how the interplay between SGC types and relationship norms facilitates consumers’ second-hand purchase intention via distinct trust pathways. Through three experiments, we demonstrate that seller-generated content (informational vs. emotional) and relationship norms (exchange vs. communal) interact to influence consumers’ second-hand purchase intention. Specifically, informational seller-generated content is more effective under exchange relationship norms in fostering competence-based trust and promoting purchase intention, whereas emotional seller-generated content is more effective under communal relationship norms in strengthening benevolence-based trust and driving purchase intention. These findings contribute to research on trust formation and consumer decision-making in P2P resale markets and offer practical implications for designing norm-congruent seller communication on second-hand platforms.

latest.title: Attention Economy and Marketing Mechanisms: A Comparison of Low- and High-Involvement Products
latest.venue: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
latest.abstract: In the era of the attention economy, consumer attention has become an increasingly scarce and valuable marketing resource. With the rapid development of digital platforms and algorithmic recommendation technologies, the way firms acquire and utilize consumer attention has undergone significant changes. This paper uses a conceptual analysis examines how attention-based marketing mechanisms differ across products with different levels of consumer involvement. By integrating insights from attention-based marketing theory and consumer decision-making literature, this paper analyzes two distinct pathways through which attention is transformed into purchase behavior: low-involvement products primarily rely on attention repetition and mental availability to stimulate purchasing, while high-involvement products require deeper information processing and trust formation after attention is captured. The study further discusses how firms can allocate attention resources effectively by adopting broad attention strategies for low-involvement products and deep attention strategies for high-involvement products in the digital marketing environment. This paper contributes to a better understanding of attention allocation in marketing and provides both theoretical and practical implications for firms seeking to improve marketing effectiveness in the attention economy.

latest.title: Exploring How to Optimize Enterprise Marketing Strategies in the Digital Age
latest.venue: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
latest.abstract: The rapid advancement of digital technologies and the proliferation of new media platforms are fundamentally transforming the retail landscape and reshaping consumer decision-making processes. In this evolving environment, conventional, mass-oriented marketing approaches are increasingly inadequate for sustaining competitive advantage in digital markets—evidenced by persistently low customer acquisition efficiency and diminishing brand resonance. This paper systematically examines enterprise-level digital marketing strategies through a dual-method approach: comprehensive literature review and in-depth case analysis. It first maps the current state of the digital marketing ecosystem, then identifies and analyzes critical implementation barriers—including organizational silos, data fragmentation, and capability gaps—that hinder effective digital marketing adoption, further clarifies the core strategic advantages of digital marketing (e.g., real-time responsiveness, audience precision, and iterative optimization) and its tangible business value, and finally proposes forward-looking, actionable recommendations aligned with emerging industry trajectories. Empirical findings indicate that sustainable marketing transformation hinges on three interdependent pillars: seamless cross-channel integration, granular data-driven operationalization, and audience-centric content innovation. These insights provide a rigorous, practice-oriented framework to guide traditional enterprises in navigating their digital marketing transformation.

latest.title: Cognitive bias across generations: The influence of online reviews on consumer decision-making in E-commerce
latest.venue: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
latest.abstract: This study examines whether purchase intentions in response to online review scenarios differ across generational cohorts. Survey data were collected from 1028 Czech online panellists grouped into Baby Boomers, Generation X, Generation Y (Millennials), and Generation Z. Participants evaluated ten fictitious reviews developed around anchoring, attribute emphasis, framing, recency, and hindsight-related cues. Kruskal–Wallis tests yielded nominally significant cohort differences for positive anchoring, design-focused attribute emphasis, positive framing, and the older-review scenario. All four omnibus effect sizes were very small (η 2 H = 0.005–0.009). Holm-adjusted Dunn comparisons identified differences between Baby Boomers and Generations Y and Z for positive anchoring, between Baby Boomers and Generation Z for design-focused attribute emphasis, and between Baby Boomers and Generation Y for the older-review scenario. No pairwise comparison for positive framing remained significant after adjustment. These findings suggest that cohort membership alone provides limited information about responses to the scenarios and does not justify generation-specific review-interface strategies. The attribute-emphasis scenarios vary substantive product information and therefore do not isolate a priming mechanism. More generally, the Czech quota sample, hypothetical purchase-intention measures, and confounded stimuli restrict generalisability and causal interpretation. The study provides exploratory descriptive evidence rather than a basis for inferring stable generational differences in susceptibility to cognitive bias.

latest.title: Decision pathways in mobile-app shopping: a Throughput Model study of online consumers
latest.abstract: Purpose Mobile shopping environments increasingly rely on artificial intelligence (AI) to personalise recommendations, curate product information and support purchase decisions. Yet, existing consumer decision-making models maintain a linear, stage-based logic that fails to capture how AI-enabled interfaces compress, extend or reconfigure the pathways consumers actually follow. This study aims to use the Throughput Model (TPM) to conceptualise and empirically validate distinct algorithmic decision pathways through which perception, information search and evaluative judgement interact to shape purchase intentions in mobile-app shopping contexts. Design/methodology/approach Survey data were collected from Gen Z consumers with recent mobile-app shopping experience. The study applies partial least squares structural equation modelling and mediation analysis to test the TPM and estimate one-step, two-step and three-step decision pathways in AI-enabled mobile commerce. Findings Perception, information search and judgement each exert significant effects within the model, with judgement emerging as the central integrative mechanism linking upstream inputs to purchase intention. These results demonstrate that AI-enabled mobile interfaces simultaneously support impulsive, efficiency-driven and deliberative decision architectures. Originality/value To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this study provides the first empirical operationalisation of the TPM in mobile-app commerce, reconceptualising purchase decisions as coexisting algorithmic pathways rather than a single sequential route. It offers marketers a diagnostic framework for segmenting consumers by decision architecture and designing adaptive AI-enabled shopping experiences accordingly.

latest.title: Drivers of sustainable fashion purchase in India: a moderated value framework
latest.abstract: Purpose Although sustainable fashion research has extensively examined either consumer attitudes or purchase intentions, limited studies have explicitly distinguished between the cognitive foundation of attitude and the situationally driven nature of intention within the eco-fashion context. Furthermore, the interactive role of psychological traits such as altruism and mindfulness, along with economic considerations like willingness to pay a premium, in moderating the attitude–intention relationship remains underexplored, particularly in emerging markets such as India. This study aims to address these gaps by developing and empirically validating an integrated framework that captures both individual and contextual drivers of eco-fashion purchase intention. Design/methodology/approach Adopting a comprehensive mixed-methods design informed by grounded theory principles, this study explores the underlying factors that shape the phenomenon. Qualitative data from interviews and FGD enabled themes to emerge inductively, while quantitative survey data validated and extended these insights. Statistical analyses examined relationships among variables, and hypotheses were tested using SEM to ensure robustness of the conceptual model. Findings Environmental consciousness, social influence and marketing stimuli considerably shape eco-fashion attitude and purchase intention, while attitude mediates these relationships. Altruism, mindfulness and willingness to pay strengthen the relationship between attitude and purchase intention. Originality/value The study proposes a moderated value framework that explains sustainable fashion purchase more dynamically by treating altruism, mindfulness and willingness to pay as moderators in the Indian context.

latest.title: Tác động của nỗi lo sợ bỏ lỡ và hiệu ứng đám đông đến hành vi mua sắm bốc đồng của người tiêu dùng trẻ trong mua sắm livestream: bằng chứng từ ngành thời trang Việt Nam
latest.venue: The University of Danang - Journal of Science and Technology
latest.abstract: Trong lĩnh vực livestream thời trang tại Việt Nam, hành vi ra quyết định mua của nhóm khách hàng trẻ chịu ảnh hưởng bởi các tín hiệu xã hội, đặc biệt là cảm giác sợ bỏ lỡ và xu hướng hành động theo đám đông. Dựa trên khung Kích thích – Chủ thể – Phản hồi (S-O-R), nghiên cứu kiểm định tác động của nỗi lo sợ bỏ lỡ (FoMO) và hiệu ứng đám đông đến hành vi mua sắm bốc đồng, đồng thời phân tích vai trò trung gian của trạng thái tâm lý thúc đẩy mua sắm bốc đồng. Dữ liệu 308 người tiêu dùng trẻ đã tham gia mua sắm livestream thời trang được phân tích bằng PLS-SEM. Kết quả cho thấy, FoMO và hiệu ứng đám đông đều ảnh hưởng tích cực đến trạng thái tâm lý thúc đẩy mua sắm bốc đồng và hành vi mua bốc đồng. Trạng thái tâm lý thúc đẩy hành vi mua sắm bốc đồng đóng vai trò trung gian một phần. Nghiên cứu góp phần cung cấp thêm bằng chứng thực nghiệm trong livestream commerce ngành thời trang tại Việt Nam và gợi ý hàm ý quản trị cho doanh nghiệp.

latest.title: Modeling Circularwashing Risk in Renewable Energy Adoption: A Structural Equation Approach for Sustainable Consumption
latest.abstract: Abstract Circularwashing limits eco-friendly consumption by overstating, confusing, or inadequately proving the circular properties of products. While regular greenwashing makes ambiguous claims about the environmental characteristics, circularwashing takes advantage of the complicated nature of resource loops and the quality of the supply chain, causing significant market friction and high information asymmetry. Hence, an unexpected change in information distorts price signals, weakens customer trust, and jeopardizes market transparency by creating a lemon market for real circular goods. The present research presents the idea of circularwashing risk and provides a model to analyze the effect of false claims on the customers’ skepticism, decision-making risk perception, institutional trust, penalties for unreasonable behavior, and post-decision actions. The model is based on the Signaling Theory and the Stimulus Organism Response theory and is verified with the help of the survey data collected from 607 digital consumers in Colombia using the method of Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Model (PLS SEM). The measurement properties were assessed through composite reliability, average variance extracted, and heterotrait monotrait discriminant criteria and bootstrap resampling. The findings imply that misleading environmental claims correlate with consumer skepticism, which has a positive relationship with perceived decision risks and the erosion of institutional trust. Moreover, the effects of perceived decision risk and erosion of institutional trust on behavioral penalty are considerable. latest.title: Green or Greenwashed? Eco-Anxiety and Teen Consumer Choice
latest.venue: Critical Debates in Humanities Science and Global Justice
latest.abstract: Prior research has found that environmental anxiety is becoming prominent among teenagers and can increase their green purchasing intentions. To appeal to growing consumer interest, many companies use greenwashing, a deceptive environmental marketing tactic to appeal to interested consumers but keep their product costs low by avoiding actual eco-friendly production. This tricks worried consumers into believing they are purchasing eco-friendly products when they are not. A survey was conducted to see if there was correlation between how teens analyzed and selected between eco-friendly versus greenwashed product advertisements and their measured eco-anxiety levels. The survey showed low eco-anxiety levels had no association with product selections, medium eco-anxiety levels had notable association with greenwashed selections, and high eco-anxiety levels had notable association with eco-friendly selections. The association between moderate eco-anxiety and greenwashed selections highlights why greenwashing poses an issue to teens who want to make green purchases. However, it is unlikely that the study’s results are highly generalized to a larger population, and the survey should be replicated on a larger scale for better results.

latest.title: NEURO-EMOTIONAL ADVERTISING AND SUBCONSCIOUS CONSUMER DECISION-MAKING IN THE FAST-MOVING CONSUMER GOODS SECTOR IN SOUTH-WEST NIGERIA.
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: This study examines how five dimensions of neuro-emotional advertising (emotional appeal, sensory stimuli, neurological engagement, message framing, and brand personality projection) relate to subconscious consumer decision-making among fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) consumers in South-West Nigeria. A cross-sectional survey was conducted in Lagos, Ogun, and Oyo States using a structured five-point Likert questionnaire distributed to FMCG consumers. Of the 384 questionnaires administered, we analysed 208 usable responses (54.2%) using Pearson correlation and multiple regression in SPSS. All five dimensions correlated positively with subconscious consumer decision-making (r = 0.246 to 0.506, p < 0.01). In the regression model (R² = 0.527; adjusted R² = 0.519; F(5, 202) = 65.29, p < 0.001), all five dimensions were positive and statistically significant predictors. Brand personality projection had the largest standardised coefficient (β = 0.345), followed by emotional appeal (β = 0.306), sensory stimuli (β = 0.292), message framing (β = 0.214) and neurological engagement (β = 0.116). The results suggest that FMCG advertising works through several complementary routes at once, and that projecting a distinctive, trustworthy brand personality is the strongest single correlate of automatic, emotion-driven purchase tendencies in this market. Because the outcome and predictors are self-reported and the design is cross-sectional, the findings describe associations, not causal effects, and should be followed by experimental and neurophysiological work

latest.title: Does the Right Package Color Brew Better Feelings About the Product? Emotional Congruence, Perceived Fit, and Brand Affect in Coffee Packaging
latest.venue: Journal of Applied Business and Economics
latest.abstract: Packaging color is a powerful brand signal that shapes perceptions and purchase behavior, yet managers select packaging colors based on convention or aesthetic preference rather than congruence with a category's emotional objectives. Drawing on color-in-context theory, schema congruity, and sensory marketing, this study explores whether matching package color to a product category’s emotional meaning improves brand affect. In a coffee packaging study, red packaging produced higher brand affect than blue packaging, and perceived package-category fit mediated the effect. The findings translate color theory into an applied decision framework for packaging audits, portfolio management, retail and digital merchandising, and global expansion.

latest.title: The Effects of Digital Entrepreneurship, Digital Literacy, and Digital Platforms on Gen Z Purchase Decisions
latest.abstract: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) and digital technologies has fundamentally transformed the competitive landscape of micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). To remain competitive, MSMEs are increasingly required to strengthen their digital entrepreneurial capabilities, improve consumers' digital literacy, and optimize the use of digital platforms. This study examines the effects of digital entrepreneurship, digital literacy, and digital platforms on Generation Z purchase decisions as a strategy for strengthening MSME competitiveness in the era of artificial intelligence. The study employed a quantitative approach involving 175 Generation Z consumers of a local culinary MSME in Bogor, Indonesia. Data were collected through questionnaires and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4. The findings demonstrate that digital entrepreneurship has a positive and significant effect on purchase decisions (β = 0.336, t = 4.040, p < 0.001). Digital literacy also positively and significantly influences purchase decisions (β = 0.205, t = 2.009, p = 0.045), while digital platforms show a positive and significant effect (β = 0.296, t = 3.180, p = 0.001). The model explains 55.8% of the variance in Generation Z purchase decisions. These findings highlight the importance of integrating entrepreneurial digital capabilities, consumer digital literacy, and effective digital platform utilization to enhance MSME competitiveness. In the era of artificial intelligence, these capabilities provide an important foundation for MSMEs to improve market engagement, strengthen consumer decision-making, and sustain their competitiveness in an increasingly technology-driven business environment.

latest.title: Understanding the Mediating Role of Purchase Intention in Personality-Driven Sustainable Consumption Behaviour
latest.venue: International Journal of Academic Research in Business and Social Sciences
latest.abstract: Sustainable consumption has gained increasing attention due to growing environmental concerns and the need to encourage responsible consumer behaviour. Despite greater awareness of sustainability issues, many consumers continue to exhibit a gap between favourable sustainability perceptions and actual purchasing behaviour. This study examines the influence of personality traits and perceived behavioural control on sustainable consumption behaviour, with particular attention to the mediating role of purchase intention. Drawing on personality-based and intention-driven behavioural perspectives, the study investigates the effects of openness to experience, conscientiousness, and perceived behavioural control on consumers’ sustainable purchasing decisions. A quantitative research design was employed, and data were analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM). The findings reveal that purchase intention is the strongest predictor of sustainable consumption behaviour. Conscientiousness significantly influences both purchase intention and sustainable consumption behaviour, while openness to experience demonstrates an indirect effect through purchase intention but does not directly predict behaviour. Perceived behavioural control significantly affects purchase intention and sustainable consumption behaviour, highlighting the importance of consumers’ perceived capability to engage in sustainable purchasing practices. The mediation analysis confirms that purchase intention serves as a critical mechanism linking personality traits with sustainable consumption behaviour. latest.title: Integrating Conventional and Islamic Economic Perspectives into Financial Literacy Education: A Comparative Analysis of Consumption, Saving, and Investment Theories
latest.abstract: This study compares consumption, saving, and investment theories in conventional and Islamic economics and develops their implications for financial literacy education and economics teaching. Using a qualitative descriptive-comparative literature review, it examines Keynesian consumption theory, life-cycle and permanent-income approaches, saving–investment coordination, national-income equilibrium, and Islamic principles of moderation, lawful transactions, social responsibility, and maqasid al-shariah. The comparative synthesis identifies complementary learning dimensions: conceptual understanding of economic relationships, analytical interpretation of macroeconomic models, ethical evaluation of financial choices, and contextual application to household budgeting and investment decisions. A proposed pedagogical framework connects comparative theory, scenario-based discussion, numerical exercises, and reflective assessment. The study argues that macroeconomic identities remain analytically applicable across economic perspectives, while Islamic economics contributes explicit normative criteria for financial decision-making. These findings are conceptual curriculum implications, not measured improvements in students’ literacy or behavior. The article contributes an interdisciplinary foundation for designing financial literacy lessons that integrate economic reasoning and ethical reflection in secondary and higher education.

latest.title: How does a disaster change consumers' belief systems and retail expenditure?
latest.venue: Family and Consumer Sciences Research Journal
latest.abstract: Abstract Theory of awe suggests that awe elicited by disasters can affect both consumers' belief systems, such as new ecological paradigm (NEP), and their behavioral patterns. In this vein, this research examined how a disaster experience was associated with consumers' NEP endorsement and shopping motivations. It also profiled consumers based on expenditure changes across product categories, comparing pandemic experiences, NEP, shopping motivations, and demographic characteristics. Analysis of responses from 259 U.S. consumers confirmed the NEP as a central mechanism linked to consumption changes and identified four consumer typologies with unique profiles, offering insights for retailers to predict consumer behaviors during future disasters.

latest.title: A Study on Consumer Buying Behaviour in the Cosmetic Industry in India
latest.abstract: Abstract This paper explores buyer behaviour in the Indian cosmetic market, considering the demographic, psychological, socio-cultural, and digital influencing factors. As the market is growing fast and getting more digital, it has become critical to comprehend the changing consumer motivations. The literature review chapter critically looks at the literature review on the consumer buying behaviour of the cosmetic industry in India, and analyses the demographic, psychological, cultural, and digital factors influencing consumer buying behaviour. The secondary results indicate that cosmetic purchasing behaviour in India is multidimensional and the interplay of socio-economic, psychological assessment, cultural identity, and digital influence. Income and value perception influence brand choice, and specialised categories, green and halal cosmetics, depend on environmental concern and religiosity. The purchase and repurchase intention are strongly based on perceived quality and brand trust. Further, online marketing and social media activate decision-making processes faster by influencing attitudes, improving access to information and strengthening social validation.

latest.title: The Artificial Intelligence and Social Media Marketing Performance: Evidence on Personalization and Predictive Analytics from Pakistan’s Consumer Products Industry
latest.abstract: This study examines how artificial intelligence (AI) affects social media marketing in Pakistan’s consumer products industry, focusing on both its opportunities and its challenges. It uses a mixed-method design that combines 20 in-depth interviews with a structured questionnaire completed by 150 marketing professionals in firms that use AI. Multiple regression analyses show that AI-enabled personalized content and predictive analytics are significant positive predictors of ROI, customer engagement, and conversion rates, and together explain 43% to 50% of the variance in these outcomes. Personalized content is most strongly associated with ROI, while predictive analytics is most strongly associated with conversion rates. The interviews point to three main opportunities: enhanced personalization, greater efficiency and cost savings, and better data-driven decisions. They also point to three main challenges: high implementation costs, data privacy and security concerns, and a shortage of AI skills. The findings highlight the importance of strong data protection, transparency, and staff training for maintaining consumer trust and complying with regulations. The study offers practical recommendations for using AI responsibly in social media marketing. Because the data are cross-sectional, self-reported, and drawn from one industry in one country, the results show associations rather than cause and effect.

latest.title: Impact of restaurant robot service consumption values on their consequences: the moderating effects of perceived risk and human–robot interaction quality
latest.venue: Journal of Hospitality and Tourism Insights
latest.abstract: Purpose This study examined the effects of consumption values on customers' behavioral intentions toward robot service restaurants, based on the theory of consumption values and the value attitude behavior model. It also analyzed the moderating effects of perceived risk and human–robot interaction quality. Design/methodology/approach The study collected data from 756 customers who experienced robot services in restaurants. A structural equation modeling (SEM) analysis with a multi-group approach was used to test relationships. Findings The results showed that functional, human-like capability, social, emotional and epistemic values significantly predicted attitudes toward robot services, while price, safety and privacy did not. Most consumption values also influenced perceived brand equity, which strongly affected all outcomes including customers' intention to pay more, loyalty, intention to recommend and participation in value co-creation. Perceived risk and human–robot interaction quality partially influenced relationships in the structural model. Research limitations/implications This study has contributed to the literature on consumption value theory by incorporating a new construct – human-like capability – and emphasizing price value and safety and privacy values in the context of robot-provided restaurant services. However, future studies could examine robotic consumption values across a broader range of robot-assisted hospitality and tourism sectors. Practical implications This study provided valuable insights for restaurant managers by identifying robot service consumption values that significantly influence customers' behavioral intentions. Additionally, it demonstrates that service robots enhance service providers' performance through improved service efficie

latest.title: Too little, too much, or just right? How AI recommendation information volume shapes trust and consumer behavior
latest.venue: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
latest.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) shopping assistants explain why a product is selected, yet the appropriate defaults remain unclear. We define recommendation information volume as the amount of nonredundant, product-relevant information and compare five ordered explanation packages. Study 1 identifies an inverted-U response in a randomized Chinese mobile-retail experiment. Study S1 compares identical messages attributed to an AI assistant or a human salesperson, with separate source-neutral measurement validation. Study 2 reports conditional positive indirect associations through perceived usefulness, trust in AI, and decision comfort, and conditional negative indirect associations through information overload and algorithmic over-justification. Same-session estimates do not establish causal mediation. Its product-version comparison combines complexity, functionality, and safety considerations. Study 3 provides behavioral evidence across 51,248 recommendation impressions and service outcomes for 5000 distinct users. Moderate packages perform best within the tested sets. Bounded information processing explains the benefit–burden trade-off; persuasion knowledge suggests that disproportionate justification depends on expectations of selective versus comprehensive advice, across AI and human sources. Because amount, diagnostic priority, and content composition vary jointly, the experiments identify assigned-package effects, not pure quantity effects. The findings support category-specific testing of default explanations without establishing an exclusively algorithmic mechanism.

latest.title: UNDERSTANDING GEN-Z’S ATTITUDE TOWARDS PENANG’S LOCAL FOOD: THE ROLE OF EMOTIONAL, PRESTIGE, AND QUALITY-VALUES
latest.venue: Quantum Journal of Social Sciences and Humanities
latest.abstract: Penang’s local food creates an important element of the state’s cultural identity and serves as a key driver of tourism attractiveness. As Generation Z (Gen-Z) increasingly becomes a prominent consumer group in both the food and travel industries, understanding their perceptions and engagement with local food experiences has become increasingly important for sustaining culinary tourism and preserving cultural heritage. This study aims to examine the factors that contribute to Gen-Z’s attitude towards Penang’s local food by focusing on three variables which is emotional value, prestige value and quality value. A quantitative cross-sectional survey design was employed, utilizing a self-administered questionnaire distributed to 431 Gen-Z respondents aged 18-29 years in Malaysia who had prior experience consuming Penang's local food. Convenience sampling was used, and data were analyzed using Pearson correlation and multiple regression analyses. Results indicated that all three variables significantly influence Gen-Z’s attitudes with prestige value emerging as the strongest predicator, followed by quality and emotional value. These findings suggest that social recognition, sensory satisfaction and emotional connections play an essential role in shaping young consumers’ perception of local food. The study provides useful insights for tourism authorities, local food businesses, and cultural stakeholders to develop more effective strategies in preserving Penang’s culinary heritage while aligning with the preferences of the younger generation in a rapidly digitalized and globalized food culture.

latest.title: Analyzing Consumer Loyalty to Ultra‐Fast Fashion: An Integrative Analysis Based on the Stimulus‐Organism‐Response Model
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT The ultra‐fast fashion industry generates massive online sales, partly because of its ability to attract the custom of Generation Z (Gen Z). Given that this generational cohort typically has low brand loyalty, this paper examines how the dimensions of the stimulus‐organism‐response (S‐O‐R) model explain Gen Z's loyalty to the ultra‐fast fashion industry. For this purpose, the analysis presented in this paper relies on both a linear and an evolutionary view of the S‐O‐R model. Based on data from 208 questionnaires completed by consumers of ultra‐fast fashion, two analytical phases were conducted: (1) partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS‐SEM) and (2) qualitative comparative analysis (QCA). The results of the first phase suggest that consumer sustainability consciousness is associated with brand loyalty directly and under mediation, whereas social media peer communication is associated with brand loyalty only under mediation by brand equity. The second phase shows the relevance of brand equity in explaining both high and low brand loyalty. The configurations explaining high brand loyalty or low brand loyalty show that the relationship of each outcome with consumer sustainability consciousness and social media peer communications reflects psychological mechanisms that allow consumers to overcome the cognitive dissonance between their attitudes and behavior.

latest.title: Customer Engagement and Lead Conversion in Automotive Retail
latest.venue: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management
latest.abstract: This exploratory research paper examines customer engagement and lead conversion at a private Škoda dealership in Pune, India. The study draws on a confirmed aggregate activity summary of 52 walk-in customers observed during a three-month internship, together with an anonymised 24-record enquiry extract. Of the 52 walk-ins, 45 completed a test drive, six booked within the internship period, and three additional bookings were known to occur later. The enquiry extract shows interest concentrated in the Slavia and Kylaq models, although the extract is not a complete cohort and cannot represent the dealership or market as a whole. Field observations from both authors inform a process-level interpretation of needs discovery, product explanation, test-drive coordination, and follow-up. The analysis is descriptive: it does not estimate causal effects, compare dealerships, or attribute booking outcomes to a single intervention. The findings suggest that a dealership should treat the test drive as an intermediate engagement stage and maintain a consent-aware, structured follow-up process that distinguishes in-period bookings from later conversions. The paper contributes a carefully bounded practitioner account of how customer-journey concepts can be applied to automotive retail while preserving the limits of a small, private operational dataset. Keywords: automotive retail; customer engagement; lead conversion; customer journey; exploratory research paper; Pune

latest.title: Retail Sales Promotion and Consumer Conversion of Wellness-Oriented Food Products: An Exploratory Field Study of Nutrica at Sai Bazar, Mamurdi
latest.venue: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management
latest.abstract: Purpose: This study examines how point-of-sale promotion and need-based personal selling are used to engage shoppers and support purchase conversion for Nutrica wellness-oriented food products at Sai Bazar, Mamurdi. It focuses on the practical selling process, customer questions and objections, and the role of product knowledge in retail interactions. Design/methodology/approach: The study adopts an exploratory, descriptive single-site case-study design based on a two-month sales internship conducted from 1 June to 31 July 2026. Evidence comprises the trainee’s field observations, customer-facing selling activities, an internship activity diary and a summary of outlet-level records supplied in the source report. No structured questionnaire, probability sample or controlled experiment was reported. Findings: The field account indicates that concise, customer-centred communication, active listening, product familiarity and responses tailored to specific objections were central to the selling process. The source report records 247 customer interactions and 192 conversions. If these counts use consistent definitions and refer to the same observation period, the implied descriptive conversion ratio is 77.7%; this should be treated as provisional because the underlying transaction-level records and operational definitions were not included. The report also lists 1,014 L as units sold, but the measure requires clarification because the promoted portfolio included oils, honey and peanut butter. Practical implications: Retail promoters may benefit from short question-led scripts, approved product-information sheets, systematic objection logs and consistent recording of approaches, meaningful conversations, transactions and SKU-level quantities. latest.title: Reclaiming the Tap, Curbing Single-Use Bottled Water: An Agenda for Research and Policy
latest.abstract: The dramatic global growth of bottled water over the past five decades, particularly in nations with nearly universal access to high-quality, low-cost public tap water, has generated a host of harmful environmental impacts, including a substantial contribution to the crisis of single-use plastic pollution, as well as negative social and economic impacts due to its far higher cost and unequal patterns of distrust in tap water. More recently, bottled water's rapid spread has produced a major backlash, which is increasingly linked to the broader reaction against single-use plastics overall. A surge of activity by local governments, civil society, and private businesses-employing a combination of policy change, regulation, education, promotion, and social marketing-has emerged with the aim of curtailing bottled water sales and consumption, expanding access to free drinking water in public spaces, and restoring trust in and consumption of tap water. This commentary reviews several key bodies of scholarship and outlines the scale, causes, and consequences of bottled water's dramatic spread and of growing public distrust in tap water. It examines a range of responses, including campaigns to increase tap water consumption, restrict sales and consumption of single-use bottled water by governments, institutions, and individuals, and expand access to public tap water, profiling several examples of such initiatives. These efforts have spread worldwide and achieved substantial reach and momentum. The discussion takes stock of these developments and suggests potential implications and research directions for scholars of sustainability, consumer behavior, and other fields.

latest.title: TRENDING TASTES: EXPLORING THE ROLE OF SOCIAL-MEDIA IN DRIVING FOOD INNOVATION AMONG CULINARY STUDENTS
latest.venue: Quantum Journal of Social Sciences and Humanities
authors: WAN SITI NOR AZMA AB AZIZ
latest.abstract: Culinary students occupy an increasingly influential position in shaping food innovation within the Food and Beverage (F&B) industry, yet the way they engage with digital trends remains underexplored. This study, "Trending Tastes: Exploring the Role of Social Media in Driving Food Innovation Among Culinary Students," examines how social media trends drive the tendency to innovate food among culinary students at UiTM Permatang Pauh. Although food-related trends proliferate across social media platforms, there remains a limited understanding of how culinary students draw on this digital content as a guide for their own food innovation. This study addresses that gap by applying the Theory of Planned Behavior to analyze the factors, namely attitude, subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control that shape students' tendency to innovate food. A quantitative survey design was adopted, with data collected through a structured questionnaire administered via Google Forms and completed by a total of 147 respondents selected through stratified random sampling. The data were analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics, applying descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, correlation, and regression to test the proposed relationships. The findings indicate that attitude and perceived behavioral control significantly predict culinary students' tendency to innovate food in response to social media trends, whereas subjective norms do not exert a significant influence. These results underscore the value of social media as a pedagogical and professional resource, offering practical insights for culinary educators and the wider F&B industry seeking to cultivate an innovative and adaptive future workforce.

latest.title: Managing Sustainability in Hospitality Industry: A Theory of Planned Behaviour
latest.venue: International Journal of Modern Science and Research Technology
latest.abstract: With increasing environmental concerns and growing expectations for responsible business practices, sustainability has become a critical priority within the hospitality industry. The industry faces significant challenges associated with resource consumption, waste generation, carbon emissions, and the need to balance environmental responsibility with economic performance and customer satisfaction. The Theory of Planned Behaviour (TPB), introduced by Ajzen in 1991, provides a valuable theoretical framework for understanding the psychological factors influencing individuals’ intentions and behaviours towards sustainable practices. The theory proposes that attitudes, subjective norms, and perceived behavioural control influence behavioural intentions, which subsequently contribute to actual behaviour. This study aims to explore the application of the Theory of Planned Behaviour in managing sustainability within the hospitality industry, with particular attention to sustainable consumption, environmentally responsible customer behaviour, and the adoption of sustainable business practices. A systematic review of relevant empirical studies published during the past ten years is proposed to examine the contribution of TPB to understanding sustainability-related intentions and behaviours in hospitality settings. The study is expected to identify how environmental attitudes, social expectations, and perceived control influence sustainable decision-making among hospitality consumers and other relevant stakeholders. Furthermore, it seeks to identify theoretical and empirical gaps concerning the relationship between behavioural intentions and actual sustainable practices, particularly within developing-country contexts. latest.title: DETERMINANTS OF HALAL FOOD CONSUMPTION BEHAVIOUR AMONG GENERATION Z AT UITM PERMATANG PAUH
latest.venue: Quantum Journal of Social Sciences and Humanities
latest.abstract: Halal food consumption behaviour is not only a dietary requirement but also a religious obligation for Muslims, making informed and trustworthy food choices essential. In Malaysia, Generation Z (Gen Z) is increasingly exposed to different global food cultures and digital media, creating new challenges in navigating halal food consumption. Despite previous studies devoted to halal food consumption and intention to consume halal products, there has been limited attention to the roles of food neophobia, religiosity and social media influence in shaping halal food consumption behaviour among Gen Z. Therefore, this study aims to examine the influences of religiosity, food neophobia and social media influence on halal food consumption behaviour among Gen Z Muslim students in UiTM Permatang Pauh. This study is theoretically informed by the Theory of Planned Behaviour (TPB). The study employed a quantitative research methodology, and data were collected from 177 students at the Faculty of Hotel and Tourism Management, Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) Permatang Pauh, through an online structured questionnaire. The data were analysed with descriptive statistics and multiple regression analysis. The findings indicate that social media influence and food neophobia significantly predicted halal food consumption behaviour, but religiosity was not a significant predictor. The findings highlight the roles of food neophobia, religiosity, and social media influence in understanding halal food consumption behaviour among Gen Z. Practically, the study provides valuable insights for halal authorities, policymakers, educational establishments, and food businesses to develop halal decision-making among young Muslim consumers.

latest.title: Store Environment, Store Image, And Coffee Purchase Decisions: Evidence From Cadoha Coffee Shop In Manado
latest.venue: International Journal of Economics Business and Innovation Research
latest.abstract: This study aims to examine the effect of store environment on store image, the effect of store image on purchase decisions, and the mediating role of store image in explaining the relationship between store environment and coffee purchase decisions at Cadoha Coffee Shop in Manado City. A quantitative explanatory design was employed utilizing non-probability purposive sampling. The sample consisted of 100 respondents who were at least 17 years old and had previously purchased coffee beverages at Cadoha Coffee Shop. Data were collected using a structured Likert-scale questionnaire (1–5). Data analysis procedures included instrument testing (validity and reliability), descriptive statistics, regression analysis, and path analysis using SPSS software. The findings revealed that store environment has a positive and significant impact on store image (R^2 = 0.572, p < 0.001). Store image also demonstrated a positive and significant effect on purchase decisions (R^2 = 0.576, p < 0.001). Furthermore, path analysis confirmed that store image significantly acts as an intervening variable mediating the influence of store environment on purchase decisions, yielding an indirect effect coefficient of 0.574. These results highlight the essential role of store atmospherics and physical design in building a favorable brand image and driving consumer purchase behavior in local coffee retail management.

latest.title: THE ROLE OF BRAND AMBASSADORS IN STRENGTHENING BRAND TRUST AN EXPLORATORY STUDY OF THE VIEWS OF A SAMPLE OF ASIACELL CUSTOMERS
latest.abstract: This study examines the influence of brand ambassadors on customers’ trust in the Asiacell telecommunications brand. It adopts a descriptive analytical approach, drawing on questionnaire data collected through the company’s head office. The sample comprised 269 respondents who completed 19 items measuring the study variables on a five-point Likert scale. Responses were analysed using SPSS Version 24. The survey outcomes confirmed that respondents generally have quite positive views about the role of brand ambassadors and brand trust. Of the characteristics of an ambassador that were analyzed in the survey, expertise scored the highest mean score, followed by attractiveness and trustworthiness respectively. Further statistical processing revealed a strong positive link between brand ambassadors and consumers trust toward brands and the correlation coefficient computed was *r* = 0.804. In addition, the regression calculations proved that the evaluation of the ambassadors accounted for 64.7% of the variations in brand trust. After providing detailed analysis of individual characteristics, it became evident that attractiveness was the most significant attribute with regard to its contribution to the mentioned process and the latter two traits followed. All of these findings confirm the relevance of including the three mentioned features into the process of selecting ambassadors and planning marketing strategies. However, it should be noted that the research has certain limitations namely small size of the sample and its cross-sectional nature that raises some issues regarding the validity of the results.

latest.title: Certification trust and cultural authenticity in sustainable destination branding: traveller perceptions, choice and loyalty-related intentions
latest.abstract: This study examines how sustainability certification and perceived cultural authenticity relate to traveller responses in sustainable destination branding. An exploratory mixed-methods design combined an online survey of 128 Europe-based travellers with comparative case studies of Slovenia, Costa Rica and New Zealand, treated as independent evidence streams. Survey findings provided little evidence of an association between certification trust and reported influence on destination choice. In contrast, perceived cultural authenticity was strongly associated with authenticity-driven revisit intention, while revisit and recommendation intentions also showed a strong positive association, indicating co-variation between related loyalty responses rather than a directional relationship. The case studies showed that all three destinations combine sustainability certification or quality-assurance systems with community- and authenticity-oriented branding practices. Descriptive findings revealed relatively high trust in sustainability certification, but lower reported influence on destination choice, termed a certification trust–choice gap, without implying causality or a gap estimated through correlation analysis. The findings suggest that destination managers should combine credible and visible sustainability signals with authentic, locally grounded cultural experiences to strengthen traveller engagement and support loyalty-related intentions in sustainable destination branding strategies.

latest.title: The effects of visual cues on sustainable consumer behavior and their underlying mechanisms
latest.abstract: 摘要： 视觉元素是消费者感知环境刺激、加工产品信息的重要输入, 对可持续消费决策具有重要影响。针对现有关于视觉元素影响可持续消费的研究较为碎片化、结论零散甚至矛盾等问题, 本文基于视觉元素所传递的象征意义与物理功能差异, 将色彩、图像、字体、标识、立体形态与材质等元素归类为图形线索与结构线索, 并系统梳理其对绿色购买、可持续使用与循环处置等行为的影响。为推进视觉线索作用机制的结构化研究, 本文借鉴可持续消费决策中的合意性与可行性考量, 从意义价值评估与执行可能性判断两个维度, 构建视觉线索影响可持续消费的解释框架。具体而言, 图形线索主要通过合意性路径发挥作用, 概念隐喻与认知图式等机制具有较强解释力; 结构线索主要通过可行性路径发挥作用, 可供性与自动分类等机制具有较强解释力。此外, 为丰富视觉线索作用效果的边界研究, 本文从个体层、产品层与环境层挖掘影响视觉线索效应的调节因素。未来可进一步比较两类线索的相对效应, 拓展视觉线索的分类维度, 深入探讨可持续消费行为的多样化表现, 并在数字化场景与互动媒介中推进多感官整合研究。

latest.title: The Nexus Between Sustainable Human Resource Management and Sustainable Development Goals—Literature Review and Future Research Directions
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT Sustainable Human Resource Management (SHRM) has emerged as a strategic approach for enabling organisations to simultaneously achieve economic, social and environmental sustainability. Despite the growing body of SHRM research, limited attention has been devoted to systematically examining how SHRM contributes to the achievement of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). This study addresses this gap by combining a bibliometric analysis with a systematic literature review to examine the evolution, intellectual structure and research themes of SHRM, while developing a transparent framework for mapping SHRM research to the SDGs. Following the PRISMA guidelines, 1129 articles published between 2015 and 2026 were retrieved from the Scopus and Web of Science databases and analysed using VOSviewer. The findings reveal a substantial increase in SHRM research since 2020 and identify six dominant clusters. Building on these themes, this study develops a coding framework that systematically links the identified clusters to multiple SDGs. The findings highlight the multidimensional role of SHRM in advancing the social, economic, environmental and institutional dimensions of the 2030 Agenda while identifying emerging future research areas. This study extends the existing SHRM literature by providing a comprehensive synthesis of the field, introducing a transparent SDG mapping framework and offering practical guidance for organisations seeking to align their human resource strategies with sustainable development objectives.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: A Study on the Impact of Social Media and Digital Marketing on Consumer Buying Behaviour
latest.venue: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
latest.abstract: Digital marketing has changed the way businesses communicate with consumers, present products and influence purchase decisions. Search engines, social media, websites, email, online reviews and digital advertising provide businesses with opportunities to reach audiences and interact with customers. This paper examines the role of digital marketing in consumer buying behaviour through a review of selected academic literature and published industry evidence. It discusses the contribution of digital marketing to product awareness, information search, and evaluation of alternatives, consumer engagement and purchase intention. The study is descriptive and conceptual in nature and relies entirely on secondary sources; it does not claim to conduct a consumer survey or generate new statistical results. The reviewed literature indicates that digital channels create multiple consumer touchpoints and support interaction, while the effectiveness of campaigns depends on content relevance, trust, customer experience and suitable performance measurement. Published research also highlights challenges relating to privacy, personalization and the influence of online consumer-to-consumer communication. The paper concludes that businesses should use integrated digital marketing strategies, measure outcomes against clear objectives and communicate transparently with consumers..

latest.title: Mining Utility-Maximizing Prices for Mixed Bundles
latest.venue: ACM Transactions on Management Information Systems
latest.abstract: We study a data-driven bundle pricing problem with the following objective: given a predefined set of bundles, determine prices that maximize revenue under utility-maximizing consumer behavior. Classical mixed bundling models either assume a complete bundle menu with single-bundle choice or impose simplified pricing structures to ensure scalability. In contrast, we consider a setting in which the seller offers a restricted and potentially overlapping bundle catalog, allowing consumers to optimally select multiple non-overlapping bundles. This setting necessitates addressing two tightly coupled challenges: determining the price of each bundle and computing the revenue it generates under dependent consumer choice. Together, these challenges introduce additional combinatorial complexity in consumer decision-making and preserve strong price interdependencies across bundles. To address these challenges, we propose the Integrated Price Mining Method (IPMM), a scalable approach that approximates fully conditional pricing while explicitly accounting for dependent demand. We formalize consumer response as a utility maximization problem and show that it corresponds to a weighted set packing formulation. For price determination, IPMM combines balanced partitioning, sequential price search guided by competitive independence, dominance-based pruning, and cross-partition refinement to manage price dependence efficiently. Extensive experiments on synthetic instances and curated real-world bundle catalogs demonstrate that IPMM consistently achieves higher revenue coverage than classical and modern pricing baselines while remaining computationally tractable.

latest.title: Enhancing Market Capitalizing Agility: The Role of Technological, Financial, and Human Capital in Home-Based Catering Businesses in Bandung City, Indonesia
latest.abstract: The rapid development of digital technology has reshaped economic activities and consumer behaviour, particularly in the food sector, which is among the most frequently purchased categories online. This transformation requires Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs) to strengthen their ability to recognize and capitalize on market opportunities in digital environments by mobilizing their organizational resources. However, existing research has predominantly examined organizational resources and agility in larger firms, while empirical evidence from MSEs remains limited. Accordingly, this study examines the effects of technological, financial, and human capital on market capitalizing agility among online home-based catering MSEs in Bandung city, Indonesia. Data were collected through structured online questionnaires from 100 home-based catering business owners operating on Instagram and analyzed using PLS-SEM. The results indicate that technological, financial, and human capital each have a positive and significant effect on market capitalizing agility. Financial capital and human capital exhibited relatively larger standardized path coefficients than technological capital. These findings highlight the complementary roles of technological resources, financial capacity, and human competencies in supporting market-capitalizing agility among online home-based catering MSEs.

latest.title: Market Penetration Strategies of Sid’s Farm: Challenges and Solutions in General and Modern Trade in Pune
latest.venue: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management
latest.abstract: A new premium dairy brand has to win over retailers and shoppers before it can count on repeat purchases, and dairy's short shelf life makes that harder. This paper is a descriptive, exploratory case study of how Sid’s Farm tried to do this in two Pune retail channels: General Trade (GT) in Ravet and Modern Trade (MT) at Deli Essentials, Baner. The data come from an on-the-job training placement between 21 May and 21 July 2026, and include face-to-face conversations with retailers and customers, a 53-store retailer audit, and direct observation of merchandising and sampling. In GT, 27 of the 53 retailers approached (50.9%) showed interest, 21 (39.6%) placed a first order, and 13 of those 21 (61.9%) were recorded as reordering. Govind and Amul appeared in 94.3% and 88.7% of audited stores, so a newcomer is clearly competing with entrenched brands. In MT, about 30–35 customer interactions were observed. Price was the main objection, High Protein Curd and Paneer attracted the most interest in a store below a gym, and moving products to the front of the freezer and running two weekend Cow Dahi sampling sessions were followed by purchase interest. Overall, GT penetration was driven by the retailer and hinged on margin, reliable supply, returns support and cold-chain care, while MT penetration was driven by the shopper and hinged on visibility, trial and health-focused messaging. The paper closes with channel-specific recommendations and suggestions for more structured research. Keywords: Market Penetration, General Trade, Modern Trade, Dairy Marketing, Retailer Acquisition, Product Sampling, Pune

latest.title: Prior brand cognition and behavioral intention: omnichannel experience and consumer trust as complementary psychological pathways
latest.abstract: Restaurant consumers increasingly encounter brands across interconnected online and offline touchpoints, yet less is known about how prior brand knowledge relates to the interpretation of these encounters and subsequent decision making. Drawing on customer-based brand equity, schema-based information processing, customer-journey research, and trust theory, this study examines a cognition–experience–trust–behavior model. Survey data were collected from 510 restaurant consumers in three Chinese cities who had used at least two channels of a focal restaurant brand. Confirmatory factor analysis and structural equation modeling were conducted in R/lavaan, and indirect effects were assessed using 10,000 bootstrap resamples. Cognitive brand equity was positively associated with omnichannel experience and consumer trust. Omnichannel experience was positively associated with trust and behavioral intention, while trust showed the strongest proximal association with behavioral intention. All three specific indirect effects were significant, including the sequential pathway through omnichannel experience and trust, and the model explained 52.2% of the variance in behavioral intention. The findings are consistent with two complementary psychological routes: a practical route related to reduced interactional friction and a diagnostic route in which coherent cross-channel experiences provide cues associated with trust. Given the cross-sectional design, these pathways are interpreted as theory-guided associations rather than established causal processes.

latest.title: Self-identity and cool destinations: An interpretative phenomenological analysis of Chinese youth travellers
latest.venue: Journal of Hospitality and Tourism Management
latest.abstract: This research investigates the relationship between cool destinations and self-identity in the Chinese context and the role of the “coolness” phenomenon in tourism destination marketing. In doing so, this study explores how Chinese youth travellers construct their identity through their lived experiences in cool destinations. Interpretative phenomenological analysis is employed to investigate young travellers’ narratives of visiting destinations they perceived as “cool”. Findings reveal that cool destinations serve as spaces for self-discovery and as a self-reflective mirror, where encounters with divergent social realities prompted participants to reassess their identity in everyday life. How travellers negotiate between individual self-identity and their social identity is evident, and the role of travel in challenging social norms is also revealed. The study advances understanding of the connection between personal and social identity and destination coolness. Implications for understanding youth travel motivations and the symbolic role of cool destinations in identity are presented.

latest.title: CLO 3D VISUALIZATION AND INFLUENCER MARKETING IMPACT ON CONSUMER BUYING BEHAVIOR IN THE FASHION INDUSTRY: A COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF TRUST, ENGAGEMENT, AND PERSONALIZATION
latest.abstract: This study compares the effects of influencer marketing and CLO 3D-based garment visualization on consumers’ purchase intention in the fashion industry. The paper investigates trust and involvement as mechanisms by which both strategies function and estimates the two strategies on six consumer outcomes including personalization. A cross-sectional study involving 250 online fashion shoppers with a prior experience of influencer-marketing and CLO 3D and virtual try-on technology was conducted through purposive and snowball sampling methods. Hypotheses were evaluated by means of hierarchical multiple regression, parallel mediation analysis with Monte Carlo confidence intervals, and Steiger’s tests of difference of dependent correlations. Influence marketing predicted purchase intention (β = .49), as did CLO 3D visualization (β = .56) when both were introduced more than once (β = .31 and β = .43; R² = .39). Trust and engagement were partial mediators of both influences; together, they carried about 58% of influencer marketing influence and about 31% of CLO visualization influence. The connection of the CLO 3D visualization with understanding of the product, personalization, and purchase confidence was considerably stronger than that of influencer marketing with brand attachment and awareness of trends. However, there were no significant differences in the strategies’ overall connections to purchase intention. The cross-sectional self-reported non-probability design does not allow for causal conclusions and generalizability of the findings and the use of experimental and longitudinal approaches is recommended. Fashion brands need to consider both strategies as complementary, mostly by employing influencers in the discovery phase and using CLO 3D visualization in the evaluati

latest.title: Effects of sustainable packaging cues on perceived sustainability, purchase intention and price acceptance of cosmetic products
latest.abstract: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractSustainable cosmetic packaging is increasingly important as consumers use packaging-related cues to evaluate the environmental attributes and value of products. However, empirical evidence on consumer responses to different sustainable packaging configurations and communication cues remains limited in Central and Eastern Europe. This study examines perceived environmental sustainability, purchase intention and price acceptance across cosmetic packaging configurations featuring conventional plastic, biodegradable plastic and glass, as well as consumer evaluations of Vegan and Cruelty-Free labels and QR-code cues. A quantitative within-subject study was conducted among 204 adult Slovak consumers using an online questionnaire with nine visual stimuli. Data were analyzed using the Friedman test, Wilcoxon signed-rank test and Spearman’s rank correlation coefficient. Significant differences were identified across packaging configurations in perceived sustainability (χ²(2) = 8.21, p = 0.016), purchase intention (χ²(2) = 16.09, p < 0.001) and price acceptance at the premium price level (χ²(2) = 28.48, p < 0.001). Perceived sustainability was strongly and positively associated with purchase intention (ρ = 0.686, p < 0.001). Configurations featuring biodegradable plastic and glass received higher perceived sustainability evaluations than those featuring conventional plastic, while no significant difference was detected between biodegradable plastic and glass configurations. Biodegradable plastic and glass configurations generated higher purchase intentions than conventional plastic. hot.title: Sustainable Consumption and Branding for Gen Z: How Brand Dimensions Influence Consumer Behavior and Adoption of Newly Launched Technological Products
hot.abstract: Generation Z is emerging as a powerful force in shaping global consumer behavior, particularly in the market of digital and technological products. This study examines how specific branding dimensions, such as online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and brand knowledge, influence Gen Z’s purchase intention, emphasizing sustainable consumption. Sustainable consumption, in this context, refers to the preference for tech products that minimize the environmental impact through eco-friendly design, energy efficiency, and responsible sourcing. Using a quantitative approach, this cross-sectional research explores the effects of online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and knowledge on purchasing newly launched technological products that align with sustainability. Data were collected from a Gen Z sample using a combination of convenience and systematic sampling, and multiple regression analysis identified the most significant predictors of purchase intention. The results indicate that online brand experience, brand image, brand trust, and brand loyalty play the most crucial roles, having a greater effects on Gen Z’s purchase intention, while brand awareness and knowledge also contribute. However, brand engagement and behavioral intention have weaker effects. These findings suggest that brands targeting Gen Z should prioritize building a strong, trustworthy, and engaging online presence while highlighting their sustainability efforts, and when Gen Z consumers have favorable digital interactions with a brand, perceive its image positively, trust it, and feel loyal to it, they are more likely to consider purchasing its sustainable offerings. hot.title: The moderating role of personalized recommendations in the trust–satisfaction–loyalty relationship: an empirical study of AI-driven e-commerce
hot.abstract: Abstract Purpose This study investigates the effects of trust, satisfaction, and loyalty on AI-driven e-commerce, with a particular focus on how personalized recommendations moderate these relationships. It aims to explore how personalized AI features reshape consumer perceptions and decision-making. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research approach was used to collect data from a diverse group of e-commerce users who had interacted with AI-based recommendation systems. An online survey employing standardized scales for trust, satisfaction, loyalty, and personalization was administered, and data were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) to test the hypotheses. Findings The study reveals that trust has a significant positive influence on both satisfaction and loyalty. Personalization further strengthens these relationships by moderating the trust–satisfaction–loyalty dynamic. Satisfaction partially mediates the relationship between trust and loyalty, with the model’s explanatory power improving by 5% when personalization is included as a moderator. These results highlight the pivotal role of personalized recommendations in shaping consumer trust and satisfaction in AI-driven e-commerce. Practical implications Businesses can use personalized recommendation systems to enhance trust and satisfaction, thereby fostering loyalty. For example, platforms like Amazon and Netflix have successfully employed personalized AI algorithms to boost customer retention and engagement.
