latest.title: Pemberdayaan UMKM Batik Gama Wening melalui Pengembangan Identitas Merek Berbasis Kearifan Lokal dan Media Pemasaran Digital Berbasis Storytelling
latest.venue: KENDURI Jurnal Pengabdian dan Pemberdayaan Masyarakat
latest.abstract: Batik Gama Wening, a micro, small, and medium enterprise (MSME) located in Pait Village, Kasembon District, Malang Regency, lacks an adequate brand identity and effective digital marketing management. This community service program aimed to develop a brand identity rooted in local wisdom and enhance the partner's capacity to create storytelling-based digital marketing content to support market expansion. The program involved needs assessment, collaborative brand identity development through a co-creation approach, training in storytelling-based digital marketing content development, outcome-based evaluation, and sustainability enhancement. The program outputs included a logo and corporate color scheme reflecting local characteristics, brand identity applications across supporting media, packaging design, a one-month content calendar, and 12 Instagram content packages. The partner also demonstrated the ability to explain the meaning of the brand identity, plan content themes, develop content using Gemini AI, and prepare materials for publication. Periodic monitoring is necessary to assess the consistency of implementation, the partner's management capacity, and the program's contribution to market expansion and sales transactions.

latest.title: Decision pathways in mobile-app shopping: a Throughput Model study of online consumers
latest.abstract: Purpose Mobile shopping environments increasingly rely on artificial intelligence (AI) to personalise recommendations, curate product information and support purchase decisions. Yet, existing consumer decision-making models maintain a linear, stage-based logic that fails to capture how AI-enabled interfaces compress, extend or reconfigure the pathways consumers actually follow. This study aims to use the Throughput Model (TPM) to conceptualise and empirically validate distinct algorithmic decision pathways through which perception, information search and evaluative judgement interact to shape purchase intentions in mobile-app shopping contexts. Design/methodology/approach Survey data were collected from Gen Z consumers with recent mobile-app shopping experience. The study applies partial least squares structural equation modelling and mediation analysis to test the TPM and estimate one-step, two-step and three-step decision pathways in AI-enabled mobile commerce. Findings Perception, information search and judgement each exert significant effects within the model, with judgement emerging as the central integrative mechanism linking upstream inputs to purchase intention. These results demonstrate that AI-enabled mobile interfaces simultaneously support impulsive, efficiency-driven and deliberative decision architectures. Originality/value To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this study provides the first empirical operationalisation of the TPM in mobile-app commerce, reconceptualising purchase decisions as coexisting algorithmic pathways rather than a single sequential route. It offers marketers a diagnostic framework for segmenting consumers by decision architecture and designing adaptive AI-enabled shopping experiences accordingly.

latest.title: Drivers of sustainable fashion purchase in India: a moderated value framework
latest.abstract: Purpose Although sustainable fashion research has extensively examined either consumer attitudes or purchase intentions, limited studies have explicitly distinguished between the cognitive foundation of attitude and the situationally driven nature of intention within the eco-fashion context. Furthermore, the interactive role of psychological traits such as altruism and mindfulness, along with economic considerations like willingness to pay a premium, in moderating the attitude–intention relationship remains underexplored, particularly in emerging markets such as India. This study aims to address these gaps by developing and empirically validating an integrated framework that captures both individual and contextual drivers of eco-fashion purchase intention. Design/methodology/approach Adopting a comprehensive mixed-methods design informed by grounded theory principles, this study explores the underlying factors that shape the phenomenon. Qualitative data from interviews and FGD enabled themes to emerge inductively, while quantitative survey data validated and extended these insights. Statistical analyses examined relationships among variables, and hypotheses were tested using SEM to ensure robustness of the conceptual model. Findings Environmental consciousness, social influence and marketing stimuli considerably shape eco-fashion attitude and purchase intention, while attitude mediates these relationships. Altruism, mindfulness and willingness to pay strengthen the relationship between attitude and purchase intention. Originality/value The study proposes a moderated value framework that explains sustainable fashion purchase more dynamically by treating altruism, mindfulness and willingness to pay as moderators in the Indian context.

latest.title: Talking to the Market: Field Evidence on AI Chatbots, Digital Advice Utilization, and Retail Trading Outcomes
latest.venue: International Journal of Science Strategic Management and Technology
latest.abstract: Background: Conversational AI chatbots are increasingly embedded in retail brokerage applications, yet empirical evidence on how chatbot-based advice influences investor behaviour in real-world trading contexts remains limited. Purpose: This study investigates whether perceived chatbot competence and trust predict digital advice utilisation, and whether such utilisation is associated with self-reported trading outcomes, with financial literacy examined as a moderator. Uniqueness: The study extends prior research by focusing on investor–chatbot interaction and actual utilisation of chatbot guidance among active retail investors, rather than evaluating algorithmic stock-picking performance or purely conceptual advisory models. Methodology: A cross-sectional survey was conducted with 300 active retail investors who had recently interacted with AI-enabled investment chatbots. Multiple regression models were used to test direct relationships and the moderation effect of financial literacy. Findings: Perceived competence (B≈0.32, p<0.001) and trust (B≈0.32, p<0.001) are independently associated with higher digital advice utilisation (R²=0.306). Digital advice utilisation is positively associated with trading outcomes (B≈0.32, p≈0.02). Financial literacy also shows a positive association with trading outcomes (B≈0.30, p≈0.03), while the utilisation×literacy interaction is not statistically significant. Implications: The findings suggest that brokerage chatbots may support more disciplined investing behaviour, though causal interpretation is limited by the survey design. Future work should integrate chatbot interaction logs with objective brokerage trading records to evaluate long-run behavioural and performance effects. Keywords: AI chatbots; Digital advice; Retail investors;

latest.title: Determinants of Entrepreneurial Intention among Fisheries Students in Kerala: Evidence from a Primary Quantitative Survey Using the Theory of Planned Behaviour
latest.abstract: The objective of this research is to identify the determinants of entrepreneurial intention among students of fisheries and allied programmes in Kerala using the Theory of Planned Behaviour (TPB) after extending it with entrepreneurship awareness and perceived government support. This research employed a primary cross-sectional survey conducted on 424 fisheries and allied students, which was analyzed through various quantitative techniques that include reliability analysis, Pearson correlations, confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), structural equation modelling (SEM), and bootstrapped indirect-effect tests. Results reveal that all six multi-item constructs display acceptable to excellent internal consistency (Cronbach’s α = .798–.914). There is a positive and significant correlation for entrepreneurial intention. Of the correlates, perceived behavioural control (PBC) has the highest bivariate correlation (r = .658), followed by attitude (r = .614), awareness (r = .562), government support (r = .534), and subjective norms (r = .498). Measurement model provides a good fit (χ²/df = 2.41, CFI = .941, TLI = .927, RMSEA = .049, SRMR = .042). According to the structural model, there is the strongest direct effect of PBC on entrepreneurial intention (β = .34, p < .001). This is followed by attitude (β = .29), awareness (β = .24), government support (β = .21), and subjective norms (β = .18), all p < .001. The value of the model indicates 57.9% of the variance in entrepreneurial intention (R² = .579; adjusted R² = .574). The results in terms of awareness further showed that it has indirect effects on PBC (β = .17, p < .001) and government support (β = .11, p = .004). The study adapts the original TPB for a special fisheries-students population by incorporating the psychological, c

latest.title: ANALISIS PENGARUH UGC (USER GENERATED CONTENT) DAN BGC (BRAND GENERATED CONTENT) TERHADAP BRAND AUTHENTICITY MELALUI PURCHASE INTENTION PADA KLAPPERTAART KAWANUA MANADO
latest.venue: JURNAL RISET EKONOMI, MANAJEMEN, BISNIS DAN AKUNTANSI
latest.abstract: This study aims to examine and analyze the effects of User Generated Content (UGC) and Brand Generated Content (BGC) on Brand Authenticity, both directly and indirectly through Purchase Intention as a mediating variable among consumers of Klappertaart Kawanua Manado. A quantitative explanatory design was applied using an online Likert-scale questionnaire survey. A sample of 160 respondents was selected via purposive sampling. Data were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling based on Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS) executed in SmartPLS software version 4.2.9. The empirical findings reveal that: (1) UGC has a positive and significant effect on Purchase Intention; (2) BGC has a positive and significant effect on Purchase Intention; (3) UGC has a positive and significant effect on Brand Authenticity; (4) BGC has a positive and significant effect on Brand Authenticity; (5) Purchase Intention has a positive and significant effect on Brand Authenticity; (6) Purchase Intention partially mediates the effect of UGC on Brand Authenticity; and (7) Purchase Intention partially mediates the effect of BGC on Brand Authenticity. All hypotheses (H1–H7) were supported. Overall, BGC exerts a more dominant influence than UGC in driving purchase intention and enhancing perceived brand authenticity. Culinary MSMEs should combine professional, transparent official brand messaging with customer endorsements to sustain competitive advantage. Keywords: User Generated Content, Brand Generated Content, Purchase intention, Brand Authenticity, Social Media.

latest.title: Algorithmic riba and algorithmic Shariah non-compliance: risk mechanisms and a proposed governance protocol for Islamic banks
latest.abstract: Abstract Machine learning (ML) systems are increasingly used in the credit, pricing, and collections decisions of financial institutions, including Islamic banks, yet Shariah oversight remains primarily contract-centred. This conceptual paper identifies three distinct pathways of algorithmic Shariah non-compliance. Algorithmic riba, used narrowly, concerns profit-rate models whose optimisation objective may reproduce the time-value logic prohibited by riba; conventional benchmarking of murabahah (cost-plus sale) margins is not itself impermissible. Algorithmic injustice concerns credit-scoring outcomes that may violate the ‘adl (justice) obligation, and algorithmic gharamah (penalty) concerns collections systems that may impose charges beyond ​ta’widh (compensation for documented loss). To support model-level review, we propose the Shariah Algorithmic Compliance Screen (SACS), a five-component protocol grounded in Maqasid al-Shariah and offered as a first-iteration design proposal. Model owners disclose use cases, training data, objective functions, and outputs; independent technical validators test the relevant model evidence; and Shariah Supervisory Boards (SSBs) determine compliance. Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) methods are used descriptively, while established fairness diagnostics (subgroup calibration, error-rate comparison, and disparate-impact measurement) provide separate evidence on outcome equity. The three mechanisms are derived analytically from doctrine and the ML literature and are stated as conditional hypotheses. The study completes the construction stage of the design: SACS is conceptually grounded and operationally specified, and its components adapt existing artificial intelligence governance practice to jurisprudential review. SACS has n

latest.title: From landlocked to linked: how the China–Europe Railway Express attracts foreign investment
latest.abstract: Purpose International transportation networks are crucial to global capital allocation. This study aims to examine whether and how the China–Europe Railway Express (CR Express) attracts foreign direct investment (FDI) to connected Chinese cities. It identifies the causal effect of railway connectivity on FDI; investigates trade expansion, industrial upgrading and financial development as potential mechanisms; and explores variations across cities with different economic sizes, urban scales and industrial structures. Design/methodology/approach Using panel data for 285 Chinese prefecture-level cities from 2003 to 2022, this study treats the staggered launch of the CR Express as a quasi-natural experiment and applies a staggered difference-in-differences model to estimate its effect on inward FDI. Parallel trends test, instrumental-variable tests and other a range of robustness tests assess robustness and endogeneity. Mechanism and heterogeneity analyses examine transmission channels and differences across cities. Findings The research results show that the launching of the CR Express has significantly increased the inflow of FDI to cities along the route. The conclusion is still valid after many robustness tests. Mechanism analysis shows that the CR Express may influence FDI through three potential channels: expanding trade scale, upgrading industrial structure and promoting financial development. Further analysis found that this positive impact is more obvious in economically less-developed cities, service-oriented cities and small- and medium-sized cities. Originality/value This study extends FDI location theory by showing how cross-border railway connectivity can offset inland geographical disadvantages and reshape the spatial distribution of foreign investment. It br

latest.title: When AI thinks about culture: comparing language-based and empirical measures of individualism–collectivism
latest.abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to generate cultural insights, yet little is known about their cultural expertise and the extent to which their outputs replicate or correct for cultural stereotypes. This study compares country-level estimates of individualism–collectivism (I-C) derived from five different LLMs with a recently validated I-C index based on nationally representative surveys. The LLM-based estimates correlate highly with the survey-based index (up to r = 0.874) but also exhibit systematic deviation from the benchmark: Western societies are consistently overestimated on individualism, while Confucian East Asian societies are underestimated. Statistically, the type of benchmark-relative deviations suggests group-specific baseline distortions rather than random noise, with smaller and older models showing weaker alignment. Moreover, the deviations are systematically aligned with Hofstede’s original I-C rankings, suggesting that LLM-generated cultural representations may reflect information from legacy cultural frameworks alongside contemporary empirical patterns. These findings demonstrate both the potential and the risks of using LLMs as cultural interpreters. In consequential settings, LLM-generated cultural insights should be used responsibly—with calibration, human oversight, and awareness of potential biases. Used uncritically, they risk reinforcing outdated narratives that misdirect academic research and managerial decisions.

latest.title: Pengaruh Pemahaman AI Dan Inovasi Digital Serta Literasi Pasar Modal Terhadap Niat Berwirausaha Digital Dengan Efikasi Diri Sebagai Variabel Mediasi
latest.venue: Zentrum Economic Business Management Accounting Research
latest.abstract: The development of artificial intelligence (AI) and digital capital markets creates new business opportunities, yet little is known about how students' understanding of both domains shapes their digital entrepreneurial intention. This study examines the effect of understanding of AI and digital innovation and of capital market literacy on digital entrepreneurial intention, with self-efficacy as a mediating variable. A quantitative survey of 153 students attending a public lecture was analysed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS 4 with 5,000 bootstrap subsamples. The measurement model met the criteria for convergent validity, reliability, and discriminant validity. Understanding of AI and digital innovation (β = 0.480) and capital market literacy (β = 0.325) had positive and significant effects on self-efficacy. Self-efficacy had the strongest effect on digital entrepreneurial intention (β = 0.526) and mediated the effects of both independent variables. Capital market literacy also had a significant direct effect (β = 0.286), whereas understanding of AI and digital innovation had no direct effect (β = 0.099; p = 0.238), so its influence operates fully through self-efficacy. The model explains 69.8% of the variance in digital entrepreneurial intention. The findings imply that public lectures and entrepreneurship education should build students' self-belief rather than only transfer knowledge.

latest.title: An Intelligent Multi-objective Decision Support Model for Sustainable Remanufacturing
latest.venue: Process Integration and Optimization for Sustainability
latest.abstract: Remanufacturing offers small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) viable pathways towards transitioning to a circular economy; however, intelligent decision-making systems are needed to accelerate its adoption. Balancing the economic, environmental, and social dimensions of sustainability requires the use of analytical tools that can handle multi-dimensional complexity. This study presents a multi-objective optimization model where remanufacturing tasks are allocated to machines in a factory on the basis of minimizing costs, emissions, and noise exposure. Tri-objective optimization has been carried out using the quadrant shrinking method, and Pareto optimal solutions are translated to an implementation framework that can equip SMEs with an intelligent tool for circular economy adoption. In addition to this, we propose an implementation framework for circular economy in manufacturing based on the DMAIC (define, measure, analyze, improve, and control) approach.

latest.title: Who Made This Ad in the AI Era? Unpacking AI and Human Authorship Disclosure Effects
latest.abstract: As generative AI becomes increasingly common in advertising, disclosure of its use is required in some regions and countries. Prior research shows that AI authorship disclosure can harm consumer responses, but less is known about how explicit authorship disclosure shapes source attribution, whether human authorship disclosure generates positive effects, and how these effects vary across advertising contexts. We conducted three experiments manipulating actual authorship (AI vs. human) and disclosure (disclosed vs. undisclosed) using closely matched AI-generated and human-crafted ads. Study 1 focused on product-centered luxury brand ads, Study 2 on luxury brand ads featuring models, and Study 3 on small-business sponsored posts featuring models. Across all three studies, disclosing AI authorship (vs. no disclosure) consistently produced negative indirect effects on brand attitude through lower perceived effort. By contrast, the effects of disclosing human authorship (vs. no disclosure) varied by context: it had no downstream effect in Study 1; it increased perceived emotion expression without affecting brand attitude in Study 2; and it produced a positive indirect effect on brand attitude in Study 3 through perceived effort. These findings highlight the role of explicit disclosure in shaping source attribution and suggest that AI disclosure and human disclosure can trigger distinct consumer responses across contexts.

latest.title: How Can a Circular Economy for Sustainable Tourism be Assessed? Evidence From an Ecological Resort in Taiwan
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT Climate mandates pressure the tourism and hospitality industry to decarbonize rapidly, making circular economy implementation in fragile destinations an immediate priority. Hotels usually focus inward on building efficiencies. Ecological resorts, however, must operate within natural environments, a difference requiring a specialized framework that bridges natural resource assessment with stakeholder collaboration to reduce environmental degradation. We thus developed a circular framework tailored for forest eco‐resorts via a mixed‐methods design using three distinct panels. We ran a fuzzy Delphi survey to refine the indicators, used the analytic hierarchy process with 25 experts to weight them, and assessed practical field performance via 79 employee responses. This process yielded 52 indicators spanning seven subcategories. The conservation of natural resources scored the highest weight (0.0514), followed closely by the installation of water‐saving equipment (0.0433). The quadrant distributions demonstrated that destinations must first implement advanced technical strategies for robust wastewater treatment to anchor macrolevel circularity before behavioral programs can mature successfully. These indicators, ultimately, offer a robust assessment instrument for sustainable development throughout the eco‐resort sector.

latest.title: Digital transformation and organisational performance: The mediating role of marketing agility among guesthouse operators in Accra Metropolitan District
latest.abstract: This study examines how digital transformation influences organisational performance, with marketing agility as a mediating variable, among guesthouse operators in the Accra Metropolitan District, Ghana. A survey of 301 employees and managers from 51 guesthouses was conducted using questionnaires and partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) was conducted in SmartPLS version 4.1.1.4 to analyse the research model and its associated hypotheses. The results show that digital transformation has a significant positive relationship with marketing agility. Marketing agility fully mediates the relationship between digital transformation and guesthouse performance. The study also found a significant positive relationship between marketing agility and guesthouse performance. However, the direct relationship between digital transformation and guesthouse performance was not statistically significant, indicating that digital transformation alone does not drive organisational performance. Instead, marketing agility is the key, an underexplored link that makes digital transformation effective. It is recommended that guesthouses adopt tailored digital tools, social media platforms and emerging technologies and develop flexible marketing strategies that adapt to changing customer needs to boost performance and remain competitive in the industry.

latest.title: Glottolab: A Linguistic Adventure...In Italian!Developing a Gamified Linguistics Activity for the Italian-Speaking Community
latest.abstract: Glottolab: A Linguistic Adventure (Cattaneo et al. 2025) is a game-based learning activity developed with RPG Maker MZ and designed to introduce a non-specialized audience to core concepts in linguistics through an interactive and engaging environment. Building on the development and evaluation of the English version of the game, a new Italian version was designed, Glottolab: Un’avventura linguistica. A combination of approaches was employed. Dialogues necessary for the progression of the game were manually translated into Italian; dialogues of the Non-Playable Characters, who represent famous linguists, were generated in Italian using Artificial Intelligence systems, and a set of linguistic puzzles specifically focusing on properties of the Italian language was designed to better align the gameplay with the linguistic knowledge of Italian-speaking participants. The development of the Italian version of the game was embedded within a teaching project carried out in collaboration with students enrolled in the Linguistic Data Lab course of the Master’s Degree in Theoretical and Applied Linguistics at the University of Pavia. Within this educational framework, students contributed to the translation, design, and validation of dialogues and to the creation of Italian-focused linguistic puzzles. The initial results obtained from the English version of Glottolab suggested that the game has significant potential as a tool for the dissemination of linguistic knowledge and for promoting awareness of language structure among non-specialist audiences. The development of the Italian version represents a further step towards expanding the pedagogical and dissemination potential of the project, while also serving as a collaborative learning experience for the university students invo

latest.title: Data Governance and Ethical Issues in Accounting Technology
latest.venue: International Journal of Science Strategic Management and Technology
latest.abstract: Purpose: The introduction of advanced technologies like artificial intelligence (AI), blockchain, and enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems has transformed accounting practices, allowing for quicker processing, greater transparency, and more informed decision-making. Despite these benefits, they also bring up crucial concerns related to data governance and ethical responsibility. This paper explores how governance frameworks and ethical standards can be applied to ensure trust, adherence to regulations, and integrity in technology-driven accounting settings. Methodology: This study utilizes a conceptual and case-based approach, referencing regulatory frameworks such as IFRS, Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS), GDPR, and the EU AI Act. It addresses ethical challenges like bias in AI predictions, transparency in disclosures, risks of fraud in digital records, and responsibility for technology-driven mistakes. Case studies, including ERP breaches revealing client information, incorrect reporting of crypto assets due to a lack of standards, and inaccuracies in ESG reporting, are analyzed to demonstrate real-world issues. Findings: The research finds that strong data governance ensures accuracy, integrity, and compliance, while ethical oversight protects stakeholder trust. Weak governance leaves organizations vulnerable to cybersecurity threats, harm to reputation, and regulatory fines. Excessive reliance on automation without professional skepticism weakens ethical judgment, while emerging areas such as ESG reporting and blockchain require new accountability frameworks. The findings highlight that accountants must transition from traditional record keepers to digital stewards of trust. Implications: The paper suggests practical strategies, including forming AI govern

latest.title: Customer Retention and Entrenchment Strategies and Competitiveness of Commercial Banks in Nakuru City, Kenya
latest.venue: International Journal of Social Science and Humanities Research (IJSSHR)
latest.abstract: Customer retention and entrenchment strategies are deliberate organizational approaches through which firms sustain long-term customer relationships, reduce switching behaviour and strengthen customer commitment. Commercial banks in Kenya have invested heavily in such strategies, yet intensifying fintech and mobile-money competition, rising customer churn and fluctuating profitability indicate that their contribution to competitiveness remains unclear. The purpose of this study was to examine the effect of customer retention and entrenchment strategies on the competitiveness of commercial banks in Nakuru City, Kenya. Specifically, it assessed the influence of service quality, service personalization, product bundling and digital platforms on competitiveness. The study was anchored on Relationship Marketing Theory, the Resource-Based View, Switching Cost Theory and Customer Lifetime Value Theory. A descriptive correlational research design was adopted. The study targeted 376 managements and customer-facing staff in 62 commercial bank branches in Nakuru City, from which a sample of 111 respondents was drawn using the Nassiuma formula and stratified random sampling. Data were collected through a structured questionnaire, of which 96 were returned (86.5% response rate), and analysed using descriptive statistics and multiple regression. The four strategies jointly explained 62.6% of the variation in competitiveness (R² = 0.626; F = 38.068, p < 0.05). Service quality had the strongest influence (β = 0.460, p < 0.05), followed by digital platforms (β = 0.411, p < 0.05), service personalization (β = 0.277, p < 0.05) and product bundling (β = 0.159, p < 0.05), and all four null hypotheses were rejected. The study concludes that service quality and digital platforms are the princ

latest.title: The effect of talent and knowledge management on employee retention: The mediating role of employee engagement
latest.abstract: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractAmid rising labor mobility and competition for skilled employees, this study aims to examine how talent and knowledge management relates to employee engagement and retention, with employee engagement as a mediator, among private-sector employees in Indonesia’s manufacturing, banking, retail, service, and logistics sectors. Using a combination of purposive and snowball sampling, 543 valid responses (from 964 distributed questionnaires across 97 companies) were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). Talent management (β = 0.554) and knowledge management (β = 0.379) were positively associated with employee engagement (R² = 0.721), and both were also directly associated with employee retention (β = 0.275 and β = 0.315, respectively; R² = 0.632). Employee engagement was positively associated with employee retention (β = 0.290), and its indirect effects for talent management (β = 0.161) and knowledge management (β = 0.110) were statistically significant (p < 0.001), confirming employee engagement as a significant partial mediator (VAF = 36.93% and 25.88%, respectively). Direct effects of talent and knowledge management on retention remained somewhat larger than their indirect effects through engagement, but the substantial VAF values indicate that employee engagement is a meaningful complementary pathway, alongside direct organizational investment in talent development and knowledge management, through which these practices are associated with employee retention. The study extends social exchange theory and the resource-based view and offers practical implications for strengthening retention in the sampled Indonesian private companies.AcknowledgmentsThanks to the lecturers of the Faculty of Eco

latest.title: Mechanisms and Pathways of Artificial Intelligence–Driven Rural Industrial Integration
latest.venue: International Journal of Finance and Investment
latest.abstract: The penetration of artificial intelligence (AI) into rural industries is reshaping the underlying logic of integration among the primary, secondary and tertiary sectors in rural areas. Based on a systematic review of the relevant literature, this paper develops a four-dimensional analytical framework—technological penetration, actor empowerment, network restructuring and value co-creation—to explain the micro-level mechanisms through which AI drives rural industrial integration. The analysis shows that AI reduces information asymmetry by embedding data as a production factor, alters the resource endowments and bargaining power of diverse business actors through tool-based empowerment and knowledge diffusion, reshapes the distribution of benefits by restructuring collaborative networks, and ultimately manifests itself in industrial chain extension, value chain upgrading and the sharing of value-added gains. Accordingly, drawing on resource endowments, industrial foundations and locational conditions, villages are classified into three types—peri-urban technology-integrated villages, specialty agriculture–empowered villages and eco-cultural tourism innovation villages—for which differentiated integration pathways are identified. A three-tier dynamic evaluation indicator system covering foundational support, integrative application, and impacts and benefits is then constructed. The paper argues that the extent to which smallholder farmers share in the gains should serve as the core criterion for assessing integration outcomes, and that progress should be advanced in a coordinated manner through precision-oriented technology supply, cultivation of actors' digital literacy, innovation in benefit-linkage mechanisms and optimization of institutional safeguards.

latest.title: Prediction markets in the United States: a youth public health perspective
latest.abstract: Prediction markets (PMs) provide the opportunity to trade on the likelihood of an event, such as will Team A beat Team B. PMs are increasingly popular, particularly among young people, because unlike legalized online sports betting, PMs can be accessed in all 50 United States and in some PMs, at age 18. PM's accessibility to young people, gamified features, and strong peer context for transactions contribute to PM popularity among young people, highlighting the urgent need for research on the prevalence of youth PM involvement, youth exposure to PM marketing, and impacts of PM on youth well-being to inform prevention and intervention. This Perspective reviews the distinction between PM and gambling, the appeal of PMs for young people, PM marketing practices that appeal to young people, the developmental context of youth prediction market involvement, and discusses prevention and intervention methods for possible PM-related adverse effects on health among young people.

latest.title: Harnessing multimodal digital markers to advance personalized mental health care: distinguishing trait-like and state-like mechanisms
latest.abstract: Mental health disorders pose a critical global challenge, affecting millions and imposing substantial socio-economic burdens. Traditional one-size-fits-all interventions often fail to capture the complexity of individual mental health trajectories, highlighting the urgent need for more personalized approaches. Digital phenotyping, which leverages multimodal data from smartphones and other sensors, offers a promising avenue for advancing mental health care. However, existing research largely relies on single-modality approaches or “black-box” machine learning (ML) models, limiting both interpretability and clinical applicability. This paper proposes a conceptual framework for integrating multimodal digital markers–including text, acoustic signals, facial expressions, physiological data, and behavioral patterns–with the aim of refining mental health assessment and intervention. A key innovation of this framework is distinguishing between trait-like markers (relatively stable, individual-specific characteristics) and state-like markers (within-individual changes over time). This distinction is crucial for understanding psychopathology and therapeutic change yet remains largely unexamined in existing research. By synthesizing findings across affective, cognitive, and behavioral domains, we demonstrate how automated markers can potentially offer novel insights into mental health mechanisms. The framework implementation flow is illustrated by a clinical demonstration using information from a psychotherapy treatment of an individual diagnosed with depression. Focusing on markers such as vocal tone, facial expressivity, or linguistic features, the trait-like components predict treatment prognosis and state-like components track real-time therapeutic progress. This approach prov

latest.title: Role of Digital Technologies in Small Business: A Statistical Analysis of Adoption, Performance, and Growth Outcomes
latest.venue: International Journal of Science Strategic Management and Technology
latest.abstract: The rapid diffusion of digital technologies including social media marketing, e-commerce platforms, mobile payment systems, cloud-based accounting, and customer relationship management (CRM) tools has fundamentally reshaped the operating environment of small businesses worldwide. This study statistically examines the relationship between the extent of digital technology adoption and small business performance, measured through sales growth, customer reach, operational efficiency, and profitability. A structured survey was administered to a sample of small business owners/managers (N = 250) across retail, services, and manufacturing sectors. Data were analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics through descriptive statistics, reliability analysis (Cronbach's Alpha), Pearson correlation, independent samples t-tests, one-way ANOVA, and multiple linear regression. Results indicate a statistically significant and positive relationship between digital technology adoption and overall business performance (r = 0.612, p < 0.01). Regression analysis reveals that digital marketing adoption (β = 0.34, p < 0.001) and digital payment/financial tools (β = 0.28, p < 0.001) are the strongest predictors of performance, jointly explaining 46.8% of the variance (R² = 0.468, Adjusted R² = 0.459, F(4,245) = 53.87, p < 0.001). Businesses with high digital adoption reported significantly higher performance scores than low-adoption businesses (t(248) = 7.42, p < 0.001). The findings underscore the strategic necessity of digital technology integration for small business competitiveness and sustainability, while also highlighting persistent barriers related to cost, digital literacy, and infrastructure. The study concludes with policy and managerial recommendations to accelerate inclusive digital adoption

latest.title: The Cluster Approach to Digitalizing Entrepreneurship: Emerging Opportunities and Persistent Challenges
latest.venue: WSEAS TRANSACTIONS ON BUSINESS AND ECONOMICS
latest.abstract: Digitalization now sits at the heart of how entrepreneurial economies transform, compete, and innovate. Its rollout, however, has been uneven. Digital infrastructure is distributed unequally, and public policy often lacks the coordination needed to make it work. Clusters offer one way forward. When firms, research institutions, and public authorities cooperate within a cluster, they exchange knowledge more freely and share resources more efficiently. This study looks at the period 2022–2024 and asks how far the cluster approach actually drives the digitalization of entrepreneurship ̶ and where it falls short. We combine factor, regression, correlation, and cluster analysis on data from national and international reports, and we supplement these with case material and expert interviews. The evidence points in one direction: clustering speeds up digitalization by opening access to technology, finance, and specialized expertise. Firms inside digital clusters tend to innovate more, raise productivity faster, and adopt digital tools earlier than firms outside them. Yet two constraints persist ̶ insufficient public support and a stubborn digital-skills gap. On this basis we argue for integrated policies that nurture cluster development and deepen public–private cooperation.

latest.title: Sustainability-Driven Luxury Hotel Choice: The Role of Eco-Consciousness, Sustainable Values, and Fintech Adoption among Young Travellers in Sri Lanka
latest.abstract: This study explores how young travellers understand and interpret sustainability when selecting luxury hotels in Sri Lanka. Specifically, it investigates the meanings and experiences associated with eco-consciousness, perceptions toward eco-sustainability, and eco-sustainable values, while also examining how sustainability initiatives implemented by luxury hotels and fintech-enabled services are perceived within the hotel selection process. By addressing a gap in understanding the lived experiences and perspectives of young travellers, the study contributes to emerging discussions on sustainability-oriented luxury consumption within an emerging tourism destination. Guided by an interpretivist research philosophy and an inductive qualitative approach, the study collected primary data through semi-structured interviews with purposively selected young travellers and luxury hotel managers in Sri Lanka. The research was informed by the Theory of Reasoned Action as a sensitizing theoretical framework. Data were analysed using thematic analysis to identify recurring patterns, perceptions, and meanings associated with sustainable luxury hotel selection. The findings reveal that sustainability is increasingly viewed by young travelers as an integral component of luxury hospitality rather than an optional attribute. Participants associated eco-sustainable practices with authenticity, ethical responsibility, and enhanced travel experiences. Visible sustainability initiatives, environmental transparency, and community-oriented practices emerged as important considerations in hotel evaluations. Fintech-enabled services were perceived as facilitating sustainable travel experiences by improving convenience, transparency, and engagement with sustainability-related initiatives. However,

latest.title: Can rural e-commerce policies enhance the total factor productivity of agricultural enterprises? Causal inference based on dual machine learning models
latest.abstract: Introduction Rural e-commerce policies, as an important component of the digital economy, are profoundly reshaping the agricultural value chain and food supply chain, and are of great significance for enhancing the economic efficiency of the grain industry. Methods Based on the panel data of 231 A-share agricultural listed enterprises in China from 2010 to 2024, this paper takes the comprehensive demonstration policy of e-commerce entering rural areas in China as the standard natural experiment, constructs A dual machine learning model, and systematically examines the impact of rural e-commerce policies (RECP) on the total factor productivity (TFP) of agricultural enterprises and its mechanism of action. Results The research findings are as follows: (1) RECP significantly enhanced the TFP of agricultural enterprises. After introducing high-dimensional fixed effects, replacing machine learning algorithms, and using instrumental variable methods to alleviate potential endogeneity, the conclusion remained robust. (2) Mechanism analysis indicates that RECP mainly promotes the improvement of TFP in agricultural enterprises by reducing information asymmetry, increasing R&D investment and optimizing the human capital structure. (3) Heterogeneity analysis shows that this promoting effect is more significant in enterprises in the growth stage, those with lower financing constraints, those engaged in agricultural product processing, and large listed agricultural enterprises. Discussion The research conclusion provides new empirical evidence for understanding the micro-mechanism by which the digital economy empowers the productivity improvement of listed agricultural enterprises, and offers policy implications for enhancing the supporting digital ecosystem of listed agricultural e

latest.title: Market access, agricultural product prices, and smallholder farm income in China
latest.abstract: This paper examines the causal effects of digital market access on agricultural product prices and smallholder farm income in China, using a balanced county panel. We construct a Digital Market Access Index (DMAI) through principal component analysis of multiple dimensions: e-commerce adoption, mobile payment penetration, price information access, and rural logistics services. County and year fixed effects, instrumental variable estimation, and Hansen panel threshold regression identify large, nonlinear, and causally robust effects of DMAI on farm gate prices, price transmission efficiency, marketing margins, and farm income. An improvement in DMAI raises log farm gate prices and log per-capita farm income while compressing wholesale-to-retail marketing margins. Threshold analysis identifies significant transition points that partition counties into early-adoption, expansion, and maturity regimes, with increasing marginal effects across regimes. Bootstrap mediation decomposes the total price effect into price information capacity, supply chain reduction, bargaining power, and logistics efficiency channels, which jointly account for most of the total effect. Moderation analysis reveals complementarities with road infrastructure, farmer education, and cooperative membership. Spatial Durbin models document significant cross-county price spillovers. Results are robust across multiple alternative specifications.

latest.title: The double-edged sword of virtual influencer anthropomorphism: a paradoxical framework of social presence and identity threat
latest.venue: Journal of Humanities and Applied Social Sciences
latest.abstract: Purpose This study investigates how the perceived physical and psychological anthropomorphism of virtual influencers shape consumers’ attitude toward virtual influencers through the competing psychological pathways of social presence and identity threat. Design/methodology/approach Through a cross-sectional survey, a sample of 448 Instagram users in Egypt was collected and analyzed using CB-SEM through AMOS v.23. Findings Both perceived physical and psychological anthropomorphism of virtual influencers have a positive influence on both social presence and identity threat. Importantly, both social presence and identity threat concurrently mediate the relationships between both dimensions of anthropomorphism and attitudes toward virtual influencers. Therefore, both dimensions of anthropomorphism influence consumers’ attitudes toward virtual influencers through the positive mediating role of social presence and the negative mediating role of identity threat. Research limitations/implications The study expands anthropomorphism research to the virtual influencer context by showing that anthropomorphism is not unequivocally superior. Therefore, grounding in social presence and social identity theory, we suggest that anthropomorphism is a double-edged sword in shaping attitudes toward virtual influencers. Practical implications Both designers and marketers employing virtual influencers should consider the multi-dimensionality anthropomorphism. Moreover, they should aim to maximize social presence while reducing identity threat when utilizing virtual influencers. Originality/value This study conceptualizes anthropomorphism as a multifaceted construct composed of physical and psychological dimensions and it can work through two opposing positive and negative pathways.

latest.title: Corporate Competitive Practices and Performance of Leading Tea Brands in Kenya
latest.venue: International Journal of Social Science and Humanities Research (IJSSHR)
latest.abstract: Corporate competitive practices are deliberate strategic choices through which firms enhance efficiency, competitiveness and performance in dynamic markets. In Kenya’s tea industry, which remains a leading source of export earnings and rural livelihoods, leading brands operating under broadly similar strategic frameworks continue to record uneven profitability, fluctuating market shares and varying levels of customer loyalty. This study examined the influence of corporate competitive practices on the performance of leading tea brands in Kenya. Specifically, it assessed the influence of growth and expansion, integration and diversification, stability and renewal, and restructuring practices on brand performance. The study was anchored on Porter’s Generic Competitive Strategies Theory, the Weber–Fechner Law and Ansoff’s Growth Strategy Theory. An explanatory research design was adopted. A census of the 10 leading tea brands in Kenya was undertaken, while purposive sampling was used to select 80 senior and middle-level managers and supervisors as respondents. Primary data were collected using a structured, pre-tested questionnaire, of which 71 were returned (88.75% response rate), and analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation and multiple regression. The four practices jointly explained 46.5% of the variation in brand performance (R² = 0.465; F(4, 66) = 14.354, p < 0.001). Integration and diversification had the strongest influence (β = 0.385, p = 0.001), followed by stability and renewal (β = 0.285, p = 0.008), growth and expansion (β = 0.215, p = 0.029) and restructuring (β = 0.159, p = 0.035); all four null hypotheses were therefore rejected. Gaps were nonetheless observed in technology adoption, perceived product quality, regional customization, custom

hot.title: Interaction with AI companions and psychological well-being
How generative AI Is shaping the future of marketing
hot.venue: Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science
hot.abstract: Abstract Generative AI (Gen AI) is shaping the future of marketing. In the next decade, Gen AI will influence how marketers interact and communicate with customers, help create and deliver marketing content (text, images, and video), and inform methods for researching and developing new products and services. In both service and sales settings, Gen AI will affect customers directly and significantly. Therefore, marketers, researchers, and public policy makers require a clear understanding of Gen AI and its potential, as well as its limitations. To assist marketers in thinking through the adoption and implementation of Gen AI, the current article presents a four-quadrant organizing framework that highlights trade-offs in both the nature of Gen AI inputs and the extent of human augmentation needed to deliver Gen AI–generated outputs. This framework provides guidance for the selection and implementation of Gen AI tools, as well as recommendations for further research.

hot.title: The moderating role of personalized recommendations in the trust–satisfaction–loyalty relationship: an empirical study of AI-driven e-commerce
hot.abstract: Abstract Purpose This study investigates the effects of trust, satisfaction, and loyalty on AI-driven e-commerce, with a particular focus on how personalized recommendations moderate these relationships. It aims to explore how personalized AI features reshape consumer perceptions and decision-making. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research approach was used to collect data from a diverse group of e-commerce users who had interacted with AI-based recommendation systems. An online survey employing standardized scales for trust, satisfaction, loyalty, and personalization was administered, and data were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) to test the hypotheses. Findings The study reveals that trust has a significant positive influence on both satisfaction and loyalty. Personalization further strengthens these relationships by moderating the trust–satisfaction–loyalty dynamic. Satisfaction partially mediates the relationship between trust and loyalty, with the model’s explanatory power improving by 5% when personalization is included as a moderator. These results highlight the pivotal role of personalized recommendations in shaping consumer trust and satisfaction in AI-driven e-commerce. Practical implications Businesses can use personalized recommendation systems to enhance trust and satisfaction, thereby fostering loyalty. For example, platforms like Amazon and Netflix have successfully employed personalized AI algorithms to boost customer retention and engagement. Transparency features, such as explaining why certain products are recommended, and cultural sensitivity in algorithm design can further enhance customer trust and acceptance. e-commerce organizations should also invest in data privacy measures and clear algorithms to maintain consumer

hot.title: A Closer Look into Recent Video-based Learning Research: A Comprehensive Review of Video Characteristics, Tools, Technologies, and Learning Effectiveness
hot.venue: International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education
hot.abstract: People increasingly use videos on the Web for learning, be it for daily tasks in formal or informal educational settings. To enhance this type of learning, scientists are continuously conducting experiments, proposing guidelines, analyzing data, and researching artificial intelligence methods for tool development. In this comprehensive review, we analyze 257 articles (using PRISMA guidelines) on video-based learning from a technological perspective for the period from 2016 to 2021. One of the aims is to identify video characteristics that support learning as explored by previous research. Based on our analysis, we suggest a taxonomy that organizes the video characteristics and contextual aspects into eight categories: (1) audio features, (2) visual features, (3) textual features, (4) instructor behavior, (5) learners’ activities (play, pause, etc.), (6) interactive features (quizzes, etc.), (7) production style, and (8) instructional design. Also, we identify four representative methodological approaches: (1) tool support of video-based learning, (2) controlled experiments, (3) data analysis studies, and (4) design guidelines for learning videos. We find that the most explored characteristics are textual features followed by visual features, learners’ activities, and interactive features. Tools that aid learning through videos frequently utilize text from transcripts, video frames, and images. The learner’s activity is heavily explored through log files in data analysis studies, and interactive features are frequently scrutinized in controlled experiments. As further contributions, we contrast research findings on how video characteristics affect learning effectiveness, report on tasks and technologies used to develop tools, and summarize design guideline trends to prod

hot.title: Leading in the Digital Age: The Role of Leadership in Organizational Digital Transformation
hot.abstract: In the modern digital age, organizations face unprecedented challenges and possibilities while managing the intricacies of digital transformation. Accelerated technological developments, changing customer preferences, heightened competition, and dynamic regulatory environments necessitate companies to synchronize their business goals with technological innovations. Leadership is crucial in steering businesses through changes, requiring a deep understanding of change processes and the capacity to adjust leadership accordingly. This research addresses the central question: How does leadership effectively promote organizational digital transformation? The study examines how leaders can effectively promote the adoption of advanced technologies and the promotion of innovation, by first exploring the nature of digital transformation within organizations and then analyzing the evolving dynamics of leadership in this context. An integrative review of the Web of Science (WoS) and Scopus databases was conducted, using the search terms: “Leadership” and “Digital Transformation”. The findings emphasize that effective leadership is crucial for managing the minutiae of digital transformation, integrating technology into organizational processes to facilitate learning, collaboration, and agility, enabling companies to adapt to market shifts, reduce uncertainty, and enhance decision-making for sustainable growth. By using the right tools and with the right frequency, leaders may develop team cohesion—even at a distance. Attentive digital-age leaders will know how to leverage the right mechanisms, and herein, we hope to give some indication of how that may be achieved, so that digital transformation increases rather than decreases team motivation levels.
