latest.title: The Mediating Role of Self-Injurious Thoughts in the Relationship Between Psychological Distress and Death Obsession with Suicide Attempts Among Adolescents Experiencing War Anxiety
latest.venue: Journal of Adolescent and Youth Psychological Studies (JAYPS)
latest.abstract: Objective: This study aimed to examine the mediating role of self-injurious thoughts in the relationship between psychological distress and death obsession with suicide attempts among adolescents experiencing war anxiety. Methods and Materials: This applied study was conducted using a correlational design based on structural equation modeling. The statistical sample consisted of 215 adolescents aged 15 to 18 years living in Mahshahr, who were selected through voluntary sampling. The research instruments included the Shomali and Barkhordari War Anxiety Questionnaire, the Osman et al. Suicide Attempt Questionnaire, the Abdel-Khalek Death Obsession Scale, the Kessler et al. Psychological Distress Scale, and the Shomali and Barkhordari Self-Injurious Thoughts Questionnaire. Data were analyzed using Pearson correlation and structural equation modeling through SPSS version 27 and AMOS version 24. Findings: The inferential results showed that the direct effects of psychological distress and self-injurious thoughts on suicide attempts were positive and statistically significant. The direct effects of psychological distress and death obsession on self-injurious thoughts were also positive and statistically significant. In addition, the indirect effects of psychological distress and death obsession on suicide attempts through self-injurious thoughts were positive and statistically significant. However, the direct effect of death obsession on suicide attempts was not significant in the final structural model. These findings confirmed the mediating role of self-injurious thoughts in the relationship between psychological distress, death obsession, and suicide attempts among adolescents experiencing war anxiety. Conclusion: The findings indicate that self-injurious thoughts are a ke

latest.title: The Relationship of Classroom Emotion, Self-Compassion, and Tolerance of Ambiguity with Academic Anxiety among Female Senior High School Students in District 9 of Karaj
latest.venue: Journal of Adolescent and Youth Psychological Studies (JAYPS)
latest.abstract: Objective: This study aimed to examine the relationship of classroom emotion, self-compassion, and tolerance of ambiguity with academic anxiety among female senior high school students in District 9 of Karaj. Methods and Materials: The present study employed a descriptive-correlational research design. The statistical population consisted of female senior high school students in District 9 of Karaj, from whom 210 students were selected initially through multistage cluster sampling and finally through convenience sampling. Data were collected using the Friedman and Jacob Test Anxiety Questionnaire (1997), the Classroom Emotion Questionnaire developed by Titsworth et al. (2010), the Tolerance of Ambiguity Questionnaire developed by Weden et al. (2003), and the Short Form of the Self-Compassion Scale developed by Raes et al. (2011). The collected data were analyzed using descriptive indices, Pearson correlation coefficient, and stepwise multiple regression analysis. Findings: The inferential findings indicated a significant negative relationship between classroom emotion and academic anxiety, suggesting that more positive classroom emotional experiences were associated with lower levels of academic anxiety. A significant negative relationship was also found between self-compassion and academic anxiety, indicating that students with higher self-compassion experienced lower academic anxiety. In the stepwise regression analysis, classroom emotion emerged as the strongest predictor and explained 15.50% of the variance in academic anxiety. Self-compassion was added in the second step and explained an additional 2.20% of the variance. Together, classroom emotion and self-compassion accounted for 17.70% of the total variance in academic anxiety. Tolerance of ambiguity did not ent

latest.title: Prediction of Cognitive Flexibility Based on Attention Control, Working Memory, and Problem-Solving Skills in Adolescents Using CatBoost
latest.venue: Journal of Adolescent and Youth Psychological Studies (JAYPS)
latest.abstract: Objective: The present study aimed to predict cognitive flexibility based on attention control, working memory, and problem-solving skills in adolescents using the CatBoost machine learning algorithm. Methods and Materials: This study was conducted using a quantitative, descriptive-correlational, and predictive design. The statistical population included adolescents studying in secondary schools in Tehran during the 2025–2026 academic year. The final sample consisted of 384 adolescents selected through multistage cluster sampling. Data were collected using standardized self-report instruments measuring cognitive flexibility, attention control, working memory, and problem-solving skills. After preliminary data screening, descriptive indices, reliability coefficients, Pearson correlation coefficients, and machine learning-based predictive analyses were conducted. The CatBoost algorithm was used to predict cognitive flexibility, and the dataset was divided into training and test subsets. Model performance was evaluated using mean absolute error, mean squared error, root mean squared error, coefficient of determination, and five-fold cross-validation. Feature importance analysis was also performed to determine the relative contribution of each predictor. Findings: The results showed that cognitive flexibility had significant positive correlations with problem-solving skills (r = 0.61, p < 0.01), attention control (r = 0.55, p < 0.01), and working memory (r = 0.48, p < 0.01). The CatBoost model demonstrated acceptable predictive accuracy. In the training set, the model explained 76.5% of the variance in cognitive flexibility, while in the test set, it explained 65.2% of the variance. The cross-validation results also supported the stability of the model, with an average R² o

latest.title: Assessing the attentional dynamics of Responding to Joint Attention in infancy via online webcam-based eye-tracking
latest.abstract: Responding to Joint Attention (RJA) is a foundational social-cognitive skill that unfolds through a sequence of distinct attentional processes: engagement with a social partner, orienting toward a referent, and sustained attention to a shared point of interest. Traditional assessments of joint attention often rely on aggregate behavioral scores that may not capture this fine-grained temporal structure. The present study developed and tested a remotely administered, webcam-based eye-tracking task, delivered via the Labvanced platform, to characterize the attentional dynamics underlying RJA in infants and toddlers aged 10 to 36 months ( N = 29). The task decomposed RJA into three sequential phases and included a gaze-contingent delay manipulation to probe how infants balance attention between the social partner and the cued object under varying temporal demands, quantified through dwell time and gaze re-engagement (entry rate) toward the face, the cued object, and an uncued object. Infants showed a clear attentional hierarchy, with the greatest engagement directed toward the face during the early phases, followed by a gradual reallocation of attention toward the cued object as the referent became identifiable. This temporal profile is consistent with theoretical accounts describing joint attention as an unfolding sequence, in which infants first anchor attention to the social partner before coordinating it with a shared referent. Age-related differences emerged selectively in later phases of attentional maintenance, with older infants showing reduced monitoring of the social partner's face after the partner's gaze had shifted toward the referent while attention to the target itself remained stable across age, although the wide age range relative to sample size may limit s

latest.title: Exploring Kindergarten Teachers’ Experiences in Using Teacher-Made Interactive Reading Materials
latest.venue: Journal of Education and Learning Reviews
latest.abstract: Background and Aim: Teacher-made interactive reading materials can provide context-responsive opportunities for early literacy instruction. This study explored kindergarten teachers’ experiences in developing and using these materials in Tubod, Lanao del Norte, Philippines, focusing on preparation, instructional use, perceived benefits, challenges, and coping strategies. Materials and Methods: A qualitative single-case study involved seven purposively selected public-school kindergarten teachers with relevant experience. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, field notes, artifact analysis, and document review and analysed thematically. Triangulation and member checking supported credibility. Classroom observations were not conducted. Results: Teachers developed three main categories of materials: flash cards and charts, multisensory and hands-on resources, and materials informed by the Marungko Approach and Claveria Technique. Preparation reflected learning objectives, learner readiness, and available low-cost resources. Teachers integrated the materials into guided instruction, scaffolding, questioning, modelling, repeated practice, and play-based activities. They reported increased attention and participation, as well as support for letter–sound recognition and foundational reading skills. Financial constraints, preparation demands, and limited durability complicated implementation. Teachers addressed these challenges through alternative and backup materials, durable resources, resource optimisation, and instructional flexibility. Conclusion: Teacher-made interactive reading materials offered adaptable resources for kindergarten literacy instruction, reflecting teachers’ creativity and responsiveness to classroom needs. Reported benefits represent te

latest.title: Physical activity engagement and the well-being of freshman students of local college in Lipa City
latest.venue: International Journal of Sports Health Fitness and Movement Studies (IJSHEFMS)
latest.abstract: Aim: This study examined physical activity engagement and the academic, social, and emotional well-being of 110 freshman Bachelor of Secondary Education (BSED) students at Kolehiyo ng Lungsod ng Lipa (KLL).It assessed autonomy, competence, and relatedness; described the three well-being domains; tested their relationships; and developed a proposed physical activity program.Methodology: A quantitative descriptive-correlational design was used.All 110 eligible freshman BSED students were included through total population enumeration.Data were gathered using structured questionnaires based on Self-Determination Theory and established student well-being measures.Composite means and inferential statistics were used for analysis.Results: Physical activity engagement was High for autonomy (3.40) and competence (3.34), and Very High for relatedness (3.55).Well-being was High for academic (3.32) and social (3.48), and Very High for emotional well-being (3.55).No statistically significant relationship was found between physical activity engagement and academic (p = .183),social (p = .207),or emotional well-being (p = .261).Conclusion: Respondents reported favorable physical activity engagement and well-being, with relatedness and emotional well-being receiving the highest means in their respective domains.The analyses found no statistically significant associations between physical activity engagement and the three well-being domains.The proposed KLL Holistic Well-Being Movement Initiative offers structured activity opportunities; its effectiveness remains to be evaluated.

latest.title: Leyendo lo propio: evidencia científica sobre textos del patrimonio cultural local y comprensión lectora en educación básica rural
latest.venue: Neosapiencia Revista especializada en Ciencias de la Educación
latest.abstract: Las escuelas rurales suelen enseñar a leer con textos ajenos al entorno de sus estudiantes, y el patrimonio cultural local se propone como alternativa. El presente trabajo analiza la evidencia publicada entre 2023 y 2025 sobre el efecto de las estrategias basadas en textos del patrimonio cultural local en la comprensión lectora de estudiantes de educación primaria, con el fin de fundamentar una intervención en la escuela rural ecuatoriana. Se realizó una revisión sistemática exploratoria de enfoque mixto: la búsqueda en OpenAlex, ERIC y SciELO recuperó 397 registros, de los cuales 41 estudios cumplieron los criterios de elegibilidad. El corpus se concentró en Indonesia (63,4 %) y en diseños evaluados con un solo grupo (36,6 %). Diez estudios emplearon grupo de comparación: ocho, con textos patrimoniales, informaron mejoras en la comprensión lectora, y dos localizaron el efecto en la comprensión del lenguaje y el vocabulario. Cinco estudios se situaron en contextos rurales y ninguno midió la comprensión lectora con grupo de comparación. Se concluye que la evidencia es abundante y favorable, pero de certeza baja y ajena a la escuela rural: el vacío es de validación contextual y de rigor, no de fundamentación.

latest.title: The Influence of Work Environment and Organizational Culture on Employee Job Satisfaction at PT Semen Indonesia Logistik
latest.abstract: Employee job satisfaction is an essential factor in maintaining workforce effectiveness and organizational performance, particularly in logistics operations that require effective coordination and reliable work processes. This study aimed to examine the influence of work environment and organizational culture on employee job satisfaction at PT Semen Indonesia Logistik. A quantitative approach using a survey method was employed, involving 30 employees from the Procurement, General Affairs and Asset Management, and Corporate Finance departments, selected through a saturated sampling technique. Data were collected using a closed-ended questionnaire with a four-point Likert scale and analyzed through multiple linear regression using IBM SPSS. The findings revealed that the work environment had a positive and statistically significant relationship with employee job satisfaction (B = 1.182, t = 2.774, p = 0.010), whereas organizational culture showed a positive but statistically non-significant partial relationship (B = 0.331, t = 1.891, p = 0.069). Nevertheless, the overall regression model was statistically significant (F = 14.051, p < 0.001), with an adjusted R-squared value of 0.474, indicating that the two independent variables jointly explain g.ed 47.4% of the variation in employee job satisfaction. These findings highlight the importance of maintaining a supportive work environment, providing adequate facilities, and strengthening organizational practices related to employee recognition and rewards. This study contributes empirical evidence concerning the relationship between organizational conditions and employee job satisfaction in a logistics and cement-distribution company, although its findings are limited to the selected departments.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Hubungan Self-Esteem dengan Prokrastinasi Akademik pada Mahasiswa Bekerja di Universitas Esa Unggul
latest.venue: JISOSEPOL Jurnal Ilmu Sosial Ekonomi dan Politik
latest.abstract: Prokrastinasi akademik merupakan fenomena yang banyak terjadi di kalangan mahasiswa dan dapat berdampak pada kualitas belajar serta penyelesaian tugas akademik. Kondisi ini juga dapat dialami oleh mahasiswa bekerja yang menjalani peran ganda sebagai mahasiswa dan pekerja, sehingga dituntut untuk mampu mengelola waktu, tanggung jawab, dan tuntutan akademik secara seimbang. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui hubungan self-esteem dengan prokrastinasi akademik pada mahasiswa bekerja Universitas Esa Unggul. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan metode korelasional. Subjek penelitian berjumlah 261 mahasiswa bekerja jenjang S1 Program Studi Psikologi Universitas Esa Unggul. Pengumpulan data dilakukan menggunakan skala self-esteem dan skala prokrastinasi akademik. Analisis data menggunakan korelasi Spearman. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan koefisien korelasi sebesar, 0,628 dengan nilai signifikansi 0,001 (p < 0,01), yang menunjukkan adanya hubungan negatif yang kuat dan signifikan antara self-esteem dan prokrastinasi akademik. Artinya, semakin tinggi self-esteem mahasiswa, semakin rendah kecenderungan melakukan prokrastinasi akademik, dan sebaliknya.

latest.title: Beyond the Classroom: A Case Study of Parents' Experiences in Parent-Mediated Interventions for Learners with Special Needs
latest.venue: Journal of Education and Learning Reviews
latest.abstract: Background and Aim: Parent-mediated interventions have gained recognition as a cost-effective approach to supporting children with special needs, particularly in low-resource settings where professional services remain inaccessible. While existing literature has examined the effectiveness and barriers of these interventions, it has not fully captured how parents themselves experience their transition into this role, particularly through the lens of established transition theory. This qualitative case study addresses this gap by exploring how parents and caregivers of learners with special needs experience their transition into and sustained involvement in parent-mediated intervention, using Schlossberg's Transition Theory as a theory-informed analytic lens and extending it by examining how geographic and institutional scarcity appears to shape each of its four factors within a single resource-constrained setting. Materials and Methods: A descriptive qualitative case study design was employed, anchored in an interpretivist and constructivist paradigm. Semi-structured, in-depth interviews were conducted with six parents and caregivers who had sustained active involvement in parent-mediated intervention for at least six months at Malangas Central SPED Center, Malangas District, Division of Zamboanga Sibugay, Philippines. Data were analyzed using Braun and Clarke's six-phase thematic analysis, applied deductively at the level of Schlossberg's four predetermined factors, Situation, Self, Support, and Strategies, with sub-themes developed inductively within each factor. Results: Analysis within the four predetermined factors surfaced patterns of necessity-driven entry into the interventionist role, an initial period of self-doubt giving way to a personally constructed sense o

latest.title: Human Capital in the Creative Industries and a Competency Model for Performing Arts Producers
latest.abstract: This article proposes a conceptual competency model for performing arts producers that explains their role in forming, coordinating, and developing the human capital of creative teams. The research problem concerns the limitations of individual lists of producer skills in explaining how diverse professional knowledge becomes a team's capacity to deliver a cultural project. The methodological framework combines research on human capital, project-based organizing, and team learning through theoretical synthesis. The article distinguishes individual human capital, team human capital resources, the social capital of professional networks, and the organizational conditions of collaboration. The model comprises six interconnected competency domains: industry-specific, managerial, creative, interpersonal and communication, digital, and adaptive competencies. Their relationships with team outcomes are explained through the selection of complementary team members, role alignment, knowledge sharing, psychological safety, and organizational reflection. The article formulates theoretical propositions for future empirical testing and proposes behavioral indicators and applications in education and creative team management. It also considers the ethical limits of a resource-based approach and the model's application under organizational instability. The contribution lies in linking producers' individual competencies, mechanisms of team interaction, and creative project outcomes. The model is a theoretical proposal; its structure, indicators, and anticipated relationships require further validation.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: THE ROLE OF NATIONAL TENNIS CHAMPIONSHIPS IN JUNIOR-TO-SENIOR ATHLETE TRANSITION: PERCEPTIONS AND BARRIERS
latest.venue: Journal of Physical Activity and Sports (JPAS)
latest.abstract: The transition from junior to senior competition is a critical phase in an athlete’s career, requiring technical and psychological readiness. In Indonesia, National Championships (Kejurnas) are expected to facilitate this transition. This study examined junior tennis athletes’ perceptions of the 2024 National Tennis Championship in Riau as a transitional platform and identified related challenges. A quantitative descriptive survey was conducted involving 25 junior tennis athletes in the KU 16 and KU 18 categories. Data were collected using validated closed-ended and open-ended questionnaires and analyzed through descriptive statistics and thematic narrative analysis. The findings showed that 68% of athletes had a very positive perception of the championship, while 68% felt very ready to transition to senior competition. Furthermore, 72% considered the event very helpful in supporting their development. Despite these positive perceptions, athletes reported several challenges. Performance anxiety and psychological instability were the most frequently identified barriers (n = 9), followed by disparities in opponents’ strength and competitive experience (n = 7). These findings indicate that junior athletes generally perceive themselves as prepared for senior-level competition and recognize the championship’s developmental value. However, psychological readiness and competitive adaptation remain important concerns. Therefore, targeted mental skills training and structured exposure to high-intensity competition are recommended to strengthen athletes’ confidence, resilience, and adaptability, ultimately supporting a more effective transition from junior to senior tennis competition.

latest.title: The Effect of Emotional Regulation on Stress
latest.abstract: This study aims to determine the stress conditions and emotional regulation in students of SMP Negeri 1 Pantai Labu, and to analyze the effect of emotional regulation on their stress levels. The study used a quantitative approach with a correlational method. The study sample consisted of 399 students selected through a sampling technique appropriate to the characteristics of the population. Data collection was conducted using a closed questionnaire that had been tested for validity and reliability. Data analysis included prerequisite tests (normality and linearity tests) and hypothesis testing through Pearson correlation analysis and simple linear regression. The results showed that there was a significant influence between emotional regulation and student stress, evidenced by a significance value of 0.000 < 0.05. The regression equation obtained was Y = 50.227 + 0.376X, with a beta coefficient value of 0.266. This indicates that emotional regulation plays a role in determining stress levels, although the direction of the relationship depends on the interpretation of the scale used. The coefficient of determination (R²) value of 0.071 indicates that emotional regulation explains 7.1% of the variation in stress in students, while the rest is influenced by other factors outside the variables studied. This study concluded that students' ability to manage their emotions contributes to reducing stress levels, although this contribution is limited. Therefore, improving emotional regulation skills needs to be considered as a strategy for managing stress among students.

latest.title: Socio-Demographic and Behavioral Determinants of Poor Sleep Quality in Third-Trimester Pregnancy: A Study from Central Brazil
latest.abstract: Abstract Objective To evaluate the prevalence of poor sleep quality and identify its associated factors among third-trimester pregnant women attending a public healthcare service in a municipality in Goiás, Brazil. Methods This was a cross-sectional, analytical, and epidemiological study conducted with a probabilistic sample of 243 pregnant women. Sleep quality was assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), along with sociodemographic, behavioral, health, sexual, and pregnancy-related variables. Data were analyzed using Poisson regression with robust variance to estimate prevalence ratios (PR) and their respective 95% confidence intervals (95% CI), with a significance level of 5% ( p < 0.05). Results The prevalence of poor sleep quality was 24.7%. Multivariate analysis identified non-white race/color (PR = 4.30; 95% CI 1.48–12.56), unemployment (PR = 3.07; 95%CI 1.23–7.63), and not engaging in physical activity (PR = 3.28; 95% CI 1.37–7.83) as independent predictors of poor sleep quality. Additionally, excessive daytime sleepiness (PR = 3.48; 95% CI 1.55–7.82) and high risk of stress (PR = 2.71; 95% CI 1.09–6.75) were also significantly associated with the outcome. Conclusion Poor sleep quality is a highly prevalent issue in the studied population and is strongly associated with sociodemographic and behavioral factors. These findings highlight the importance of integrating into prenatal care interventions that address the social determinants of health.

latest.title: Beyond competencies: a CBT-informed approach to leadership development in the public sector
latest.abstract: Purpose This paper examines a developmental gap in competency-led public-sector leadership: leaders may know expected behaviours yet find them less accessible under pressure. It considers a cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT)-informed response centred on interpretation, regulation and behavioural choice. Design/methodology/approach This conceptual Viewpoint synthesises selected scholarship on public leadership and competencies, leadership cognition, emotion regulation, reflexivity and coaching psychology. These literatures are integrated with practice-informed reflection to develop Reframe. Regulate. Lead. as one structured response to the competency-access problem. Findings Cognition, appraisal and affect are established influences on leadership behaviour, but their implications are not always integrated into practitioner-facing public-sector development. Leadership development should therefore address interpretation, regulation and purposeful behavioural choice alongside observable competence. Research limitations/implications The framework is conceptual and has not been empirically validated. Future research should test its mechanisms, feasibility, contextual and cultural applicability and comparative value alongside other coaching and reflective-development approaches. Practical implications Reframe. Regulate. Lead. may support self-reflection, executive coaching, reflective supervision and post-incident review, with appropriate facilitator competence and clear boundaries from clinical treatment. Social implications If empirically supported, more reflective and proportionate leadership may contribute to conditions associated with psychological safety, fairness, learning and institutional trust. Originality/value The paper does not claim cognition or emotion as new t

latest.title: The Impact of Higher Educational Qualification on Job Performance in Public Sector Institutions: A Case Study of the Ghana Audit Service
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: Organisations are relying more on continuous skill acquisition and higher educational qualifications (HEQs). This study evaluates the impact of acquiring HEQs as a form of self-development on the job performance of employees in the public sector. Using the branches of the Ghana Audit Service (GAS) in the Greater Accra Region as a case study, the research collected data from 327 staff of six major operational departments using a descriptive cross-sectional quantitative survey design. Through descriptive statistics, most employees believed that the acquisition of higher educational qualifications enhanced their role clarity and technical auditing skills, as well as their ability to achieve their targets and communicate functionally. Chi-square test analysis showed that there was no statistically significant linear association between the level of formal higher education and standardised metrics of job performance. The study concluded that while acquiring higher education qualifications has a positive influence on an individual's self-reported level of efficiency, this is not the case for public sector job performance. Job performance remains influenced by different contextual factors such as frameworks and structures of career development, as well as the nature of employment support provided by the organisation.

latest.title: Perceived Social Support And Parenting Stress Among Indonesian Family Caregivers Of Persons With Disabilities: Do Sources Of Support Matter?
latest.abstract: Family caregivers of persons with disabilities may experience substantial parenting demands, making interpersonal resources such as perceived social support potentially important for their adjustment. This study examined the association between perceived social support and parenting stress among Indonesian family caregivers of persons with disabilities and explored whether support from family, friends, or a significant other showed the strongest relationship with lower parenting stress. A cross-sectional design was used. Participants were recruited through nonprobability purposive sampling in a community-based program conducted by Universitas Tarumanagara in collaboration with the Indonesian National Commission on Disabilities. Valid data from 152 caregivers were analyzed. Perceived social support was assessed using the Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support, whereas parenting stress was measured using the Indonesian adaptation of the Parental Stress Scale. Participants generally reported high perceived social support and relatively low parenting stress. Perceived social support was negatively associated with parenting stress, rs = −.388, p < .001, and significantly predicted parenting stress, β = −.422, p < .001, accounting for 17.8% of its variance. Support from family, friends, and significant others was negatively associated with parenting stress. Support from a significant other showed the strongest observed association and remained the only significant unique predictor when the three sources were examined simultaneously, β = −.302, p = .010. These findings suggest that perceived social support represents an important interpersonal resource in disability caregiving, while highlighting the potential relevance of dependable, personally meaningful relation

latest.title: Analisis Faktor yang Memengaruhi Kecenderungan Inferiority Feeling pada Remaja Putri di Makassar
latest.abstract: Adolescents often face a wide variety of problems. These problems typically include physical, mental, social, and emotional issues. One of the mental health issues among adolescents is a feeling of inferiority. This has become a major concern in adolescent mental health. Parenting styles, physical disabilities, and socioeconomic status are known to influence the tendency toward feelings of inferiority. Islam has taught us not to be weak or feel inferior, as stated, for example, in Surah Ali Imran/3:139. This study aims to determine the influence of parenting styles, physical disabilities, and socioeconomic status on the tendency toward feelings of inferiority among adolescent girls in Makassar. This study is an analytical observational quantitative study using a cross-sectional approach. It was conducted among adolescents aged 14-15 years selected from five schools in the city of Makassar using the Proportionate Stratified Random Sampling technique, yielding a sample of 227 respondents. Data were collected via a questionnaire. Data analysis was performed using the chi-square test. The results indicate a significant association between parenting styles and physical disabilities and the tendency toward feelings of inferiority (p < 0.05), whereas economic status did not show a significant association with this tendency (p > 0.05). This study underscores the importance of interventions to enhance parents’ understanding of parenting styles and to foster greater self-confidence in adolescents to support better mental health.

latest.title: Challenges and Barriers to Implementing Effective Supply Chain Management (SCM) on Manufacturing-Based Projects
latest.venue: WORLD JOURNAL OF INNOVATION AND MODERN TECHNOLOGY
latest.abstract: The study's specific goal was to evaluate the challenges and barriers to implementing efficient SCM in manufacturing-based projects in Imo state. This research was influenced by the resource based approach, systems, supply chain collaboration, and lean production and supply chain integration theories. The investigation was conducted using a survey research methodology, with a purposive sampling strategy using the Cochran's method to choose the sample size from a population of manufacturing-based project enterprises in Imo state. To collect data and conduct surveys, a well-structured questionnaire was used, as well as personal observations and trips to manufacturing-based project firms. The collected data was displayed as frequency distribution in tables and figures using IBM SPSS Statistics version 26.0. The primary aims of the study were analysed using exploratory factor analysis. A study of 415 respondents who were involved in manufacturing-based project-related activities revealed that the challenges and barriers to effective SCM implementation in manufacturing-based projects in Imo state Nigeria include: lack of commitment and support by top management, supply chain risk management, resistance of management to change, inventory management, buyer-supplier relationship, resistance of workers to change, organisational barriers, and insufficient This study suggests that crucial solutions include building procurement practices, encouraging collaboration with suppliers, and guaranteeing top management support.

latest.title: IMPACT OF BUYER BEHAVIOUR AND BRAND LOYALTY ON BRAND PREFERENCE OF CHOCOLATES (A STUDY ON CONSUMER’S PERCEPTION IN CHENNAI CITY)
latest.venue: RCHUB JOURNAL OF CONTEMPORARY TRENDS IN MANAGEMENT COMMERCE AND ECONOMICS (JCMCE)
latest.abstract: Chocolate is consumed by several people all over the world. Chocolate is made out of cocoa which brings delight to its consumers. Consumer’s buying behaviour has drawn an impact on designing marketing strategies to create brand preference. Several brands available in the market are laying attention on the consumers to reap the benefits of repeat sales that increases brand loyalty of customers. Brand preference denotes the brand that is preferred under expectations of equality in price and availability. The main aim of this study is to understand the consumer’s perception, buyer behaviour, brand loyalty and brand preference towards chocolates. Data had been collected with the help of structured questionnaire which comprised of two parts. Part I dealt with demographic profile of the respondents and part II dealt with the perception of consumers relating to buyer behaviour, brand loyalty and brand preference as regards chocolates. Questionnaire was circulated among 100 respondents in the city of Chennai. Simple percentage analysis was used to find out the demographic profile and perception of the respondents. Chi-Square test was used to find out the association between the occupation and the brand loyalty of consumers with respect to chocolates. Factor Analysis revealed that the major factors influencing brand preference were brand awareness, brand appearance, emotional attachment and brand experience

latest.title: Beyond bedtime routines: sleep-schedule organization, sleep-onset conditions, and nighttime parental practices associated with early-childhood sleep quality in Armenia
latest.abstract: Background Parental sleep-related behaviors may have different functional meanings depending on whether they occur before sleep or are maintained as sleep begins. We examined associations of sleep-schedule organization, sleep-onset conditions, and nighttime resettling practices with BISQ-R Infant Sleep scores among Armenian children aged 6–36 months. Methods This cross-sectional study included 417 families recruited by systematic random sampling at Wigmore Women's and Children's Hospital between December 2025 and March 2026. Mothers completed the culturally adapted Armenian Brief Infant Sleep Questionnaire-Revised (BISQ-R). Univariable analyses assessed reported bedtime, bedtime-preparation start time, and bedtime regularity. Hierarchical regression sequentially included child/family, sleep-schedule, and behavioral/contextual variables. Nighttime breastfeeding was examined among children with nighttime awakenings. Results Later reported bedtime and later bedtime-preparation start time were associated with lower Infant Sleep scores, whereas greater bedtime regularity was associated with higher scores in univariable analyses. Sleep-schedule variables added 2.7% of variance (Δ R 2 = 0.027, p = 0.004), and behavioral/contextual factors an additional 15.5% (Δ R 2 = 0.155, p < 0.001). The final model explained 18.7% ( R 2 = 0.187; adjusted R 2 = 0.157). Bedtime regularity remained positively associated with Infant Sleep score (unstandardized coefficient [ B ] = 0.936, standardized coefficient [β] = 0.091, p = 0.047), whereas reported bedtime was non-significant ( p = 0.101). Compared with being held/rocked, falling asleep with an adult present without being held/rocked ( B = 4.861, β = 0.136, p = 0.009) or independently ( B = 15.758, β = 0.176, p < 0.001) was associated with

latest.title: Comprehensive treatment of psychological trauma patients: professional actors’ experiences of external framing factors and treatment characteristics in a Norwegian inpatient context
latest.abstract: Abstract Background Evaluations of treatment of psychiatric patients often consist of comparisons of quantitative patient-level data pre- and post-treatment. This qualitative study explores the thoughts of different actors in contact with psychological trauma patients before, during, and/or after comprehensive treatment. The treatment consisted of physical activity, healthy nutrition, social support, and psychoeducation, in addition to pharmacology and psychotherapy. The study aim was to explore factors influencing the comprehensive treatment on trauma patients, from the perspective of various health-care professionals and representatives of voluntary organizations. Methods Individual semi-structured interviews were conducted with 11 informants, working in various mental healthcare organizations in Norway. Manifest content analysis was used to analyse the data. Results Two main categories emerged in the analysis; (1) External framing factors , underpinned by the two sub-categories, Referral thresholds and patient status , and Organizational aspects post-treatment , and (2) Treatment at the inpatient facility , underpinned by the sub-categories Patient participation and commitment , and Feeling safe and secure through treatment and beyond . The received responses indicated that the treatment was affected by the fact that patients referred to the inpatient facility were reported to often have more complex problems than previously. During treatment, patients’ preparedness and commitment to actively participate in the intense treatment were claimed to be important factors for treatment outcomes. Returning home after treatment tends to be a vulnerable phase, with little support from mental health care. According to the informants, there is currently no automatic follow-up ca

latest.title: Digital Transformation and Marketing Capability: The Moderating Role of Digital Marketing
latest.venue: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
latest.abstract: Based on the resource-based view and contingency theory, this study investigates the impact of digital transformation on corporate marketing capabilities and examines the moderating role of digital marketing. Using a sample of Chinese A-share listed companies from 2016 to 2024, the empirical analysis reveals that digital transformation significantly enhances marketing capabilities, while digital marketing further strengthens the causal relationship between them. Heterogeneity analysis shows that these effects vary across firms at different life cycle stages and with different pollution attributes. This study extends existing research on the microeconomic consequences of digital transformation and provides practical insights for firms in converting digital resources into competitive advantages in marketing.

latest.title: Value Orientations, Product-Specific Considerations, and Conditional Consumer Acceptance of Refrigerators Containing Recycled Materials in Poland
latest.abstract: Abstract The transition toward a circular economy requires not only technological and regulatory changes but also consumer acceptance of products incorporating recycled materials. While previous research has extensively examined pro-environmental consumption, comparatively less attention has been paid to high-involvement durable goods, where purchase decisions are infrequent and involve substantial financial and functional considerations. This study explores how consumers evaluate refrigerators containing recycled insulation by examining the interplay between personal value orientations, product-specific considerations, overall product evaluation, and conditional purchase consideration. The study draws on two qualitative focus group interviews conducted in Poland with 14 participants representing two age cohorts. The transcripts were analysed using thematic analysis combining deductive and inductive coding. The findings show that biospheric, altruistic, egoistic, and hedonic value orientations coexist in consumers’ reasoning, while their relative relevance varies with the purchase context. Product-specific considerations, including price, quality, durability and reliability, energy efficiency, functionality and usability, design and aesthetics, and credible product information formed an important complementary dimension of product evaluation. Recycled insulation was not evaluated as inherently positive; rather, participants’ evaluations were qualified by the perceived credibility of environmental benefits and expectations concerning product performance. Purchase consideration was likewise strongly conditional, particularly on price comparability, durability, reliability, and transparent environmental information. The study contributes to sustainable consumption and circ

latest.title: Investigating the mental health outcomes of caregivers of children with intellectual disabilities in Saudi Arabia
latest.abstract: Background: Understanding the mental health challenges faced by caregivers of children with intellectual disabilities is essential for the design of targeted interventions. Aim: To examine the challenges faced by caregivers of children with disabilities in Saudi Arabia and their coping strategies. Methods: Between January and April 2024, we interviewed 120 primary caregivers of children diagnosed with intellectual disabilities residing in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, and surrounding regions. We analysed the quantitative data using SPSS version 28 and qualitative data using NVivo. We performed correlation and regression analyses to examine the associations between resilience, social support and mental health outcomes. Results: There were significant correlations between higher resilience and lower depression, anxiety and stress (r = –0.61, P < 0.01 for resilience and stress; r = –0.54, P < 0.01 for resilience and depression), indicating strong associations. Perceived social support showed moderate negative correlations with mental health challenges (r = –0.48, P < 0.01 for social support and anxiety), suggesting that stronger support networks were associated with better psychological outcomes. Challenges faced by caregivers included emotional strain, financial difficulties and social stigma. The caregivers reported receiving support from families, peers and health workers, and built resilience through emotional coping, planning and problemsolving, and positive reframing and acceptance. Conclusion: The strong negative correlations between resilience and mental health outcomes indicate the need for targeted interventions among caregivers of children with disabilities in Saudia Arabia to enhance their resilience and help mitigate psychological distress.

latest.title: The Effect of Game-Based Learning on English Vocabulary Acquisition among Three-Year-Old EFL Learners in a Private Educational Institution
latest.abstract: This study examined the effect of game-based learning on English vocabulary acquisition among three-year-old EFL learners in a private educational institution. A quantitative pre-experimental design with a one-group pre-test and post-test structure was used during a six-month instructional period. The intervention incorporated age-appropriate game-based activities such as matching games, movement activities, object identification, songs, flashcards, memory games, and role-play. Vocabulary learning focused on receptive and productive knowledge through repeated visual, auditory, kinesthetic, and interactive exposure. Data were collected through a vocabulary pre-test and post-test, an observation checklist, and a teacher record sheet. The results showed an increase in the overall mean from 1.97 in the pre-test to 4.20 in the post-test. The strongest improvements were observed in the comprehension of simple instructions and vocabulary recognition, while oral vocabulary production also increased considerably. These findings suggest that game-based learning can provide developmentally appropriate and engaging opportunities for very young EFL learners to acquire and retain English vocabulary. The study highlights the importance of integrating structured play, repetition, movement, and multisensory resources into early childhood English instruction.

latest.title: Digital Skills Gap in Accounting Automation in Nigeria: A Theoretical Context
latest.venue: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SOCIAL SCIENCES AND MANAGEMENT RESEARCH
latest.abstract: This study examined the digital skills gap in accounting automation journey in Nigeria from a theoretical perspective, based on the rapid adoption of accounting technology in its various contours with its altering of the accounting landscape from its traditional manual-driven milieu to analytics and strategic focused. Gleaned from the open-source literature and Nigerian context specific studies, it is evident that there is an emerging accounting technology driven ecosystem, but the digital competencies required to effectively utilize and deepen these technologies remain inadequate among many accounting graduates and professionals in Nigeria. Hence, based on the open-source Nigerian context-based studies interrogated, there exists a significant mismatch between accounting education curricula, acquired skill sets and industry accounting technological demands. While, organisations increasingly invest in automated accounting systems, deficiencies in technical ICT skills, data analytics competence, ERP proficiency, AI knowledge, and cybersecurity awareness constrain effective utilization. The study further established from the review that contextual factors such as quality of accounting education, professional training frameworks, organizational digital investment, ICT infrastructure, and regulatory support significantly influence the magnitude of the skills gap. Hence, harnessing the gains of accounting technology is feasible only when users possess adequate digital competence. Therefore, bridging the digital skills gap requires comprehensive curriculum reform, continuous professional development, institutional investment in digital infrastructure, and stronger collaboration between academia, professional bodies, and industry.

hot.title: Trust in scientists and their role in society across 68 countries
hot.abstract: Science is crucial for evidence-based decision-making. Public trust in scientists can help decision makers act on the basis of the best available evidence, especially during crises. However, in recent years the epistemic authority of science has been challenged, causing concerns about low public trust in scientists. We interrogated these concerns with a preregistered 68-country survey of 71,922 respondents and found that in most countries, most people trust scientists and agree that scientists should engage more in society and policymaking. We found variations between and within countries, which we explain with individual- and country-level variables, including political orientation. While there is no widespread lack of trust in scientists, we cannot discount the concern that lack of trust in scientists by even a small minority may affect considerations of scientific evidence in policymaking. These findings have implications for scientists and policymakers seeking to maintain and increase trust in scientists.

hot.title: Interaction with AI companions and psychological well-being
How generative AI Is shaping the future of marketing
hot.venue: Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science
hot.abstract: Abstract Generative AI (Gen AI) is shaping the future of marketing. In the next decade, Gen AI will influence how marketers interact and communicate with customers, help create and deliver marketing content (text, images, and video), and inform methods for researching and developing new products and services. In both service and sales settings, Gen AI will affect customers directly and significantly. Therefore, marketers, researchers, and public policy makers require a clear understanding of Gen AI and its potential, as well as its limitations. To assist marketers in thinking through the adoption and implementation of Gen AI, the current article presents a four-quadrant organizing framework that highlights trade-offs in both the nature of Gen AI inputs and the extent of human augmentation needed to deliver Gen AI–generated outputs. This framework provides guidance for the selection and implementation of Gen AI tools, as well as recommendations for further research.

hot.title: The evolving field of digital mental health: current evidence and implementation issues for smartphone apps, generative artificial intelligence, and virtual reality
hot.abstract: The expanding domain of digital mental health is transitioning beyond traditional telehealth to incorporate smartphone apps, virtual reality, and generative artificial intelligence, including large language models. While industry setbacks and methodological critiques have highlighted gaps in evidence and challenges in scaling these technologies, emerging solutions rooted in co-design, rigorous evaluation, and implementation science offer promising pathways forward. This paper underscores the dual necessity of advancing the scientific foundations of digital mental health and increasing its real-world applicability through five themes. First, we discuss recent technological advances in digital phenotyping, virtual reality, and generative artificial intelligence. Progress in this latter area, specifically designed to create new outputs such as conversations and images, holds unique potential for the mental health field. Given the spread of smartphone apps, we then evaluate the evidence supporting their utility across various mental health contexts, including well-being, depression, anxiety, schizophrenia, eating disorders, and substance use disorders. This broad view of the field highlights the need for a new generation of more rigorous, placebo-controlled, and real-world studies. We subsequently explore engagement challenges that hamper all digital mental health tools, and propose solutions, including human support, digital navigators, just-in-time adaptive interventions, and personalized approaches. We then analyze implementation issues, emphasizing clinician engagement, service integration, and scalable delivery models. We finally consider the need to ensure that innovations work for all people and thus can bridge digital health disparities, reviewing the evidence on ta

hot.title: Artificial Intelligence and Its Role in Shaping Organizational Work Practices and Culture
hot.abstract: The advent of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is profoundly transforming organizational landscapes, significantly influencing work practices and triggering cultural shifts. This study explores the role of AI in reshaping organizational work practices and examines the resulting cultural transformation. Through a systematic literature review, this study synthesizes existing research to provide a comprehensive understanding of AI’s impact on organizational landscapes. A systematic literature review was conducted, analyzing peer-reviewed articles, books, and conference papers to identify key themes related to AI-driven changes in work practices, including automation, decision making, and employee roles. It also explores how these changes influence organizational culture, particularly shifts toward innovation, agility, and continuous learning, alongside challenges like resistance to change and ethical concerns. While AI adoption promises benefits such as enhanced efficiency, productivity, and innovation, it also presents significant challenges related to cultural alignment, employee resistance, ethical concerns, and leadership communication. Effective leadership, transparent communication, and investments in skills development emerge as pivotal strategies for overcoming these obstacles and ensuring successful AI implementation. The findings offer insights into the complex interplay between AI adoption and cultural transformation, highlighting gaps in the current research and suggesting directions for future studies. This study serves as a valuable resource for academics and practitioners seeking to understand the broader implications of AI on organizational structures and culture.

hot.title: Job demands-resources and conservation of resources theories: How do they help to explain employee well-being and future job design?
hot.abstract: This paper examines the Conservation of Resources (COR) theory and the Job Demands-Resources (JD-R) theory to understand and predict employee well-being and performance. COR theory suggests that individuals aim to acquire, protect, and maximize resources to reduce psychological distress and prevent burnout. JD-R theory posits that balancing job demands and resources affects employee well-being, behaviors, and performance. By exploring these theories together, the paper offers insights into supporting the workforce amid challenges like remote work and technological advancements. It highlights shared features and differences between the theories, unresolved issues, and research opportunities, such as operationalizing and testing COR theory and differentiating job demands and resources in JD-R theory. The paper concludes with predictions about future job design, emphasizing the need to balance job demands and resources to support employee well-being and performance, contributing to the literature by challenging and refining these theories.

hot.title: Sustainable Consumption and Branding for Gen Z: How Brand Dimensions Influence Consumer Behavior and Adoption of Newly Launched Technological Products
hot.abstract: Generation Z is emerging as a powerful force in shaping global consumer behavior, particularly in the market of digital and technological products. This study examines how specific branding dimensions, such as online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and brand knowledge, influence Gen Z’s purchase intention, emphasizing sustainable consumption. Sustainable consumption, in this context, refers to the preference for tech products that minimize the environmental impact through eco-friendly design, energy efficiency, and responsible sourcing. Using a quantitative approach, this cross-sectional research explores the effects of online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and knowledge on purchasing newly launched technological products that align with sustainability. Data were collected from a Gen Z sample using a combination of convenience and systematic sampling, and multiple regression analysis identified the most significant predictors of purchase intention. The results indicate that online brand experience, brand image, brand trust, and brand loyalty play the most crucial roles, having a greater effects on Gen Z’s purchase intention, while brand awareness and knowledge also contribute. However, brand engagement and behavioral intention have weaker effects. These findings suggest that brands targeting Gen Z should prioritize building a strong, trustworthy, and engaging online presence while highlighting their sustainability efforts, and when Gen Z consumers have favorable digital interactions with a brand, perceive its image positively, trust it, and feel loyal to it, they are more likely to consider purchasing its sustainable offerings. This study enhances the understandi

hot.title: The impact of artificial intelligence on organizational performance: The mediating role of employee productivity
hot.venue: Journal of Open Innovation Technology Market and Complexity
hot.abstract: The adoption of Artificial intelligence (AI) technology in the workplace is becoming more common, with several research highlighting both its positive and adverse influence on employee productivity (EP) and organizational performance (OP). Furthermore, there is a scarcity of research focused on the mediator role of EP in the nexus between AI and OP. This ambiguity underscores the need for a comprehensive understanding of how AI interacts with EP and OP within specific organizational contexts, such as Ethio Telecom. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate the impact of AI on OP with a mediating role of EP. Quantitative data was collected through an online survey using Kobo Toolbox from 172 purposively selected employees. AI was modeled as third-order formative construct, while EP and OP were first-order reflective constructs. The variables were measured using validated multi-item questionnaires with a 7-point Likert scale. The association between these variables was investigated with PLS-SEM in SMART PLS 4.1.03. The results showed that there were positive and significant relationships between AI and EP, AI and OP, EP and OP, and AI on OP through EP. Furthermore, EP served as a partial mediator between OP and AI. These findings are consistent with previous studies and theories, such as the resource-based view and human capital theories. The results suggest that organizations can dramatically improve performance in the digital age by implementing AI and creating a work environment that encourages productivity.

hot.title: The moderating role of personalized recommendations in the trust–satisfaction–loyalty relationship: an empirical study of AI-driven e-commerce
hot.abstract: Abstract Purpose This study investigates the effects of trust, satisfaction, and loyalty on AI-driven e-commerce, with a particular focus on how personalized recommendations moderate these relationships. It aims to explore how personalized AI features reshape consumer perceptions and decision-making. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research approach was used to collect data from a diverse group of e-commerce users who had interacted with AI-based recommendation systems. An online survey employing standardized scales for trust, satisfaction, loyalty, and personalization was administered, and data were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) to test the hypotheses. Findings The study reveals that trust has a significant positive influence on both satisfaction and loyalty. Personalization further strengthens these relationships by moderating the trust–satisfaction–loyalty dynamic. Satisfaction partially mediates the relationship between trust and loyalty, with the model’s explanatory power improving by 5% when personalization is included as a moderator. These results highlight the pivotal role of personalized recommendations in shaping consumer trust and satisfaction in AI-driven e-commerce. Practical implications Businesses can use personalized recommendation systems to enhance trust and satisfaction, thereby fostering loyalty. For example, platforms like Amazon and Netflix have successfully employed personalized AI algorithms to boost customer retention and engagement. Transparency features, such as explaining why certain products are recommended, and cultural sensitivity in algorithm design can further enhance customer trust and acceptance. e-commerce organizations should also invest in data privacy measures and clear algorithms to maintain consumer

hot.title: A Closer Look into Recent Video-based Learning Research: A Comprehensive Review of Video Characteristics, Tools, Technologies, and Learning Effectiveness
hot.venue: International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education
hot.abstract: People increasingly use videos on the Web for learning, be it for daily tasks in formal or informal educational settings. To enhance this type of learning, scientists are continuously conducting experiments, proposing guidelines, analyzing data, and researching artificial intelligence methods for tool development. In this comprehensive review, we analyze 257 articles (using PRISMA guidelines) on video-based learning from a technological perspective for the period from 2016 to 2021. One of the aims is to identify video characteristics that support learning as explored by previous research. Based on our analysis, we suggest a taxonomy that organizes the video characteristics and contextual aspects into eight categories: (1) audio features, (2) visual features, (3) textual features, (4) instructor behavior, (5) learners’ activities (play, pause, etc.), (6) interactive features (quizzes, etc.), (7) production style, and (8) instructional design. Also, we identify four representative methodological approaches: (1) tool support of video-based learning, (2) controlled experiments, (3) data analysis studies, and (4) design guidelines for learning videos. We find that the most explored characteristics are textual features followed by visual features, learners’ activities, and interactive features. Tools that aid learning through videos frequently utilize text from transcripts, video frames, and images. The learner’s activity is heavily explored through log files in data analysis studies, and interactive features are frequently scrutinized in controlled experiments. As further contributions, we contrast research findings on how video characteristics affect learning effectiveness, report on tasks and technologies used to develop tools, and summarize design guideline trends to prod

hot.title: Building trust in sustainable brands: Revisiting perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image
hot.abstract: This study revisits the key variables that build brand trust in consumers, addressing a critical issue for building lasting relationships between brands and consumers. Through a conceptual model, we examine how perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image influence consumer trust. The research is based on a sample of 1280 Spanish consumers over the age of 18, who responded to a questionnaire designed with previously validated scales. The PLS-SEM technique was used to validate the hypotheses and the proposed model. The findings reveal that perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image have a positive and significant effect on consumer trust. In particular, it was found that customer service directly influences customer satisfaction, which in turn reinforces brand trust. Additionally, the brand's communication strategy shows a significant positive relationship with brand image. Finally, customer satisfaction is identified as a mediating variable in the relationship between customer service and trust, indicating that a positive experience with customer service is fundamental for consolidating brand trust. This study contributes to enhancing the understanding of the factors that promote brand trust and offers practical implications for the development of effective marketing and brand management strategies. These insights can be especially relevant for sustainable brands, as the identified factors—perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image—are also critical in fostering trust in brands that prioritize sustainability. Incorporating sustainable practices into these areas may further strengthen consumer trust and loyalty toward sustainable brands.

hot.title: Leading in the Digital Age: The Role of Leadership in Organizational Digital Transformation
hot.abstract: In the modern digital age, organizations face unprecedented challenges and possibilities while managing the intricacies of digital transformation. Accelerated technological developments, changing customer preferences, heightened competition, and dynamic regulatory environments necessitate companies to synchronize their business goals with technological innovations. Leadership is crucial in steering businesses through changes, requiring a deep understanding of change processes and the capacity to adjust leadership accordingly. This research addresses the central question: How does leadership effectively promote organizational digital transformation? The study examines how leaders can effectively promote the adoption of advanced technologies and the promotion of innovation, by first exploring the nature of digital transformation within organizations and then analyzing the evolving dynamics of leadership in this context. An integrative review of the Web of Science (WoS) and Scopus databases was conducted, using the search terms: “Leadership” and “Digital Transformation”. The findings emphasize that effective leadership is crucial for managing the minutiae of digital transformation, integrating technology into organizational processes to facilitate learning, collaboration, and agility, enabling companies to adapt to market shifts, reduce uncertainty, and enhance decision-making for sustainable growth. By using the right tools and with the right frequency, leaders may develop team cohesion—even at a distance. Attentive digital-age leaders will know how to leverage the right mechanisms, and herein, we hope to give some indication of how that may be achieved, so that digital transformation increases rather than decreases team motivation levels.

hot.title: Why human–AI relationships need socioaffective alignment
hot.abstract: Humans strive to design safe AI systems that align with our goals and remain under our control. However, as AI capabilities advance, we face a new challenge: the emergence of deeper, more persistent relationships between humans and AI systems. We explore how increasingly capable AI agents may generate the perception of deeper relationships with users, especially as AI becomes more personalised and agentic. This shift, from transactional interaction to ongoing sustained social engagement with AI, necessitates a new focus on socioaffective alignment—how an AI system behaves within the social and psychological ecosystem co-created with its user, where preferences and perceptions evolve through mutual influence. Addressing these dynamics involves resolving key intrapersonal dilemmas, including balancing immediate versus long-term well-being, protecting autonomy, and managing AI companionship alongside the desire to preserve human social bonds. By framing these challenges through a notion of basic psychological needs, we seek AI systems that support, rather than exploit, our fundamental nature as social and emotional beings.

hot.title: Greenwashing prevention in environmental, social, and governance (ESG) disclosures: A bibliometric analysis
hot.venue: Research in International Business and Finance
hot.abstract: The accuracy and reliability of environmental, social, and governance (hereafter ESG) reporting are threatened by the presence of greenwashing which affects the quality of disclosure, complicates the decision-making process, adversely influences financial markets, and affects stakeholders’ trust in disclosed information. This study examines the academic literature on ESG disclosure and greenwashing prevention through a bibliometric analysis and systematic literature review. Our findings show that greenwashing is a complex phenomenon characterised by various forms, shapes, and levels, making it challenging to detect, measure, and develop prevention tools. The results show a growing trend in the academic literature on greenwashing with a strong focus on the establishment of greenwashing detection measures and the need for the creation of greenwashing prevention tools to ensure the reliability, comparability, and quality of corporate sustainability reporting. Understanding the challenges of greenwashing in ESG disclosures and the efforts toward greenwashing prevention carries significant implications for regulators and standard-setters, supervisory bodies, professional organizations, companies, researchers, and other stakeholders, especially in light of recent regulatory developments around the globe and the new forms and levels of greenwashing evolving in scientific research. • Greenwashing prevention in ESG disclosures analysed through a bibliometric analysis. • Performance, network, and systematic literature review analysis methods applied. • Greenwashing measurement is difficult as it has lots of levels, forms, and shades. • Greenwashing measurement methods at various greenwashing levels are systemized. • The creation of a credible greenwashing prevention tool in ESG d

hot.title: AI and employee wellbeing in the workplace: An empirical study
hot.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in workplace settings significantly affects employees, particularly their wellbeing. Despite its growing relevance, the impact of AI on employee wellbeing remains underexplored. To address this gap, we conducted a survey and employed structural equation modeling to analyze data from Finnish and international companies headquartered in Finland (n = 207). We found that AI adoption does not directly impact employee wellbeing but indirectly influences it through work-related factors of task optimization and safety. This highlights the importance of strategically implementing AI to enhance aspects of work that are important to employees, thereby maximizing the wellbeing benefits of AI adoption. Practically, this study underscores the need for AI adoption to result in tangible improvements in organizational tasks and processes, data security, and occupational health. When these aspects are adequately addressed, AI adoption can enhance employee wellbeing and contribute to improved human-AI integration in the workplace.

hot.title: The Typing Cure: Experiences with Large Language Model Chatbots for Mental Health Support
hot.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction
hot.abstract: People experiencing severe distress increasingly use Large Language Model (LLM) chatbots as mental health support tools. Discussions on social media have described how engagements were lifesaving for some, but evidence suggests that general-purpose LLM chatbots also have notable risks that could endanger the welfare of users if not designed responsibly. In this study, we investigate the lived experiences of people who have used LLM chatbots for mental health support. We build on interviews with 21 individuals from globally diverse backgrounds to analyze how users create unique support roles for their chatbots, fill in gaps in everyday care, and navigate associated cultural limitations when seeking support from chatbots. We ground our analysis in psychotherapy literature around effective support, and introduce the concept of therapeutic alignment, or aligning AI with therapeutic values for mental health contexts. Our study offers recommendations for how designers can approach the ethical and effective use of LLM chatbots and other AI mental health support tools in mental health care.

hot.title: Confronting and alleviating AI resistance in the workplace: An integrative review and a process framework
hot.abstract: This study involves an integrative literature review and a process framework explaining the mechanisms to confront and alleviate employee Artificial intelligence (AI) resistance in organizations. First, we conceptualize AI resistance as a three-dimensional concept embodied in employees' fears, inefficacies, and antipathies toward AI. We advance that experiencing mistrust, existential questioning, and technological reflection are key individual mechanisms to confronting AI resistance connected to organizational mechanisms to alleviate AI resistance through the continuous interaction and unfolding of anxiety and introspection. We also explain the alleviation of AI resistance as an organizational process consisting of AI accessibility, human-AI augmentation, and AI-technology legitimation, each of which maps into one of the dimensions in the employee-level confrontation mechanisms. Overall, our conceptual framework provides an overarching and granular understanding of AI resistance, how employees confront it, and how it can be alleviated in the workplace. • Develops a process framework explaining the mechanisms to confront and alleviate employee AI resistance. • AI resistance as a three-dimensional concept embodied in employees' fears, inefficacies, and antipathies toward AI. • Highlights mistrust, existential questioning, and technological reflection as key individual concerns • AI resistance is alleviated through AI accessibility, human-AI augmentation, and AI-technology legitimation.

hot.title: Gamification in education and training: A literature review
hot.abstract: Abstract Gamification, when properly implemented in education and training, can increase the engagement and motivation of learners and inspire them to change aspects of their behaviour to support learning. Although the use of gamification in the learning process might have a positive impact, its potential to strengthen education and training has not yet been confirmed. The descriptive literature review presented in this article synthesises studies and findings on the use of gamification in the education and training context. The authors used the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) model to select and analyse 46 publications from six bibliographic databases. They investigated the gamification theories, frameworks, models, elements and mechanics that can support learning. In addition, research was conducted to identify constraints, challenges and organisational impediments that may arise in gamified education and training programmes, to answer the question of how gamification can be implemented to achieve better learning outcomes. Findings show that further studies need to be conducted into this evolving learning approach. Overall, gamification is most likely to be effective when instructional design principles are used to ensure training content meets learners’ needs and expectations.

hot.title: Insights from the Job Demands–Resources Model: AI's dual impact on employees’ work and life well-being
hot.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has rapidly integrated into organizational workflows, sparking two debates: proponents argue that it increases productivity and decreases workloads, whereas opponents warn that it induces technostress (e.g., job replacement) and decreases employees' well-being. However, AI adoption by employees remains understudied, requiring both theoretical and empirical investigation to assess its positive and negative effects. This study employs the job demands–resources (JD–R) model as a guiding framework to examine the impact of AI demands (i.e., technostress) and resources (i.e., efficacy and generative AI) on employees' work and life domains (i.e., productivity, job satisfaction, and work–family conflict), with engagement and exhaustion as mediating factors. Data gathering through a three-wave survey involved 600 gender-balanced participants working with AI across diverse industries. Bayesian SEM results indicate that both AI efficacy and generative AI positively impact productivity, with AI efficacy also enhancing engagement and job satisfaction. In contrast, AI technostress increases exhaustion, exacerbates work–family conflict, and lowers job satisfaction, even though it may still contribute to productivity. These findings highlight the dual impact of AI on employees: AI technostress impairs well-being, while AI efficacy enhances it. Notably, generative AI mitigates the negative effects of technostress, a benefit not observed for AI efficacy as measured in this study. Overall, this study provides an empirical basis for understanding the resources and demands associated with AI adoption and its impact on employees' psychological processes, influencing both their work and life domains and leading to diverse outcomes. • This study explores how AI at
