The Global Flourishing Study: Study Profile and Initial Results on Flourishing
hot.abstract: The Global Flourishing Study is a longitudinal panel study of over 200,000 participants in 22 geographically and culturally diverse countries, spanning all six populated continents, with nationally representative sampling and intended annual survey data collection for 5 years to assess numerous aspects of flourishing and its possible determinants. The study is intended to expand our knowledge of the distribution and determinants of flourishing around the world. Relations between a composite flourishing index and numerous demographic characteristics are reported. Participants were also surveyed about their childhood experiences, which were analyzed to determine their associations with subsequent adult flourishing. Analyses are presented both across and within countries, and discussion is given as to how the demographic and childhood relationships vary by country and which patterns appear to be universal versus culturally specific. Brief comment is also given on the results of a whole series of papers in the Global Flourishing Study Special Collection, employing similar analyses, but with more-specific aspects of well-being. The Global Flourishing Study expands our knowledge of the distribution and determinants of well-being and provides foundational knowledge for the promotion of societal flourishing.

hot.title: Global, regional, and national burden of suicide, 1990–2021: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2021
hot.abstract: BACKGROUND: Deaths from suicide are a tragic yet preventable cause of mortality. Quantifying the burden of suicide to understand its geographical distribution, temporal trends, and variation by age and sex is an essential step in suicide prevention. We aimed to present a comprehensive set of global, regional, and national estimates of suicide burden. METHODS: We produced estimates of the number of deaths and age-standardised mortality rates of suicide globally, regionally, and for 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2021, and disaggregated these results by age and sex. The Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study (GBD) 2021 estimates of deaths attributable to suicide were broken down into two comprehensive categories: those by firearms and those by other specified means. For this analysis, we also produced estimates of mean age at the time of death from suicide, incidence of suicide attempts compared with deaths, and age-standardised rates of suicide by firearm. We acquired data from vital registration, verbal autopsy, and mortality surveillance that included 23 782 study-location-years of data from GBD 2021. Point estimates were calculated from the average of 1000 randomly selected possible values of deaths from suicide by age, sex, and geographical location. 95% uncertainty intervals (UIs) were derived from the 2·5th and 97·5th percentiles from a 1000-draw distribution. FINDINGS: Globally, 746 000 deaths (95% UI 692 000-800 000) from suicide occurred in 2021, including 519 000 deaths (485 000-556 000) among males and 227 000 (200 000-255 000) among females. hot.title: Collaborative AI in the workplace: Enhancing organizational performance through resource-based and task-technology fit perspectives
hot.abstract: This research examines how artificial intelligence, human capabilities, and task types influence organizational outcomes. By leveraging the frameworks of the Resource-Based View and Task Technology Fit theories, we executed two distinct studies to assess the effectiveness of a generative AI tool in aiding task performance across a spectrum of task complexities and creative demands. The initial study tested the utility of generative AI across diverse tasks and the significance of AI-related skills enhancement. The subsequent study explored interactions between humans and AI, analyzing emotional tone, sentence structure, and word choice. Our results indicate that incorporating AI can significantly improve organizational task performance in areas such as automation, support, creative endeavors, and innovation processes. We also observed that generative AI generally presents more positive sentiment, utilizes simpler language, and has a narrower vocabulary than human counterparts. These insights contribute to a broader understanding of AI's strengths and weaknesses in organizational settings and guide the strategic implementation of AI systems. • Firms can utilize AI to gain competitive advantages. • Firms can deploy AI to automate routine tasks and enhance decision support tasks. • Firms should focus on AI and human collaboration to boost creative and innovative tasks. • Firms benefit when employees upskill to improve performance with AI. • Generative AI tool in our study had a more positive sentiment and used simpler language than humans.

hot.title: The impacts of companion AI on human relationships: risks, benefits, and design considerations
hot.abstract: AI applications intended for companionship have increased in both availability and capabilities in recent years, alongside a spike in loneliness (Johnson 2023 ; Murthy 2023 ). According to a 2024 analysis by venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz, companion AI makes up 16 of the top 100 AI apps based on web traffic and monthly active users (Moore 2024 ). Moreover, today’s AI applications have a greater command of human language, an increasing capacity for storing memories, and more varied modalities to support an increasing diversity of experiences, a known driver in the development and deepening of emotional relationships (Skjuve et al. 2022 ).

hot.title: Organizational culture, digital transformation, and product innovation
hot.abstract: This research fills a knowledge gap by introducing a new conceptualization of digital transformation through a multidimensional digital transforming capability. It further examines the influence of four cultural types on this capability and its subsequent impact on product innovation . Empirical findings reveal that adhocracy, followed in descending order of influence by clan, market, and hierarchy cultures, is positively related to digital transforming capability, which in turn is positively related to product innovation in terms of new product newness, meaningfulness, and performance. Additionally, new product newness and meaningfulness each positively mediate the effect of digital transforming capability on new product performance.

hot.title: Supply Chain Resilience: A Critical Review of Risk Mitigation, Robust Optimisation, and Technological Solutions and Future Research Directions
hot.venue: Global Journal of Flexible Systems Management
hot.abstract: Abstract This study systematically evaluates the literature of supply chain resilience by integrating bibliometric and network analysis techniques. This analysis is conducted following the dynamic capability, as a theoretical lens, to understand and analyse supply chain resilience. We extracted and curated 294 peer‐reviewed articles from leading academic databases, Web of Science and Scopus, covering the period from January 2000 to 2024. We applied two complementary network analysis methods, a keyword co‐occurrence network (KCON) to analyse the frequency and interrelationships among key terms, and a research focus parallelship network (RFPN) to map the connectivity among research streams. These analytical approaches revealed three distinct research clusters, optimisation for supply chain resilience, technology adoption for supply chain resilience, and resilience strategies against disruptions and risk management. By linking emerging trends in digital transformation with traditional risk management practices, this study offers a new perspective for both academic inquiry and managerial practice. Practically, integrating digital technologies, especially digital twin and machine learning, into risk management processes offers a strategic roadmap for real-time monitoring and decision-making in supply chain resilience. Furthermore, this study identifies significant research gaps, including an exploration of micro‐level dynamics within organisations, and the development of advanced simulation techniques and robust approaches to manage uncertainties.

hot.title: Generative AI and its Transformative Value for Digital Platforms
hot.abstract: The emergence of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) represents a watershed moment in the evolution of digital platforms. The capabilities of this AI technology go beyond traditional AI systems, enabling the autonomous generation of novel outcomes with significant implications for platform value creation, architecture, governance, and stakeholder interactions. We develop an integrative conceptual framework that identifies four key mechanisms through which GenAI transforms digital platforms: intelligent automation, democratization, hyper-personalization, and collaborative innovation. Through intelligent automation, GenAI transforms boundary resources from passive interfaces into active, intelligent mediators of value creation. Democratization systematically lowers barriers to platform participation. Hyper-personalization enables dynamic, individual-level adaptation of platform content. Collaborative innovation transforms platform innovation by making GenAI an active participant in human-AI value co-creation. We use this framework to situate the papers in the special issue and develop a research agenda that explores the transformative impact of GenAI on platform stakeholder relationships.

hot.title: Lower Artificial Intelligence Literacy Predicts Greater AI Receptivity
hot.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) transforms society, understanding factors that influence AI receptivity is increasingly important. The current research investigates which types of consumers have greater AI receptivity. Contrary to expectations revealed in four surveys, cross-country data and six additional studies find that people with lower AI literacy are typically more receptive to AI. This lower literacy–greater receptivity link is not explained by differences in perceptions of AI's capability, ethicality, or feared impact on humanity. Instead, this link occurs because people with lower AI literacy are more likely to perceive AI as magical and experience feelings of awe in the face of AI's execution of tasks that seem to require uniquely human attributes. In line with this theorizing, the lower literacy–higher receptivity link is mediated by perceptions of AI as magical and is moderated among tasks not assumed to require distinctly human attributes. These findings suggest that companies may benefit from shifting their marketing efforts and product development toward consumers with lower AI literacy. In addition, efforts to demystify AI may inadvertently reduce its appeal.

hot.title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption for Sustainable Growth in SMEs : An Extended Dynamic Capability Framework
hot.venue: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
hot.abstract: ABSTRACT The adoption of Artificial Intelligence is transforming enterprises worldwide, influencing various aspects of business operations and affecting all dimensions of the triple bottom line. Companies ready to leverage the potential of this technology can significantly improve their performance. Therefore, it is crucial to understand the relationship between internal capabilities and contextual factors on one hand, and Artificial Intelligence adoption and its impact on performance on the other. Within this research framework, this study introduces an extended dynamic capability framework to analyze the interplay between internal factors, Artificial Intelligence adoption, and companies performance. The proposed model is tested using Partial Least Squares—Structural Equation Modeling on survey data from 210 Italian innovative startups. The findings indicate that companies with well‐developed dynamic capabilities, enabling them to adapt more effectively to environmental changes, are also better equipped to adopt Artificial Intelligence, leading to positive social, economic, and environmental performance.

hot.title: Unveiling triple bottom line's influence on business performance
hot.abstract: Addressing environmental, social, and economic challenges has become a pressing global priority. The Triple Bottom Line (TBL) framework offers a holistic approach for evaluating corporate performance by integrating economic, environmental, and social perspectives. Despite its increasing adoption in both managerial and academic research, there remains a significant gap in understanding how the TBL framework influences business performance. To address this, the study conducts a bibliometric review of 207 publications from the Web of Science database. The review highlights the multifaceted impact of practices linked to the TBL dimensions on business performance while introducing the TBL Influence on Business Performance model. This model provides valuable insights into how businesses can effectively apply TBL principles to address socio-environmental challenges, foster innovation, and achieve sustained long-term performance. The findings contribute valuable theoretical and practical insights into how organizations can utilize TBL principles to strengthen resilience, innovation, and performance in the face of global socio-environmental challenges.

hot.title: Can Generative AI Chatbots Emulate Human Connection? A Relationship Science Perspective
hot.abstract: The development of generative artificial intelligence capable of sustaining complex conversations has created a burgeoning market for companion chatbots promising social and emotional connection. The appeal of these products raises questions about whether chatbots can fulfill the functions of close relationships. Proponents argue that relationships with chatbots can be as meaningful as relationships between humans, whereas critics argue they are a dangerous distraction from genuine connections. This analysis applies theoretical tools from more than 50 years of research on close relationships to evaluate the extent to which human-chatbot interactions meet the definition of and fulfill the functions of close relationships. Interactions between humans and chatbots do possess some characteristic features of close relationships: Humans and chatbots can influence each other and engage in frequent and diverse conversations over time. Chatbots can be responsive in ways humans perceive as supportive, generating feelings of connection and opportunities for growth. Yet because chatbots make only superficial requests of their users, relationships with them cannot provide the benefits of negotiating with and sacrificing for a partner and may reinforce undesirable behaviors. Research that attends to the characteristics of users, chatbots, and their interactions will be crucial for identifying for whom these relationships will be beneficial or harmful.

hot.title: Artificial intelligence technologies and entrepreneurship: a hybrid literature review
hot.abstract: The disruptive potential of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies involves creating new entrepreneurial opportunities and reshaping the entrepreneurial process. The impact of AI technologies on entrepreneurial activity is also reflected in an explosive level of research interest, leading to the fragmentation of existing studies. This phenomenon makes generating a comprehensive and systematic overview challenging. This paper reviews the existing research on the application of AI-based technologies in entrepreneurial practice. Specifically, it conducts a hybrid literature review, analyzing 345 articles from peer-reviewed journals. It identifies the main contributions to the field; the conceptual, social, and intellectual structures; and the leading themes addressed to date. Despite growing interest in the field, this study concludes that most academic research on the subject has been superficial. This study proposes future lines of research based on the antecedents, decisions, and outcomes (ADO) and the theories, contexts, and methods (TCM) frameworks.

hot.title: What you see is not what you get: ESG scores and greenwashing risk
hot.abstract: This paper shows that ESG scores capture a company’s greenwashing behavior. Greenwashing accusations are most prevalent among large companies with high ESG scores. We empirically employ a novel theoretical model that distinguishes between the communication of a company’s environmental efforts (apparent environmental performance) and its actual environmental impact (real environmental performance). The correlation of the apparent (real) environmental performance with ESG scores is significantly positive (negative). Therefore, ESG scores are unsuitable for measuring real environmental impact. Thus, investors focusing on high ESG-rated companies may unknowingly increase their greenwashing risk exposure, and academics may use misleading information to assess greenwashing risk. • ESG scores are positively correlated with greenwashing cases. • ESG scores mainly measure the apparent rather than the real environmental performance. • Higher analyst coverage limits the exaggeration of apparent environmental performance.

hot.title: Third-party evaluators perceive AI as more compassionate than expert humans
hot.abstract: Empathy connects us but strains under demanding settings. This study explored how third parties evaluated AI-generated empathetic responses versus human responses in terms of compassion, responsiveness, and overall preference across four preregistered experiments. Participants (N = 556) read empathy prompts describing valenced personal experiences and compared the AI responses to select non-expert or expert humans. Results revealed that AI responses were preferred and rated as more compassionate compared to select human responders (Study 1). This pattern of results remained when author identity was made transparent (Study 2), when AI was compared to expert crisis responders (Study 3), and when author identity was disclosed to all participants (Study 4). Third parties perceived AI as being more responsive-conveying understanding, validation, and care-which partially explained AI's higher compassion ratings in Study 4. These findings suggest that AI has robust utility in contexts requiring empathetic interaction, with the potential to address the increasing need for empathy in supportive communication contexts.

hot.title: Sustainability or Greenwashing: Evidence from the Asset Market for Industrial Pollution
hot.abstract: ABSTRACT We study the asset market for pollutive plants. Firms divest pollutive plants in response to environmental pressures. Buyers are firms facing weaker environmental pressures that have supply chain relationships or joint ventures with the sellers. While pollution levels do not decline following divestitures, sellers highlight their sustainable policies in subsequent conference calls, earn higher returns as they sell more pollutive plants, and benefit from higher Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) ratings and lower compliance costs. Overall, the asset market allows firms to redraw their boundaries in a manner perceived as environmentally friendly without real consequences for pollution but with substantial gains from trade.

hot.title: Mapping the greenwashing research landscape: a theoretical and field analysis
hot.abstract: Abstract This study provides a comprehensive overview of greenwashing research in business and management, focusing on its conceptual and theoretical foundations. Through a systematic literature review of 97 peer-reviewed articles from Scopus and Web of Science, we use bibliometric analysis to map the evolution of greenwashing studies and network analysis and identify four thematic clusters: (1) symbolic management and CSR communication, (2) environmental regulations and institutional complexity, (3) performance and sustainable practices, and (4) marketing, perception, and trust. Additionally, we perform a full-text analysis to map the theoretical frameworks employed across these clusters, revealing the dominance of macro-level theories (e.g., legitimacy, institutional, and stakeholder theories) and their cross-level interactions with meso- and micro-level approaches. By developing a multi-level theoretical framework, we provide a structured approach to understanding greenwashing across different analytical layers. Then, focusing on the theories used to investigate greenwashing, we identify some avenues for future research. This study has practical implications for understanding how greenwashing affects corporate governance, financial performance, and stakeholder trust, providing insights for enhancing transparency and accountability in sustainable business practices.

hot.title: The past, present, and future of sustainability marketing: How did we get here and where might we go?
hot.abstract: The ever-increasing concerns about global sustainability have sparked intense debates and actions across various sectors, with marketing playing a pivotal role in influencing both the problem and potential solutions. This article maps the historical trajectory of sustainability marketing, analyzes current trends, and explores future directions to enhance sustainability within marketing practice. We show that sustainability marketing has historically centered on resource conservation and green marketing , but in recent years its scope has expanded to encompass a broader range of topics. These include the circular economy , anti-consumption, regulatory frameworks, innovation, carbon emissions , as well as the social and ethical considerations inherent in sustainability marketing. We propose three main areas within which sustainability marketing might expand in the future: system-driven changes, business-driven changes, and consumer-driven changes. Our analysis aims to deepen the understanding of sustainability marketing and inspire marketers to explore questions and solutions that will contribute to a sustainable future.

hot.title: Are lonely youngsters turning to chatbots for companionship? The relationship between chatbot usage and social connectedness in Danish high-school students
hot.abstract: • 2.44 % of Danish high-school students engage in mutual participative conversations or seek emotional support from chatbots. • Students who engage in such interactions with chatbots are lonelier than their peers. • Students seem to be using chatbots to cope with negative feelings. Are lonely youngsters turning to chatbots to fill their social needs? The present research contributes to the ongoing scientific endeavors to understand the adoption of chatbots as social companions. Specifically, we examined how many Danish high-school students engage in friend-like conversations with chatbots, why they engage in such conversations, and whether this trend is associated with the sense of social connectedness (operationalized as loneliness and perceived social support). In pursuing this goal, a preregistered mixed-methods cross-sectional survey study was carried out. A total sample of 1599 students from 15 Danish high schools was collected. In total, 234 students (14.6 %) responded that they engaged in friend-like conversations with chatbots. Qualitative thematic analyses of free-text responses revealed two dominant ways of engaging with chatbots: utilitarian conversations ( n = 174) and social-supportive conversations ( n = 39). A major finding was that social-supportive chatbot users reported significantly more loneliness than non-chatbot users ( d = 0.53) and utilitarian chatbot users ( d = 0.52). Furthermore, social-supportive chatbot users also reported significantly less perceived social support than non-chatbot users ( d = −0.46). Analyses also showed significant associations between higher loneliness and less perceived social support and various situational triggers for initiating conversations with chatbots, including bad mood, a need for self-disclosure, and a sense

latest.title: Promosi Melalui Implementasi Tiktok Ads untuk Meningkatkan Engagement Dasilva Batik Malang
latest.abstract: Dasilva Batik Malang is an MSME producing modern batik clothing whose TikTok engagement has declined due to inconsistent digital promotion and unused TikTok Ads potential. This research identifies TikTok Ads implementation as a digital promotion strategy, analyzes engagement differences among entertainment, storytelling, and promotional content, and determines the most effective content type, and identifies the obstacles encountered. The research applies the Kemmis and MeTaggart action research model through planning, action, observation, and reflection. The unit of analysis comprises 20 people: the business owner, marketing experts, computer experts, and prospective consumers selected purposively. The EPIC Model questionnaire was tested for validity using Pearson Product Moment correlation and reliability using Cronbach's Alpha via IBM SPSS Statistics 26. The EPIC Rate assessment showed all three contents were effective, with promotional content scoring highest (4.16). However, the actual engagement rate after publication via TikTok Ads showed entertainment content performed best (1.99%), followed by promotional (1.68%) and storytelling content (1.63%). Dasilva Batik Malang is advised to produce-more entertainment content without abandoning promotional and storytelling content, while future research should apply A/B Testing, add content variations, and increase the promotion budget for more representative results.

latest.title: Between Play and Pressure: Pop Mart's 'Labubu' Craze, Blind-Box Consumption, and Emotional Socialization Among Primary School Students in Beijing
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: This study investigated the psychological, consumerist, and educational intersections of Pop Mart’s ‘Labubu’ craze, analyzing how blind-box retail mechanisms impact peer dynamics and emotional socialization among primary school students in Beijing. Employing a comprehensive desk-based methodology that synthesized verified qualitative and quantitative secondary sources including municipal consumer protection reports, corporate market filings, and primary empirical school-district surveys the research examined the structural drivers of juvenile collectible consumption. Findings revealed that the algorithmic gamification of blind boxes intensifies status anxiety and peer-group stratification, compelling young learners to utilize scarce ‘secret edition’ figures as compensatory social currency. Concurrently, children internalize retail unboxing as a surrogate coping mechanism against rigorous academic pressures characteristic of Beijing’s primary education system. While informal peer trading networks fostered localized negotiation and community building, unmanaged commercial consumption precipitated compulsive spending habits and amplified classroom socio-economic divides. These insights illustrate the pressing necessity for cross-institutional regulatory oversight, school-based critical media literacy curricula, and parental financial guidance frameworks within contemporary urban educational ecosystems.

latest.title: AI-Assisted Negotiation Training: A Quasi-Experimental Examination of Buyers’ and Sellers’ Perceived Negotiation Performance in a Used-Car Sales Simulation
latest.abstract: Background: Evidence on artificial intelligence (AI) as a preparatory learning aid for novice human negotiators remains limited in consumer negotiation simulations. Existing work emphasizes automated agents rather than students preparing to negotiate. Against this backdrop, the present study examined changes in students’ perceived negotiation performance, differences in those changes between buyer and seller roles, and the purposes for which students used AI during a simulated used-car sale. The outcome was perceived performance, not economic results. Methodology: A single-group, repeated-measures quasi-experiment involved 74 undergraduate business students enrolled in a negotiation course at a university in Bangkok, Thailand. Thirty-seven students served as buyers and 37 as sellers. Participants completed two negotiations outside regular class hours within a 24–48-hour period, retaining their assigned roles and using the same scenario. The first round was conducted without AI assistance. Before the second round, students spent approximately five minutes preparing with generative AI tools of their choice for information analysis, strategy planning, role-play, or feedback. Each negotiation lasted approximately five to seven minutes. Perceived negotiation performance was assessed using five-item self-report scales in each condition. Paired-samples t-tests and a mixed-design analysis of variance (ANOVA) examined differences between conditions and across roles. Reported purposes of AI use were summarized descriptively. Results: Students reported higher perceived negotiation performance after AI-assisted preparation (M = 4.45, SD = 0.42) than after the preceding non-AI round (M = 3.78, SD = 0.58). The mean difference was 0.67 points, t(73) = −9.23, p < .001, with a large sta
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Can media use reduce procrastination? The effect of inspiring media content on academic motivation
latest.abstract: In contrast to the distracting effects digital media use poses to attention and productivity, this study examines whether prescribing small doses of inspiring and comedic media content can mitigate procrastination by evoking the emotions of hope and amusement, respectively. In this five-wave panel pretest-posttest experimental design conducted over the course of 4 weeks, undergraduate students, who generally are known to be heavy media users and prone to procrastination, were randomly assigned to one of four groups, including two video treatments (comedic and inspirational), a social media condition, or a no-media control condition ( N = 252 enrolled; N = 241 eligible for analysis). Participants reported their level of school-related stress, academic motivation and procrastination both during and after the five-day media intervention. Results indicated that comedic media and social media significantly increased amusement during the intervention week, which predicted increased procrastination in the following week. In contrast, a detrimental effect was not observed in the inspiring media group. In fact, there was a significant indirect effect of inspiring media on reducing procrastination through increases in felt hope and motivation. This study contributes to the growing body of media use and procrastination literature and demonstrates that the emotional nature of media content can be harnessed for positive outcomes.

latest.title: Exploring the value perceptions of young Indian luxury consumers towards inconspicuous luxury apparel consumption: evidence from homegrown brands
latest.abstract: Purpose With the mass-market proliferation of luxury and the evolving value orientation of millennial Indians, who embrace individualism while remaining part of a larger social framework, a bent towards subtle luxury has been observed. The study seeks to understand the value perceptions of young Indian consumers regarding the consumption of inconspicuous luxury apparel. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from respondents living in Delhi using purposive sampling (judgemental and snowball), resulting in a total of 326 respondents. Findings The study stipulates that different values, including Individual value, Functional value, Emotional value, Epistemic value and Social value, positively affect the perceptions of contemporary Indian luxury consumers towards inconspicuous luxury apparel choices. Originality/value With the rapidly evolving tastes of contemporary luxury consumers shifting towards high-quality fashion that is more personal than social, the phenomenon of inconspicuous fashion luxury is gaining traction. This holds particular relevance in an emerging economy like India, which in the past favoured the conspicuous display of material wealth through flashy apparel. By applying the theory of consumption values, this study attempts to explore the value perceptions of Indian consumers towards the consumption of inconspicuous luxury apparel. In doing so, it contributes significantly towards the limited understanding of inconspicuous luxury.

latest.title: Tourism Development and Rural Income Growth: A Micro-Macro Dual Perspective
latest.abstract: This study examines whether household income gains from tourism aggregate into regional growth. Drawing on structural transformation theory and Stolper–Samuelson factor-price logic, it treats tourism as a sector-specific demand shock. A time-varying difference-in-differences design applied to China Family Panel Studies data (2012–2022) estimates the household-level effect of the National Rural Tourism Demonstration County policy, while spatial panel models on provincial data (2011–2023) account for province-specific trajectories and exposure to the National Rural Revitalization Strategy. Tourism raises rural household income and is positively associated with provincial rural income. The regional relationship is predominantly spatially indirect; only wage income shows a significant positive local association. Human capital and consumer-market development strengthen the tourism–wage relationship, but bootstrap tests find no evidence that employment reallocation mediates it. Evidence for an income channel, therefore, does not establish the employment reallocation mechanism. Tourism strategies should pair destination promotion with workforce development and interprovincial coordination.

latest.title: IMPACT OF BUYER BEHAVIOUR AND BRAND LOYALTY ON BRAND PREFERENCE OF CHOCOLATES (A STUDY ON CONSUMER’S PERCEPTION IN CHENNAI CITY)
latest.venue: RCHUB JOURNAL OF CONTEMPORARY TRENDS IN MANAGEMENT COMMERCE AND ECONOMICS (JCMCE)
latest.abstract: Chocolate is consumed by several people all over the world. Chocolate is made out of cocoa which brings delight to its consumers. Consumer’s buying behaviour has drawn an impact on designing marketing strategies to create brand preference. Several brands available in the market are laying attention on the consumers to reap the benefits of repeat sales that increases brand loyalty of customers. Brand preference denotes the brand that is preferred under expectations of equality in price and availability. The main aim of this study is to understand the consumer’s perception, buyer behaviour, brand loyalty and brand preference towards chocolates. Data had been collected with the help of structured questionnaire which comprised of two parts. Part I dealt with demographic profile of the respondents and part II dealt with the perception of consumers relating to buyer behaviour, brand loyalty and brand preference as regards chocolates. Questionnaire was circulated among 100 respondents in the city of Chennai. Simple percentage analysis was used to find out the demographic profile and perception of the respondents. Chi-Square test was used to find out the association between the occupation and the brand loyalty of consumers with respect to chocolates. Factor Analysis revealed that the major factors influencing brand preference were brand awareness, brand appearance, emotional attachment and brand experience

latest.title: PENGUATAN HALAL SUPPLY CHAIN MELALUI SERTIFIKASI HALAL USAHA JASA PENGGILINGAN DAGING DI KABUPATEN BANGKALAN
latest.abstract: This research is motivated by the suboptimal implementation of halal assurance in meat-grinding service businesses, while the halal certification obligation for micro and small enterprises is moving toward enforcement. The study was conducted at four meat-grinding service businesses in Bangkalan Regency, East Java: Toko Barokah (Labang District), Toko Loros Mai Surya Daging and Toko Penggilingan Ali (Kamal District), and Toko UD Hasti (Bangkalan District). The problems faced were related to not having a halal certificate and the limited knowledge of business owners regarding halal certification procedures. This research aims to analyze the implementation of the halal supply chain and the role of halal certification in strengthening halal assurance in these four businesses. A qualitative method with a descriptive-analytical approach was employed, with data collected through interviews, observations, and documentation, and analyzed through data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing. The findings at Toko Loros Mai Surya Daging indicate that the business has already implemented several practices that support halal supply chain principles, such as verifying the source of the meat, washing ingredients with clean water, maintaining the cleanliness of machinery, using specific additives (flour and seasonings), and segregating customer orders. Nevertheless, the business lacks a halal certificate, which would serve as formal proof of its halal assurance. Key obstacles include a lack of understanding regarding certification procedures, as well as concerns about associated costs and taxes. On the other hand, the owner recognizes that halal certification has the potential to increase consumer trust. Similar practices were found at Toko Barokah, Toko Penggilingan Ali, and T

latest.title: How awe promotes minimalist consumption: the serial mediation of self-transcendence and authentic-self pursuit
latest.venue: Asia Pacific Journal of Marketing and Logistics
latest.abstract: Purpose This research aims to examine awe as a critical emotional precursor that drives minimalist consumption behaviors. By integrating compensatory control theory, this study constructs a theoretical linkage between awe and minimalist consumption, with self-transcendence and authentic-self pursuit constituting a serial mediation mechanism. Furthermore, drawing on risk aversion theory, this research posits that power distance belief moderates the predictive effect of self-transcendence and authentic-self pursuit on minimalist consumption. Design/methodology/approach Three scenario-based experiments were conducted to provide rigorous empirical evidence for the proposed theoretical framework. A total of 632 Chinese participants were recruited, yielding 546 valid samples for data analysis. The study employed ANOVA and the PROCESS program for data analysis. Findings The results indicate that awe exerted a significant facilitating effect on minimalist consumption, with individuals experiencing awe demonstrating a higher willingness to engage in minimalist consumption compared to those in non-awe conditions; self-transcendence and authentic-self pursuit play a serial mediating role in this process, but this mediating mechanism is moderated by power distance belief. Practical implications The present findings offer meaningful practical implications for brand strategy and consumer education. For brands positioning themselves around minimalist aesthetics, ethical consumption, or intentional living, evoking awe represents a powerful, emotion-driven lever to shape consumer preferences. Originality/value First, it expands the emotional antecedent framework of minimalist consumption by establishing awe as a critical self-transcendent emotion driving minimalist consumption. Second,

latest.title: Towards Sufficiency in Consumer Electronics? Consumers’ Perceptions of Longevity Strategies for Postponing Product Replacement
latest.abstract: The circular economy highlights the need to slow resource use by making products last longer. Although various longevity strategies have been proposed, it remains unclear whether consumers perceive these strategies as effective. This paper draws on literature on lifetime extension strategies and behavioural theories to investigate the extent to which consumers perceive these strategies as effective in postponing replacement. A survey of 617 consumers examined the perceived effectiveness of 13 product lifetime extension strategies across four product categories using ANOVAs. Durability and reliability emerged as the strategies perceived to be most effective. Preventing functional problems during product use is particularly important for postponing product replacement, as such problems appear to be prominent triggers for replacement. However, consumers remain unconvinced about the effectiveness of most other strategies. Correlational analyses revealed that satisfaction with lifetimes is negatively correlated with perceived strategy effectiveness, suggesting that consumers are less likely to search for lifetime-extending strategies as they do not see lifetime as a concern. These findings underscore the need for design/policy interventions to strengthen durability and enhance awareness of lifetime-extending strategies.

latest.title: Digital Transformation and Marketing Capability: The Moderating Role of Digital Marketing
latest.venue: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
latest.abstract: Based on the resource-based view and contingency theory, this study investigates the impact of digital transformation on corporate marketing capabilities and examines the moderating role of digital marketing. Using a sample of Chinese A-share listed companies from 2016 to 2024, the empirical analysis reveals that digital transformation significantly enhances marketing capabilities, while digital marketing further strengthens the causal relationship between them. Heterogeneity analysis shows that these effects vary across firms at different life cycle stages and with different pollution attributes. This study extends existing research on the microeconomic consequences of digital transformation and provides practical insights for firms in converting digital resources into competitive advantages in marketing.

latest.title: Value Orientations, Product-Specific Considerations, and Conditional Consumer Acceptance of Refrigerators Containing Recycled Materials in Poland
latest.abstract: Abstract The transition toward a circular economy requires not only technological and regulatory changes but also consumer acceptance of products incorporating recycled materials. While previous research has extensively examined pro-environmental consumption, comparatively less attention has been paid to high-involvement durable goods, where purchase decisions are infrequent and involve substantial financial and functional considerations. This study explores how consumers evaluate refrigerators containing recycled insulation by examining the interplay between personal value orientations, product-specific considerations, overall product evaluation, and conditional purchase consideration. The study draws on two qualitative focus group interviews conducted in Poland with 14 participants representing two age cohorts. The transcripts were analysed using thematic analysis combining deductive and inductive coding. The findings show that biospheric, altruistic, egoistic, and hedonic value orientations coexist in consumers’ reasoning, while their relative relevance varies with the purchase context. Product-specific considerations, including price, quality, durability and reliability, energy efficiency, functionality and usability, design and aesthetics, and credible product information formed an important complementary dimension of product evaluation. Recycled insulation was not evaluated as inherently positive; rather, participants’ evaluations were qualified by the perceived credibility of environmental benefits and expectations concerning product performance. Purchase consideration was likewise strongly conditional, particularly on price comparability, durability, reliability, and transparent environmental information. The study contributes to sustainable consumption and circ

latest.title: Brand-Mediated Intangible Cultural Heritage: Authenticity, Appropriation, and Consumer Legitimation in Starbucks China’s Heritage-Themed Retail Spaces
latest.abstract: Intangible cultural heritage (ICH) increasingly circulates through commercial and branded environments alongside museums, festivals, and community-based settings. This article examines Starbucks China’s heritage-themed retail spaces as a case of brand-mediated ICH, focusing on how consumers evaluate such representation. Drawing on critical heritage studies, brandscape theory, authenticity scholarship, heritage affect, and cultural appropriation research, the study tests a conditional affective legitimation model. In a stimulus-based online survey, 289 Chinese consumers living outside Guangdong Province viewed an approximately 40-s video and a written description of Starbucks China’s Guangzhou Yongqingfang ICH concept store. The original questionnaire assessed perceived cultural authenticity, cultural pride, brand attitude, and perceived cultural appropriation. These measures are interpreted, with explicit qualifications, in relation to perceived heritage authenticity, affective heritage resonance, consumer-level evaluation, and appropriation concern. Higher perceived authenticity was associated with stronger pride-related responses and more favorable brand evaluation. The estimated indirect association through pride was weaker at higher appropriation concern, although it remained positive. The study thus illustrates how favorable responses to commercially mediated heritage can coexist with ethical concern. Its empirical claims concern evaluations of a standardized representation, not sales performance, actual store experience, or legitimacy granted by heritage communities.

latest.title: Vigyapan Mart - Outdoor Advertising & Digital Marketing Agency
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: What is outdoor advertising? latest.title: A Study of CHAGEE's Marketing Strategies
latest.venue: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
latest.abstract: Against the backdrop of the growing popularity of China-chic consumption and increasing saturation and competition in the new-style tea beverage industry, young consumers' growing cultural confidence, health awareness, and desire for social sharing are reshaping the marketing strategies of tea beverage brands. Taking CHAGEE as its subject, this paper examines the factors influencing consumer behavior in the new-style tea beverage market from two perspectives: sociocultural influences and consumer psychology. It explores the underlying connections between CHAGEE's marketing strategies and consumer behavior. The study finds that CHAGEE effectively responds to the preferences of contemporary young consumers through a brand culture rooted in modern Chinese aesthetics, health-oriented product positioning, flexible tiered pricing, and culturally aligned IP collaborations, enabling the brand to rapidly gain widespread recognition. However, the brand also faces potential operational risks, including excessive dependence on a flagship product, a relatively narrow product range, and weak market performance of new products. This paper summarizes its marketing experience and existing problems, providing a reference for other new-style tea beverage brands in China seeking to avoid the pitfalls of viral popularity and achieve sustainable long-term development.

latest.title: Human factors shaping engagement with a digital treatment platform among individuals with lived experience of addiction
latest.abstract: Introduction Substance use disorders (SUDs) are highly prevalent, yet access to care remains limited. Digital interventions have been investigated as a means to expand treatment access, but individuals routinely disengage from them. We evaluated the acceptability, appropriateness, feasibility, and usability of a digital platform being tested as part of a collaborative care management-based intervention for SUD treatment in under-resourced areas to identify human factors influencing feasibility, usability, and accessibility. Methods Participants were adults with lived experience of addiction and related treatment. They engaged with the digital treatment platform for one week, then completed semi-structured interviews exploring their experience, followed by the Acceptability of Intervention Measure, Intervention Appropriateness Measure, Feasibility of Intervention Measure, and System Usability Scale. Template-based rapid analysis identified themes. Results 18 individuals ( n = 12 females) completed all assessments. Heavy text, lack of customization, and inconsistent notifications hindered usability. Participants felt assigned goals should match an individual's circumstances and resources available to them to support utilization. Participants desired personalization, integration with existing recovery supports, and features that encouraged routine use. Acceptability, appropriateness, and feasibility had respective means of 3.4 (95%CI = 3.0-3.9), 3.3 (95%CI = 2.8-3.9), and 3.4 (95%CI = 2.8-4.0) on 5-point scales with a neutral midpoint of 3. Usability scores approached the commonly used benchmark of 68 (mean=67.6, SD = 15.0). Discussion Digital interventions suffer from heavy disengagement. These findings suggest that digital interventions should fit the end-user's needs an

latest.title: EXAMINING THE MEDIATING ROLE OF TOURIST SATISFACTION IN THE TRAVEL MOTIVATION AND DESTINATION LOYALTY RELATIONSHIP: A PARTIAL LEAST SQUARES STRUCTURAL EQUATION MODELING ANALYSIS
latest.abstract: This study aims to empirically examine the relationships among travel motivation (push and pull factors), tourist satisfaction, and destination loyalty within the context of the Indian Himalayan region. Grounded in motivation theory, the study proposes that internal (push) and external (pull) motivational dimensions significantly influence tourist behavior, which in turn enhances overall satisfaction and fosters destination loyalty. Primary data were collected from 403 domestic tourists using a structured questionnaire. The data were analyzed using SPSS (Version 24) for preliminary analysis and Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to test the hypothesized relationships. The findings reveal a significant and positive relationship between tourist satisfaction and destination loyalty, indicating that satisfied tourists are more likely to revisit and recommend the destination. Furthermore, both push and pull motivation factors were found to have a substantial impact on tourist satisfaction, confirming their critical role in shaping travel experiences. The results also validate the proposed model by demonstrating statistically significant linkages among the key constructs, thereby contributing to the existing body of knowledge on tourism behavior. From a practical perspective, the study highlights the importance of designing destination attributes that align with tourists’ intrinsic motivations and expectations. Destination planners and tourism managers are encouraged to enhance the uniqueness, attractiveness, and experiential value of destinations to strengthen tourist satisfaction and loyalty. The study offers valuable insights for sustainable tourism development and strategic destination management in mountain regions.

latest.title: Role of Packaging in Dairy Products: Consumer Buying Behaviour in Anand and Vadodara, Gujarat, India
latest.venue: Journal of Scientific Research and Reports
latest.abstract: Packaging provides protection, convenience and product information and may influence consumers' decisions when purchasing dairy products. This study examined the role of packaging design, functionality, labelling, perceived quality and sustainability in the buying behaviour of consumers in Anand and Vadodara. Primary data were obtained from 300 respondents, comprising 150 consumers from each city, through a structured questionnaire using the reported random sampling method. The responses were analysed using frequency distributions and percentages. Product quality was identified as the principal purchase factor by 64% of respondents, followed by brand (33%), whereas 2% selected packaging as their principal factor. Nevertheless, 66% agreed or strongly agreed that packaging influenced their final purchase decision, and 62% reported noticing packaging before purchase. Respondents recognised packaging's contribution to safety and hygiene (73%), freshness (67%) and convenience (77%). Clear labelling was associated with greater consumer trust for 65%, while 55% expressed a preference for eco-friendly packaging. Price remained relevant to sustainable packaging choices, with 39% indicating that their preference depended on price. Leakage (35%) and difficulty in opening packages (31%) were the most frequently reported packaging-related problems. The findings suggest that packaging contributes to purchasing decisions and post-purchase experiences, although product quality and brand remain the leading primary purchase considerations among the surveyed consumers.

latest.title: Pengaruh Harga dan Promosi Online terhadap Keputusan Pembelian Online pada Aplikasi Online Shopee
latest.venue: Lead Journal of Economy and Administration
latest.abstract: The development of information technology and the internet has transformed consumer behavior regarding purchasing activities. The emergence of e-commerce has made it easier for consumers to search for product information, compare prices, and conduct transactions online. One widely used e-commerce platform is Shopee. In online shopping, price and promotion are key factors that consumers consider when making purchasing decisions. This study aims to examine the influence of price and online promotion on purchasing decisions made via the Shopee application among students at the Institut Bisnis dan Komputer Indonesia. The study employs a quantitative approach using a survey method. The respondents consist of 30 students from the Institut Bisnis dan Komputer Indonesia who have made purchases through the Shopee application. A purposive sampling technique was used based on predetermined criteria. Data were collected via a questionnaire using a Likert scale and analyzed using multiple linear regression, t-tests, F-tests, and the coefficient of determination (R²). The study seeks to determine the impact of price (individually), online promotion (individually), and both factors combined (simultaneously) on the purchasing decisions of students using the Shopee application. The results indicate that price has a positive and significant relationship with purchasing decisions (t = 2.745; p = 0.011). Online promotion also shows a positive and significant relationship with purchasing decisions (t = 2.831; p = 0.009). When considered simultaneously, both factors have a significant relationship (F = 20.898; p = 0.000004) with an R² value of 0.617 (61.7%).

latest.title: Comfort, camaraderie, conflict, contamination: examining identity and boundary work in fan experiences during troubling times
latest.abstract: During troubling times, consumers may turn to their favourite fandom to help them through, and we posit that there are overlooked aspects of fandom that hold value during troubling times. Using the context of 2020 and the release of the Harry Potter at Home initiative, we explore how fans experience fandom during troubling times. We find that fans may experience their fandom as: (1) comfort, (2) camaraderie, (3) conflict, or (4) contamination. We extend marketing theory by (1) reconceptualising fandom as an inherently imaginative phenomenon, (2) identifying fandom as providing stability and creating instability in troubling times, (3) explaining how identity and boundary work helps fans navigate troubling times, and (4) providing a framework for how the same fandom can be both stabilising and destabilising, depending on whether trouble is internal or external to it.

latest.title: Emotional Premium and Cost Escalation in Fan-Sign Events: A Mechanism Study of Affective Valuation and Scarcity-Driven Pricing
latest.venue: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
latest.abstract: K-pop fan-sign events monetise parasocial attachment by converting low-priced albums into access tokens for scarce, personalised interaction. Through the analysis of ENHYPEN's fan-sign event in Shanghai – "THE SIN: BLISS", the cost escalation process is explored. A combination of research about parasocial interaction, FOMO, fan identity, platformization, the official rules of the event and the structure of the case. The analysis results show that limited capacity, emotional attachment, platform visibility and uncertainty are the factors that move the consumers' attention from "value of the material" of the albums to "value of access". This change invalidates the price anchoring, supports the unofficial price and can stimulate re-consumption using social comparison. In the interim, fan-sign events can provide emotional gratification, a sense of community, album need and service innovation. To maintain these advantages and to reduce such damage, the study suggests that selection probabilities should be made more transparent, the verification process should be made more transparent, and that waiting lists should be officially maintained, limits should be put on campaign-level spending, and fan engagement should not be based on the number of purchases. These can assist entertainment businesses or platforms to maintain their people's confidence and help prevent over-investment and over-pricing, as well as fraud. The study offers a mechanism-based explanation of how the affective value is transfigured to monetary value in identity-bound fan experiences.

latest.title: A MARCA PESSOAL NA COMUNICAÇÃO DA WEPINK: UMA ANÁLISE DAS ESTRATÉGIAS DE PERSONAL BRANDING DE VIRGINIA FONSECA NO INSTAGRAM
latest.abstract: A transformação das redes sociais em espaços de comunicação, relacionamento e consumo ampliou a relevância da marca pessoal e do personal branding para influenciadores digitais e empreendedores. Nesse contexto, esta pesquisa teve como objetivo analisar a marca pessoal de Virginia Fonseca a partir das estratégias de personal branding utilizadas no Instagram e sua relação com a criação e consolidação da WePink. Especificamente, buscou-se identificar as estratégias utilizadas pela influenciadora para fortalecer sua marca pessoal, analisar a relação entre marca pessoal, credibilidade e engajamento no ambiente digital e investigar a contribuição da gestão da marca pessoal para a comunicação e consolidação da WePink. A pesquisa caracteriza-se como qualitativa, descritiva e exploratória, desenvolvida por meio de estudo de caso e procedimentos bibliográficos e documentais. Para a análise empírica, foram selecionadas sete publicações públicas do Instagram, relacionadas à vida pessoal, ao lifestyle, à atividade empresarial, aos produtos e às ações da WePink. Os conteúdos foram examinados por meio da análise de conteúdo, considerando aspectos de identidade, posicionamento, proximidade, credibilidade, interação e associação entre a imagem da influenciadora e a marca empresarial. Os resultados indicaram que a marca pessoal de Virginia é construída pela articulação entre exposição da vida pessoal, estilo de vida, empreendedorismo e comunicação comercial. Concluiu-se que o personal branding constitui um componente estratégico da comunicação da WePink, embora os dados analisados não permitam estabelecer relação causal direta entre a atuação da influenciadora e o desempenho econômico da empresa.

latest.title: Scarcity Marketing and Impulsive Consumption of the High-End Baijiu Industry: The "Uniqueness" of Limited Releases and Discontinued Re-Releases
latest.venue: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
latest.abstract: The marketing of scarce products has emerged as a crucial marketing concept in high-end baijiu brands to maintain premium product positions against the backdrop of consumption upgrading. The paper examines the effect of limited quantity releases and discontinued re-releases on impulsive purchasing by consumers using a typical marketing event of Kweichow Moutai as a case of analysis. Results show that small quantity sales enhance the competitive instincts of consumers to need exclusivity, and discontinuation of relaunch campaigns leads to a higher willingness to engage in impulsive purchasing due to the fear of missing out. Although these marketing channels have some positive effects, such as raising the perceived value of products and supporting social media communication, there are significant dangers in these marketing modalities: irrational over-stocking by consumers, loss of brand loyalty due to pseudo-scarcity, and speculative bubbles in the secondary markets. The three-dimensional optimization solutions that are suggested in the present paper in order to promote sustainable and responsible marketing in this industry are consumer cooling-off mechanisms, verifiable and transparent information disclosure, and multi-stakeholder collaborative supervision. This work provides theoretical insight and practical guidelines to standardize marketing activities, safeguard consumer interests, and ensure the orderly evolution of the high-end baijiu market.

latest.title: Sports Betting and Regulatory Governance in Nigeria: Consumer Protection, Disputed Winnings and Institutional Accountability
latest.abstract: This study examined sports betting and regulatory governance in Nigeria, with particular attention to disputed winnings, consumer protection and institutional accountability. It examined the practices and contractual provisions of sports-betting operators that generated disputes over winnings and assessed how effectively regulatory and consumer-protection institutions addressed such disputes. The study adopted a qualitative research design and relied on secondary data drawn from relevant laws, regulatory documents, operators’ terms and conditions, court cases, official records and credible media reports. Purposively selected cases were analysed thematically, focusing on bet cancellation and voiding, technical and settlement errors, integrity investigations, account restrictions, cash-out, payout limits, regulatory intervention and consumer redress. The findings showed that disputes often arose from the considerable contractual, technological and informational control operators exercised over betting transactions and settlement processes. Although regulatory institutions had formal mechanisms for handling complaints and enforcing regulations, their effectiveness in resolving disputes remained uneven. While some interventions resulted in payment and restoration of accounts, other cases lacked clearly documented independent determinations or meaningful redress. The study recommended that operators provide clearer reasons, applicable rules and supporting evidence for decisions affecting winnings, while regulators strengthen independent dispute-resolution mechanisms, coordinate the handling of cross-jurisdictional complaints and regularly publish information on complaints, determinations, sanctions and redress outcomes.
