latest.title: Digital Spendthrift Behavior Generasi Z dan Milenial dalam Perspektif Keuangan Islam
latest.abstract: Penelitian ini menganalisis pengaruh Islamic Financial Literacy, Proliferation of Digital Financial Apps, dan Financial Capability in Islamic Perspective terhadap Digital Spendthrift Behavior dengan Proliferation of Digital Advertising sebagai variabel mediasi, sekaligus menguji apakah pola hubungan tersebut berbeda antara Generasi Z dan Milenial. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan teknik purposive sampling berdasarkan kriteria tertentu dan menghasilkan 342 responden yang memenuhi syarat. Data diolah dengan Partial Least Squares–Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) yang dilanjutkan dengan Multi-Group Analysis (MGA) untuk membandingkan kedua generasi. Hasil analisis memperlihatkan bahwa Financial Capability in Islamic Perspective berpengaruh negatif dan signifikan terhadap Digital Spendthrift Behavior, sedangkan Proliferation of Digital Financial Apps dan Proliferation of Digital Advertising mendorong meningkatnya perilaku tersebut. Islamic Financial Literacy tidak memengaruhi Digital Spendthrift Behavior secara langsung, tetapi memiliki pengaruh tidak langsung yang signifikan melalui Proliferation of Digital Advertising. Peran mediasi Proliferation of Digital Advertising terbukti signifikan pada jalur Islamic Financial Literacy dan jalur Proliferation of Digital Financial Apps menuju Digital Spendthrift Behavior. Hasil MGA menunjukkan bahwa perbedaan antargenerasi hanya terjadi pada pengaruh langsung Proliferation of Digital Financial Apps terhadap Digital Spendthrift Behavior. Temuan ini menjadi landasan bagi perumusan strategi edukasi yang mempertimbangkan karakter setiap generasi dan berakar pada nilai-nilai keuangan Islam, serta memperkaya literatur melalui integrasi konstruk keuangan Islam dan perbedaan generasi dengan pendekatan PLS-SEM MGA.

latest.title: The Factors Influencing Customer Satisfaction with No-Code WhatsApp Automation: A Study of Yeti
latest.abstract: Quality of Support is the strongest single driver of customer satisfaction with WhatsApp business automation platforms (β = 0.470, p = 0.008), ahead of ease of use, ease of setup and product direction, even though all four attributes are strongly correlated with satisfaction (r = 0.872 to 0.917, p < 0.001). Most research on chatbots and WhatsApp marketing measures the satisfaction of end consumers who chat with a brand. The business customers who buy and run the automation platform, and the platforms themselves as competing products, are almost absent as a unit of analysis. This paper addresses that gap with a cross-sectional analysis of verified G2 user-review scores for 26 WhatsApp and conversational automation platforms, representing 4,512 reviews, collected on 1 October 2026. The study grew out of a summer internship at Yeti (IncrediBee Private Limited), an Ahmedabad-based no-code platform. It tests seven hypotheses on (1–4) the link between each platform attribute and satisfaction, (5) the joint influence of the four attributes, (6) usability differences between no-code and API-based platforms and (7) satisfaction differences between Indian and global platforms. Three findings stand out. First, the four attributes together explain 89.1% of the variation in satisfaction (F = 43.12, p < 0.001), but once they are entered together only support remains individually significant; a reduced model with ease of use and support keeps almost all of that explanatory power (R² = 0.880). Second, no-code platforms are rated easier to use than API/CPaaS providers (Mann–Whitney U = 93.0, p = 0.047). Third, Indian and global platforms do not differ significantly in satisfaction (p = 0.478). The results suggest that, in a market where features and prices have converged, support is the

latest.title: Pengaruh Kualitas, Variasi Produk, dan Persepsi Harga terhadap Keputusan Pembelian Sarung Wadimor
latest.abstract: Penurunan dan fluktuasi kekuatan merek Sarung Wadimor menjadi permasalahan yang perlu diperhatikan di tengah persaingan industri sarung yang semakin kompetitif. Kondisi tersebut menunjukkan pentingnya mengetahui faktor-faktor yang memengaruhi keputusan pembelian konsumen. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh kualitas produk, variasi produk, dan persepsi harga terhadap keputusan pembelian Sarung Wadimor di Kota Bandung. Penelitian menggunakan metode deskriptif dan verifikatif dengan pendekatan kuantitatif. Data primer diperoleh melalui kuesioner yang disebarkan kepada 385 responden masyarakat Kota Bandung yang pernah membeli Sarung Wadimor. Analisis data dilakukan menggunakan Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) versi 27 dengan analisis regresi linear berganda. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa kualitas produk, variasi produk, persepsi harga, dan keputusan pembelian berada pada kategori tinggi. Secara parsial, kualitas produk, variasi produk, dan persepsi harga berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap keputusan pembelian. Secara simultan, ketiga variabel tersebut berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap keputusan pembelian. Nilai R² sebesar 0,638 menunjukkan bahwa 63,8% keputusan pembelian dapat dijelaskan oleh ketiga variabel tersebut, sedangkan 36,2% dipengaruhi faktor lain di luar penelitian. Temuan ini menunjukkan pentingnya peningkatan kualitas, pengembangan variasi produk, dan penetapan harga sesuai nilai yang ditawarkan.

latest.title: Optimalisasi Kualitas, Citra Merek, dan Persepsi Harga Terhadap Kepuasan Pelanggan Wardah di Daerah Istimewa Yogyakarta
latest.venue: Journal of Organizational Performance and Analysis
latest.abstract: Kepuasan pelanggan menjadi hal penting dalam menentukan kesuksesan sebuah produk kosmetik, terutama di tengah persaingan yang semakin ketat. Penelitian ini membahas bagaimana kualitas produk, citra merek, dan cara konsumen melihat harga berkontribusi pada kepuasan pelanggan Wardah di Daerah Istimewa Yogyakarta. Penelitian ini melihat masing-masing faktor secara terpisah dan juga bersamaan, serta mencari tahu faktor yang paling berpengaruh. Pendekatan kuantitatif diterapkan melalui analisis regresi linear berganda terhadap jawaban 36 responden. Hasil analisis memperlihatkan kualitas produk dan persepsi harga menghasilkan dampak baik yang relevan terhadap kepuasan pelanggan, dengan nilai signifikansi di bawah 0,001. Sebaliknya, citra merek belum menunjukkan pengaruh parsial yang signifikan karena nilai signifikansinya sebesar 0,259. Ketika ketiga variabel diuji secara simultan, hasilnya tetap signifikan dengan nilai F 308,388 dan p < 0,001. Model regresi mampu menjelaskan 96,7% variasi kepuasan pelanggan, sebagaimana tercermin pada nilai R² 0,967. Kualitas produk tercatat menjadi factor dominan, dengan Standardized Beta senilai 0,562. Temuan ini menekankan bahwa peningkatan kepuasan konsumen Wardah perlu didukung oleh konsistensi mutu produk serta kesamaan antara harga dan manfaat yang dirasakan pelanggan.

latest.title: ANALISIS FAKTOR HARGA, PROMOSI, DAN ULASAN ONLINE DALAM KEPUTUSAN PEMBELIAN ONLINE PADA MAHASISWA UNIVERSITAS TERBUKA SALUT BINA MAHUNIKA BOGOR
latest.venue: Integrative Perspectives of Social and Science Journal
latest.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan mendeskripsikan pertimbangan harga, promosi, dan ulasan online dalam keputusan pembelian online mahasiswa Universitas Terbuka SALUT Bina Mahunika Bogor. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif deskriptif. Informan terdiri atas sepuluh mahasiswa yang dipilih secara purposif berdasarkan pengalaman berbelanja melalui marketplace serta pengalaman mempertimbangkan harga, promosi, dan ulasan pelanggan. Data utama diperoleh melalui wawancara semi-terstruktur. Analisis dilakukan melalui kondensasi data, penyajian data, serta penarikan dan verifikasi kesimpulan. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa pertimbangan harga mencakup keterjangkauan, kewajaran harga, perkiraan kualitas, dan biaya pengiriman. Promosi menarik perhatian serta menjadi pertimbangan waktu pembelian, tetapi tidak selalu menghasilkan transaksi. Ulasan online digunakan untuk memeriksa kesesuaian produk, pengalaman pembeli sebelumnya, dan pelayanan penjual. Harga, promosi, dan ulasan online dipertimbangkan secara berkaitan. Penawaran yang murah dan menarik dapat ditolak apabila ulasan menimbulkan keraguan. Penelitian ini menunjukkan bahwa keputusan pembelian informan melibatkan penilaian terhadap kemampuan anggaran, keuntungan penawaran, dan keyakinan terhadap produk.

latest.title: Integrated Marketing Strategy Based on 7P and 7C to Strengthen the Competitiveness of Franchise Micro-Warteg
latest.venue: International Journal of Economics Business and Innovation Research
latest.abstract: This article examines integrated marketing strategy at Warteg Kharisma Bahari Lkr Dramaga as a case study of a micro franchise food stall near the IPB Dramaga area. The study is motivated by the need for small food businesses to move beyond good food and affordable prices by managing communication, service, process, physical evidence, and customer feedback consistently. The article applies an applied case study approach using customer short interview data, employee interview data, store observation, and an assessment of offline and online touchpoints. The analysis combines descriptive quantitative reading and thematic qualitative interpretation using the 7P framework paired with 7C. The findings show that the main value of the food stall lies in taste, menu variety, affordable prices, fast service, QRIS payment, and convincing food display. The main improvement areas are price transparency, promotional signage, Google Maps review governance, coordination during peak hours, and stronger physical evidence. This article proposes a realistic integrated marketing micro toolkit for micro franchisees.

latest.title: PENGARUH KUALITAS PELAYANAN DAN HARGA TERHADAP KEPUTUSAN PEMBELIAN MINYAK GORENG PADA PELANGGAN PT RAJAWALI NUSINDO CABANG TANGERANG
latest.venue: Jurnal Ilmiah Ekonomi Manajemen Bisnis dan Akuntansi.
latest.abstract: Persaingan distribusi minyak goreng yang semakin ketat, termasuk dari pedagang perorangan yang menawarkan harga lebih murah, menuntut distributor memahami faktor yang mendorong keputusan pembelian pelanggannya. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh kualitas pelayanan dan harga terhadap keputusan pembelian minyak goreng pada pelanggan PT Rajawali Nusindo Cabang Tangerang. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan desain asosiatif. Populasi penelitian berjumlah 1.014 pelanggan, dan sampel sebanyak 99 responden ditentukan dengan rumus Slovin serta dipilih melalui teknik accidental sampling. Data dikumpulkan menggunakan kuesioner berisi 42 butir pernyataan dengan skala Likert lima poin, kemudian dianalisis melalui uji validitas dan reliabilitas, uji asumsi klasik, regresi linier sederhana dan berganda, koefisien korelasi dan determinasi, uji t, serta uji F dengan bantuan SPSS 26. Hasil deskriptif menunjukkan bahwa kualitas pelayanan dinilai baik (rata-rata 3,49), sedangkan persepsi harga (3,35) dan keputusan pembelian (3,35) dinilai kurang baik. Secara individual, kualitas pelayanan (koefisien 0,793; t = 13,629; p < 0,05) dan harga (koefisien 1,135; t = 42,200; p < 0,05) berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap keputusan pembelian. Ketika kedua variabel diuji dalam satu model, harga tetap signifikan (t = 23,300; p < 0,05), sedangkan kualitas pelayanan tidak lagi signifikan (t = 0,452; p = 0,652), yang menunjukkan bahwa kontribusinya tumpang tindih dengan persepsi harga pelanggan. Secara simultan, kualitas pelayanan dan harga berpengaruh signifikan terhadap keputusan pembelian (F = 883,204; p < 0,05) dan menjelaskan 94,8% variasinya. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa pada pasar distribusi yang didominasi pelanggan wirausaha, daya saing harga menjadi p

latest.title: Persepsi Harga, Kualitas Pelayanan Dan Kemudahan Penggunaan Terhadap Kepuasan Pelanggan Indrive Di Garut
latest.abstract: Maraknya penggunaan aplikasi ride-hailing di Indonesia, termasuk inDrive dengan skema negosiasi tarif langsung antara penumpang dan pengemudi, memunculkan pertanyaan mengenai tingkat kepuasan pengguna terhadap layanan tersebut, khususnya di Kabupaten Garut yang penggunaannya terus meningkat. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis pengaruh persepsi harga, kualitas pelayanan, dan kemudahan penggunaan terhadap kepuasan pelanggan aplikasi inDrive di Kabupaten Garut, baik secara parsial maupun simultan. Penelitian menggunakan metode kuantitatif dengan pendekatan deskriptif-asosiatif terhadap 100 responden yang dipilih melalui accidental sampling, dengan data dianalisis menggunakan SEM-PLS melalui SmartPLS. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa persepsi harga dan kualitas pelayanan berada pada kategori baik, sedangkan kemudahan penggunaan tergolong cukup baik, dan ketiga variabel tersebut baik secara parsial maupun simultan terbukti berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap kepuasan pelanggan, dengan persepsi harga sebagai prediktor paling dominan. Berdasarkan temuan tersebut, pengelola inDrive disarankan meningkatkan transparansi tarif, kualitas layanan pengemudi, dan kemudahan penggunaan aplikasi guna meningkatkan kepuasan pelanggan.

latest.title: Influence of Social Comparison Bias, Peer Pressure and Financial Anxiety on Excessive Investment Risk-Taking Among Individual Investors in Bengaluru
latest.abstract: Most individuals who invest like to feel that their choices are made based on research and a planned strategy. In practice, a lot of investing takes place on a phone, between group chats, reels and trading apps, where others’ gains are a thumb swipe away. This study asks whether this environment influences individual investors to take more risks than they can reasonably carry. Using the responses from individual investors in Bengaluru (351 observations used in estimation, against a target of 385), we test whether Social Comparison Bias, Peer Pressure and Financial Anxiety relate to Excessive Investment Risk-Taking, whether Fear of Missing Out (FOMO) carries part of that influence, and whether Financial Literacy softens it. The model was estimated using PLS-SEM in SmartPLS 4. Peer Pressure (𝛽 = 0.199, 𝑝 = 0.005), Financial Anxiety (𝛽 = 0.227, 𝑝 = 0.024) and FOMO (𝛽 = 0.346, 𝑝 < 0.001) increased risk-taking, while Social Comparison Bias did not (𝛽 = 0.029, 𝑝 = 0.591). FOMO partly transmitted the effects of Peer Pressure (indirect 𝛽 = 0.094, 𝑝 = 0.003) and Financial Anxiety (indirect 𝛽 = 0.193, 𝑝 = 0.002). Financial Literacy did not moderate any relationship (𝑝 = 0.577 to 0.821). The model explained 60.0% of the variance in FOMO and 55.0% in risk-taking. In short, it is the pressure to act, not the act of comparing, that appears to matter, and knowing more about finance did not by itself protect investors from it.

latest.title: Pemanfaatan Microsoft Excel Dalam Pengelolaan Keuangan Usaha Mikro, Kecil, dan Menengah (UMKM) Perspektif Hukum Ekonomi Syariah
latest.abstract: Micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) need orderly financial records to monitor business activities, assess performance, and make responsible economic decisions. For Muslim-owned or sharia-oriented MSMEs, financial administration also has a normative dimension: transactions should be recorded transparently, agreements should be clear, and business practices should avoid riba, gharar, and maysir. This article examines the use of Microsoft Excel in MSME financial management from the perspective of Islamic economic law. It applies a descriptive qualitative literature-review method combined with a normative-conceptual analysis of sharia business principles, relevant regulations, and studies on spreadsheet-based accounting and sharia-oriented MSMEs. The literature indicates that Excel can assist transaction recording, cash-flow monitoring, cost calculation, inventory control, and preparation of financial summaries. From an Islamic economic law perspective, these functions may support the principles of amanah, shiddiq, ‘adl, transparency, and protection of wealth (hifz al-mal), provided that the workbook records the substance of transactions accurately. For transactions using contracts such as murabahah, mudharabah, musyarakah, or ijarah, the records should identify the contract, parties, object, price or capital contribution, agreed margin or profit-sharing ratio, payment schedule, and outstanding obligations as relevant. Excel itself does not certify sharia compliance; that assessment depends on the validity of the contract and the actual conduct of the parties. The article concludes that Excel is a practical initial tool for MSMEs when supported by clear procedures, adequate user knowledge, internal checks, and accounting treatment appropriate to the transaction and

latest.title: Financial Management and Budgeting Skills Among Accounting Students: Basis for an Enhanced Financial Management Program
latest.venue: International Journal of Education, Research, and Innovation Perspectives
latest.abstract: This quantitative descriptive–correlational study examined financial management and budgeting skills among 141 students enrolled in accountancy and accounting information systems programs at two campuses of Arellano University in the Philippines. A researcher-developed questionnaire assessed five financial-management domains (knowledge, behavior, attitude, capability, and planning) and three budgeting-skill domains (budget planning, expense tracking, and financial goal setting). Responses were summarized using frequency, percentage, and weighted means; the original thesis reported a Pearson correlation between the composite constructs. Financial attitude had the highest financial-management domain mean (M = 3.50), whereas budget planning had the highest budgeting-skill mean (M = 3.53). Expense tracking had the lowest budgeting-skill mean (M = 3.20), particularly the use of financial tools for daily expense tracking (M = 3.08). Financial management and budgeting skills were strongly positively associated, r(139) = .815, with the original study reporting p = .001. The findings suggest that favorable financial attitudes and planning intentions coexist with comparatively less consistent expense-tracking practices. An enhanced financial management program is proposed, incorporating applied budgeting simulations, expense-recording routines, digital and paper-based tracking, and measurable learning outcomes. Because the study is cross-sectional and based on self-report, findings should not be interpreted causally. The reported inferential statistics and instrument reliability require confirmation against original analytical records before submission.

latest.title: Managing consumer behavior through digital marketing strategies: a comprehensive review
latest.venue: Actual problems of innovative economy and law
latest.abstract: Digital marketing has fundamentally transformed how businesses influence consumer behavior by leveraging tools such as social media, search engine optimization, content marketing, email marketing, and data analytics. This paper provides a comprehensive review of how digital marketing strategies manage consumer behavior, focusing on their impact on consumer engagement, decision-making, and brand loyalty. The purpose of the article is to conduct a comprehensive study of the theoretical and methodological foundations of consumer behavior management in the context of the digitalization of marketing activities, to systematize contemporary digital marketing strategies, and to identify the mechanisms through which they influence the processes of forming, transforming, and forecasting consumer needs, motivations, and behavioral patterns. The methodological foundation of this study consists of a set of general scientific and specialized methods, the application of which ensures a systematic and comprehensive approach to the study of consumer behavior management in the context of the digitalization of marketing activities (in particular, methods of analysis and synthesis, induction and deduction, systematization, comparative analysis, etc.). By synthesizing insights from literature and empirical studies, the study identifies and systematizes the key digital marketing tools, their applications, and their influence on consumer behavior across diverse contexts. The analysis highlights the role of personalization, social media engagement, and data-driven decision-making in fostering consumer trust and brand loyalty. It establishes the correspondence between the stages of the consumer decision-making process – awareness, information search, evaluation, purchase, and post-purchase – an

latest.title: The Role of Environmental Awareness and Green Advertising in Driving Young Consumers’ Green Purchase Intention
latest.venue: International Journal of Innovative Research in Technology
latest.abstract: This study investigates the psychological and promotional drivers influencing Green Purchase Intention (GPI) among young consumers in emerging markets, utilizing an extended Theory of Planned Behaviour framework.Amidst escalating global environmental crises, the paper specifically examines the direct and indirect roles of Environmental Awareness (EA), Green Advertising (GA), and Green Product Literacy (GPL).A quantitative cross-sectional survey was administered to 430 young consumers in the Dharmapuri district.The results demonstrate that EA is the primary foundational driver, strongly and positively influencing both GPL and GPI.GPL also emerged as a significant direct predictor of GPI, underscoring the critical need for detailed knowledge in bridging the intention-behaviour gap.Crucially, the direct relationship between GA and GPI was found to be statistically non-significant; however, GA successfully functions indirectly by enhancing EA and GPL.These findings emphasize that successful green marketing strategies must prioritize transparency and trust to build cognitive assets and literacy rather than relying on generic promotional volume, offering clear implications for marketers and policymakers dedicated to fostering sustainable consumption.

latest.title: Low-Carbon Consumer Behavior in the Digital Age: Investigating the Determinants of Green Product Purchase Intentions in E-Commerce Platforms
latest.abstract: Digital commerce is reshaping how consumers discover, evaluate, and purchase products, creating new opportunities to encourage lower-carbon consumption while also intensifying convenience-driven consumption and information overload. This article examines the determinants of green product purchase intention in e-commerce by integrating behavioral, value-based, trust-based, and digital-information perspectives. It develops an integrative conceptual framework that links environmental concern, attitudes toward green products, subjective norms, perceived behavioral control, green perceived value, price perceptions, green trust, digital information quality, electronic word of mouth, platform affordances, and perceived greenwashing to purchase intention. The article uses a structured integrative review of recent research and authoritative sustainability reports, emphasizing studies published from 2021 onward while retaining established theories where needed to explain underlying mechanisms. The synthesis indicates that pro-environmental concern is important but rarely sufficient on its own: consumers must also believe that a product performs well, offers acceptable value, can be purchased without excessive effort, and is supported by credible evidence. Digital interfaces may reduce information costs through certification details, traceability, reviews, and product comparisons, yet they can also amplify unsubstantiated environmental claims and impulsive purchasing. Green trust and perceived information usefulness therefore emerge as central mechanisms connecting digital communication to intention, while price sensitivity, perceived risk, delivery impacts, and doubts about green claims can weaken the relationship.

latest.title: Analyzing the Effects of Price and Product Quality on Sales Volume: Evidence from Pleasure Gold Products
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyze the effects of price and product quality on the sales volume of Pleasure Gold products at PT Delisari Nusantara Medan. The increasing competition in the gold product industry requires companies to understand the factors that influence sales performance, particularly through pricing strategies and product quality improvement. This research employed a quantitative approach with a causal associative research design. The population consisted of consumers who had purchased Pleasure Gold products at PT Delisari Nusantara Medan, with a total sample of 50 respondents selected using saturated sampling techniques. Data were analyzed using validity tests, reliability tests, classical assumption tests, multiple linear regression analysis, partial significance tests, simultaneous significance tests, and the coefficient of determination test. The results indicate that price has a significant effect on sales volume, as shown by the t-value of 11.214, which exceeds the t-table value of 1.677. Furthermore, product quality also has a significant effect on sales volume, with a t-value of 2.496 greater than the t-table value of 1.677. Simultaneously, price and product quality significantly influence sales volume, demonstrated by the F-value of 140.108 exceeding the F-table value of 4.040. This study contributes empirical evidence regarding the importance of pricing strategies and product quality enhancement in increasing sales performance, particularly in the gold product industry.

latest.title: ANALYSIS OF SOCIAL MEDIA MARKETING, NEW CULTURAL MARKETING AND SERVICESCAPE ON REPURCHASE INTENTION AT LANGIT SOCIETY CAFE
latest.venue: International Journal of Economic Business Accounting Agriculture Management and Sharia Administration (IJEBAS)
latest.abstract: This study was motivated by the fluctuating sales performance of Cafe Langit Society and the results of a preliminary survey indicating that consumers’ repurchase intention had not yet been optimally established. This study aims to analyze the effects of Social Media Marketing, New Cultural Marketing, and Servicescape on consumers’ Repurchase Intention at Cafe Langit Society, both partially and simultaneously. This study employed a quantitative approach with an associative research design. The sampling technique used was nonprobability sampling using purposive sampling, involving a total of 135 respondents. Data were collected through questionnaires using a Likert scale and processed using IBM SPSS Statistics version 27. The analytical techniques included multiple linear regression analysis, partial tests (t-test), simultaneous tests (F-test), and the coefficient of determination. The results showed that Social Media Marketing had a positive and significant effect on Repurchase Intention, with a t-value of 3.552 and a significance value of 0.001. New Cultural Marketing also had a positive and significant effect on Repurchase Intention, with a t-value of 3.363 and a significance value of 0.001. Servicescape had a positive and significant effect on Repurchase Intention, with a t-value of 4.380 and p < 0.001. Servicescape had the highest standardized beta coefficient of 0.349, indicating that it was the variable with the relatively strongest influence on Repurchase Intention. Simultaneously, Social Media Marketing, New Cultural Marketing, and Servicescape had a significant effect on Repurchase Intention, with an F-value of 56.334 and p < 0.001. The adjusted R-squared (R²) value of 0.553 indicates that the three variables explained 55.3% of the variation in Repurchase Inten

latest.title: ANALYSIS OF CUSTOMER RELATIONSHIP MARKETING, ELECTRONIC WORD-OF-MOUTH AND CUSTOMER PERCEIVED VALUE ON PURCHASE INTENTION FOR BATAK ULOS VESTS AT THE MSME WARUNG IMPAS
latest.venue: International Journal of Economic Business Accounting Agriculture Management and Sharia Administration (IJEBAS)
latest.abstract: Purchase intention is a psychological tendency or an inclination on the part of a prospective consumer to acquire a product, arising after a process of evaluating information, perceived value, and marketing interactions. This study aims to examine and analyze the influence of Customer Relationship Marketing, Electronic Word of Mouth, and Customer Perceived Value on the purchase intention of prospective buyers of *Ulos Batak* vests from the MSME "Warung Impas" in Medan City. The study utilizes primary data collected through questionnaires. The research was conducted with a sample of 110 respondents who were prospective buyers of *Ulos Batak* vests from the MSME "Warung Impas" in Medan City. The analysis results indicate that Customer Relationship Marketing has a positive and significant effect on prospective buyers' purchase intention. Electronic Word of Mouth does not have a significant effect on prospective buyers' purchase intention. Customer Perceived Value has a positive and significant effect on prospective buyers' purchase intention. The analysis demonstrates that Customer Relationship Marketing, Electronic Word of Mouth, and Customer Perceived Value simultaneously exert a significant influence on the purchase intention of prospective buyers of *Ulos Batak* vests from the MSME "Warung Impas" in Medan City.

latest.title: THE INFLUENCE OF EMOTIONAL INTELLIGENCE, WORK-LIFE BALANCE AND PHYSICAL WORK ENVIRONMENT ON EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE AT PT. MIDI UTAMA INDONESIA
latest.venue: International Journal of Economic Business Accounting Agriculture Management and Sharia Administration (IJEBAS)
latest.abstract: This research is motivated by the importance of improving employee performance through the management of psychological factors and a supportive work environment at PT. Midi Utama Indonesia Tbk. The purpose of this study is to analyze the effect of emotional intelligence, work-life balance, and physical work environment on employee performance. This research employed a quantitative approach using a survey method through questionnaires distributed to 88 employees and analyzed using multiple linear regression. The results indicate that emotional intelligence, work-life balance, and physical work environment have a positive and significant effect on employee performance, both partially and simultaneously. The main finding of this study confirms that work-life balance provides the most dominant contribution compared to other variables in improving employee performance. The novelty of this research lies in examining three integrated internal and external factors within a modern retail company, providing a comprehensive perspective for human resource management development. The implications of this study suggest that companies need to strengthen emotional management, work-life balance practices, and work environment quality to enhance productivity and achieve sustainable organizational goals.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Optimalisasi Peran Mahasiswa dalam Penerapan Aplikasi Pencatatan Keuangan untuk Meningkatkan Kemandirian Finansial di Politeknik Sultan Salahuddin Abdul Aziz Shah Selangor, Malaysia
latest.abstract: Mahasiswa di era ekonomi digital rentan melakukan pengeluaran impulsif, sementara kebiasaan mencatat transaksi dan menyusun anggaran masih lemah sehingga kemandirian finansial sulit terbentuk. Pengabdian internasional ini bertujuan meningkatkan kemandirian finansial mahasiswa Politeknik Sultan Salahuddin Abdul Aziz Shah Selangor, Malaysia, melalui optimalisasi peran mahasiswa dalam penggunaan aplikasi pencatatan keuangan Sakubijak. Pendekatan behavioral–digital intervention dilaksanakan dalam lima tahap: observasi, persiapan, pelatihan literasi keuangan digital, pendampingan tiga bulan bersama Peer Financial Ambassadors, dan evaluasi akhir. Dari 25 mahasiswa sasaran, 23 (92%) mengikuti program secara aktif. Sebanyak 87% peserta aktif mencatat minimal 80% transaksi, 96% menerapkan anggaran bulanan, proporsi pengeluaran non-prioritas turun 18,4 poin persentase, tabungan meningkat 27,6%, dan kepuasan mitra mencapai 88,5%. Model ini berpotensi direplikasi untuk memperkuat kapabilitas keuangan mahasiswa.

latest.title: Pengaruh Harga Dan Citra Merek Terhadap Keputusan Pembelian Produk Merek Nevada Dengan Peran Persepsi Kualitas Sebagai Variabel Mediasi Pada Konsumen Di PT Matahari Departement Store Mantos
latest.venue: JURNAL RISET EKONOMI, MANAJEMEN, BISNIS DAN AKUNTANSI
latest.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis pengaruh harga dan citra merek terhadap keputusan pembelian produk merek Nevada dengan persepsi kualitas sebagai variabel mediasi pada konsumen PT Matahari Department Store Mantos. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif asosiatif dengan data primer dari kuesioner terhadap 100 responden yang dipilih melalui purposive sampling dengan ukuran sampel dihitung menggunakan rumus Lemeshow, serta dianalisis menggunakan Partial Least Square-Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) berbantuan SmartPLS 4. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa harga (β = 0,376; p = 0,000) dan citra merek (β = 0,337; p = 0,001) berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap keputusan pembelian, serta harga (β = 0,611; p = 0,000) dan citra merek (β = 0,550; p = 0,000) berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap persepsi kualitas. Persepsi kualitas berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap keputusan pembelian (β = 0,242; p = 0,035) serta memediasi pengaruh harga terhadap keputusan pembelian (p = 0,031), tetapi tidak memediasi pengaruh citra merek terhadap keputusan pembelian (p = 0,053). Dengan demikian, harga dan citra merek merupakan determinan langsung keputusan pembelian, sedangkan persepsi kualitas berperan sebagai jalur yang memperkuat pengaruh harga. Kata kunci: harga, citra merek, persepsi kualitas, keputusan pembelian, Nevada

latest.title: Analysis of Instagram Digital Marketing and Product Quality, on Repurchase Intention in Tenpura Jakarta
latest.abstract: This study aimed to examine the effects of Instagram digital marketing and product quality on customers' repurchase intention at Tenpura Jakarta, a restaurant located in Blok M, South Jakarta. A quantitative research design with an associative approach was employed. Data were collected through questionnaires administered to 100 respondents selected using purposive sampling. The data were analyzed using validity and reliability tests, classical assumption tests, and multiple linear regression analysis with IBM SPSS Statistics. The results revealed that digital marketing had a positive and statistically significant relationship with repurchase intention, with a reported correlation coefficient (r) of 0.420 and a significance level of p < 0.001. Conversely, product quality was not significantly associated with repurchase intention (r = ?0.019, p = 0.849). The overall regression model was statistically significant (F = 10.492), with a coefficient of determination (R²) of 0.178, indicating that digital marketing and product quality collectively explained 17.8% of the variance in repurchase intention. These findings suggest that Instagram digital marketing was more strongly associated with customers' repurchase intention than product quality in the context of Tenpura Jakarta. The study highlights the importance of optimizing Instagram digital marketing strategies and recommends examining additional factors, such as brand image and customer experience, to better understand and potentially enhance customers' repurchase intention.

latest.title: Consumer financial behavior, digital payments, and financial debt during ritualized consumption
latest.abstract: Ritualized consumption combines emotional engagement, digital purchasing, and financial debt, yet these dynamics remain underexplored in crisis-affected economies. This study examines how Christmas shopping routines, gift-selection practices, and online payment methods are associated with Christmas spirit and Christmas debt among Lebanese consumers. The framework integrates Ritual Theory, Gift-Giving and Social Exchange theories, Normative Social Influence Theory, Hedonic Consumption Theory, and Self-Control Theory. Online survey data from a sample of 284 Lebanese consumers were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling. Christmas shopping routines showed the strongest association with Christmas spirit (β = 0.472, p < 0.001), while shopping routines and Christmas spirit showed the strongest associations with Christmas debt (both β = 0.380, p < 0.001). Christmas spirit significantly mediated the associations between all three antecedents and Christmas debt, supporting partial mediation. The findings indicate that ritualized, relational, and technologically enabled consumption practices are associated with both positive festive engagement and greater Christmas-related financial obligations. The study contributes to consumer behavior, consumer finance, and digital consumption research by integrating cultural, emotional, technological, and financial perspectives. It offers implications for retailers, policymakers, and digital payment providers seeking to promote responsible spending and financial transparency during high-consumption periods.

latest.title: Strategic Drivers of E-Retailer Loyalty in Emerging Markets: A Management-Oriented Analysis of E-Service Quality and Trust in Online Reviews
latest.abstract: This study examines how e-service quality, perceived price fairness, and trust in online reviews are associated with e-retailer loyalty in Kazakhstan and Türkiye. A cross-sectional online survey generated 288 complete responses from consumers with prior online-shopping experience. The principal analytical sample comprised 284 respondents from Kazakhstan and Türkiye. E-service quality was modelled as a higher-order construct comprising system efficiency, fulfilment, and privacy, while perceived price fairness, trust in online reviews, and loyalty were specified as first-order constructs. The proposed relationships were tested using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM), bootstrapped mediation analysis, predictive assessment, robustness checks, measurement-invariance analysis, and exploratory multi-group comparison. The model explained 65.8% of the variance in trust in online reviews and 70.3% of the variance in e-retailer loyalty. E-service quality showed a strong positive association with trust and the largest total association with loyalty. Trust was positively associated with loyalty and partially mediated the relationship between e-service quality and loyalty. Perceived price fairness showed no significant direct association with loyalty but contributed indirectly through trust, indicating an indirect-only mediation pattern. The main structural relationships remained stable after response-quality screening and demographic adjustment. Cross-country coefficient differences were not statistically significant. However, full compositional invariance was not established for higher-order e-service quality, so national comparisons should be interpreted as exploratory. The study integrates operational service performance, price fairness, and trust in c

latest.title: ANALYSIS OF THE ROLE OF SERVICE QUALITY, PRICE, AND PRODUCT QUALITY IN SHAPING CUSTOMER SATISFACTION
latest.venue: KOMPLEKSITAS JURNAL ILMIAH MANAJEMEN ORGANISASI DAN BISNIS
latest.abstract: Customer satisfaction is one of the key indicators of a company's success amid increasingly intense business competition in both the service and manufacturing sectors. This study aims to analyze the roles of service quality, price, and product quality in influencing customer satisfaction. This study employs a qualitative approach using a literature review method to develop an in-depth understanding of how service quality, price, and product quality influence customer satisfaction based on previous research findings. The literature review indicates that service quality plays an important role in enhancing customer satisfaction. Customer satisfaction also tends to increase when prices are perceived as fair and commensurate with the benefits received by customers. Product quality is another factor influencing customer satisfaction, particularly in terms of product performance, durability, conformance to specifications, and perceived value. Most previous studies indicate that these three variables, both individually and simultaneously, have a positive and significant influence on customer satisfaction. latest.title: Peran Citra Merek Dan Promosi Media Sosial Terhadap Keputusan Pembelian Di Mandalika Perfume Bogor
latest.venue: Jurnal Ekonomi Bisnis Manajemen dan Akuntansi
latest.abstract: Persaingan ritel parfum mendorong pelaku usaha memperkuat citra merek dan mengoptimalkan promosi digital untuk menarik konsumen. Menganalisis pengaruh citra merek dan promosi media sosial terhadap keputusan pembelian konsumen Mandalika Perfume Bogor serta menentukan variabel yang lebih dominan merupakan tujuan penelitian ini. Pendekatan kuantitatif diterapkan melalui survei terhadap konsumen yang dipilih menggunakan teknik purposive sampling. Data dikumpulkan melalui kuesioner berskala Likert lima poin dan dianalisis menggunakan SPSS, meliputi pengujian validitas, reliabilitas, asumsi klasik, regresi linear berganda, uji parsial, uji simultan, dan koefisien determinasi. Hasil analisis menunjukkan bahwa citra merek dan promosi media sosial masing-masing berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap keputusan pembelian. Kedua variabel juga secara simultan berpengaruh signifikan. Promosi media sosial menunjukkan pengaruh relatif lebih dominan dibandingkan citra merek. Penemuan ini menekankan pentingnya pengelolaan konten digital, konsistensi komunikasi pemasaran, dan interaksi pelanggan. Upaya tersebut perlu disertai pemeliharaan kepercayaan melalui keaslian produk dan kualitas pelayanan. Rekomendasi ini relevan bagi pengelola ritel parfum lokal

latest.title: ANALYSIS OF DIGITAL MARKETING, PRODUCT INNOVATION AND BRAND TRUST ON PURCHASE INTENTION AMONG CONVERSE SHOE CONSUMERS AT DELIPARK MALL MEDAN
latest.venue: International Journal of Economic Business Accounting Agriculture Management and Sharia Administration (IJEBAS)
latest.abstract: Purchase intention is a form of psychological tendency or intention of consumers to purchase a product that arises after evaluating information, perceived value, and marketing interactions. This study aims to determine and analyze the influence of Digital Marketing, Product Innovation, and Brand Trust on the Purchase Intention of Converse shoe consumers at Delipark Mall Medan. This study uses primary data where data was collected using a questionnaire. This research was conducted on Converse shoe consumers at Delipark Mall Medan with a sample of 125 respondents. The results of the analysis show that Digital Marketing has a positive and significant effect on purchase intention. Product Innovation has no significant effect on purchase intention. Brand Trust has no significant effect on purchase intention. The analysis proves that simultaneously Digital Marketing, Product Innovation, and Brand Trust have a significant effect on the Purchase Intention of Converse shoe consumers at Delipark Mall Medan.

latest.title: ANALYSIS OF SOCIAL MEDIA MARKETING, INFLUENCER MARKETING AND WORD OF MOUTH ON PURCHASING DECISIONS AT WAJIR SEAFOOD
latest.venue: International Journal of Economic Business Accounting Agriculture Management and Sharia Administration (IJEBAS)
latest.abstract: This study aims to determine the influence of social media marketing, influencer marketing, and word-of-mouth on purchasing decisions at Wajir Seafood. A quantitative research method was employed. Data sources included both primary and secondary data. The study population consisted of consumers visiting Wajir Seafood, and the sample size was determined using the Lemeshow formula, resulting in a total of 100 respondents. Partial test results indicate that social media marketing has a positive and significant effect on purchasing decisions, with a t-count of 15.542 exceeding the t-table value of 1.984. Similarly, influencer marketing has a positive and significant effect on purchasing decisions, with a t-count of 18.099 exceeding the t-table value of 1.984. The word-of-mouth variable also shows a positive and significant effect on purchasing decisions, with a t-count of 13.486 exceeding the t-table value of 1.984. Simultaneously, it can be concluded that the variables of social media marketing (X1), influencer marketing (X2), and word-of-mouth (X3) collectively exert a positive and significant influence on purchasing decisions at Wajir Seafood.

hot.title: A Glance on Changing Workplace Dynamics Post Covid-19 in India: A Review of Psychological Employee Withdrawal Behavior
hot.abstract: Advances in Consumer Research (Abbreviated as Adv. Consum. Res.) is a distinguished journal based in the United States and published by Sheridan Books. The journal is highly regarded in the academic community, particularly within the fields of Business, Management, and Accounting, with a specific focus on Marketing.

hot.title: The Impact of Visual Elements of Packaging Design on Purchase Intention: Brand Experience as a Mediator in the Tea Bag Product Category
hot.abstract: While packaging design plays a vital role in experience-oriented markets, how multiple visual elements influence purchase intention through brand experience remains unclear. This study addresses this gap by employing innovative orthogonal experiments to examine the complex relationship between the visual elements of packaging design and purchase intention for low-involvement products, integrating both design and marketing perspectives. Through orthogonal experimental design, we developed 14 packaging prototypes as stimuli by systematically manipulating five visual elements (Colour, Graphics, Logo, Typography, and Layout). The framework and prototypes were validated through expert evaluation. Data were collected via a cross-sectional survey from 490 tea bag consumers and analysed using SPSS (version 29.0) for preliminary data processing and Mplus (version 8.3) for structural equation modelling. Our results reveal the direct effects of visual packaging elements on consumer purchase intention. Notably, Colour, Graphics, Logo, and Layout significantly influence purchase intention through brand experience mediation. Importantly, our multi-level analysis of visual elements unveils distinct patterns in how different design levels (e.g., colour harmony, graphic types) affect consumer responses. This study provides novel theoretical insights into how consumers make purchase decisions based on packaging design visual elements, addressing a significant gap in existing research. Unlike previous studies focusing on isolated design elements, our systematic classification and multi-level analysis offer both theoretical insights into packaging design mechanisms and practical guidelines for designers and practitioners.

hot.title: Factors influencing Generation Z’s intention to purchase sustainable clothing products in Vietnam
hot.abstract: The increasing awareness of environmental challenges has significantly influenced consumer behavior, with sustainable products, particularly sustainable clothing, becoming a top priority for Generation Z consumers. This study aims to investigate the factors influencing Generation Z's purchase intentions toward sustainable clothing in Vietnam, guided by the Stimulus-Organism-Response (SOR) model and Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) frameworks. Specifically, it examines the effects of green perceived value, green perceived quality, perceived price, social influence, product design, environmental concern, and environmental knowledge on purchase intentions. The study also explores the mediating roles of environmental attitude and product attitude in these relationships. The research employed a quantitative approach, using a Likert scale questionnaire to gather data from 641 Vietnamese Generation Z consumers. The study utilized exploratory factor analysis (EFA), confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), and structural equation modeling (SEM) to analyze the data. The results revealed that all proposed hypotheses were supported, indicating that all factors significantly impact environmental attitude and product attitude, which, in turn, influence purchase intention. The results emphasize the strong mediating role of environmental attitude and product attitude, suggesting that consumers with positive attitudes toward the environment and products are more likely to intend to purchase sustainable clothing. This research provides valuable insights into the psychological and contextual factors that influence Generation Z's sustainable consumption behavior. For marketers, these findings underscore the need to promote transparency in sustainable practices, emphasize high product quality an

hot.title: Digital Tourism and Smart Development: State-of-the-Art Review
hot.abstract: The intersection between digital technologies and tourism emerges as a prominent area of research within the tourism industry. This is primarily driven by the immense complexity of digital tourism itself as a multifaceted social, economic, and cultural phenomenon. This paper reveals the future implications of tourism in the context of digital intelligence. To gain insights into the latest applications of digital tourism, this work reviews 278 studies spanning from 2012 to 2024. A systematic literature analysis method is proposed to identify the research hotspots and trends. Through value co-creation theory and Schumpeter’s innovation theory, five key trajectories are suggested, as follows: in-depth application of digital technologies in tourism, spawning new scenarios, new forms and new modes of digital tourism, and deep integration of digital economy and tourism real economy. This state-of-the-art review will help to reflect the efforts towards promoting the smart development of digital technologies in tourism.

hot.title: Perceived Value, Consumer Engagement, and Purchase Intention in Virtual Influencer Marketing: The Role of Source Credibility and Generational Cohort
hot.venue: Journal of theoretical and applied electronic commerce research
hot.abstract: As virtual influencers gain popularity, understanding the factors driving consumer responses is essential. However, limited research explores how perceived value (informativeness, entertainment, novelty, and incentives) and consumer engagement influence purchase intention. Perceived value is a key predictor of consumer behavior, while consumer engagement enhances perceived value and marketing effectiveness. Additionally, the moderating roles of source credibility and generational cohort remain underexplored. This study examines these relationships through a survey of 331 Chinese Generation Y and Z consumers, analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM). The results show that informativeness, entertainment, and incentives positively influence purchase intention, while novelty has a negative effect. Consumer engagement drives purchase intention and enhances perceived value. Source credibility and generational cohort moderate these effects. When source credibility is low, novelty reduces purchase intention, while incentives increase it. High source credibility makes consumer engagement more influential. Informativeness enhances purchase intention among Generation Y, whereas Generation Z is more influenced by consumer engagement. This study extends research on advertising value and consumer engagement, offering insights for brands optimizing virtual influencer marketing strategies across different consumer segments.

hot.title: Investigating the factors influencing customer loyalty and the mediating effect of customer satisfaction in online food delivery services: empirical evidence from an emerging market
hot.abstract: This study investigates the factors affecting customer loyalty and the mediating role of customer satisfaction in online food delivery services (OFDS) in Bangladesh. An analysis of 300 responses via structural equation modeling (SEM) revealed that perceived food and service quality alone did not significantly impact customer loyalty. While these qualities are essential, they must enhance customer satisfaction in order to boost loyalty. Significant relationships exist among perceived price, ease of payment, time efficiency, and customer loyalty, with customer satisfaction acting as a crucial mediator. Strategies focusing on pricing, payment convenience, and timely delivery are the most effective for building loyalty. The interplay between perceived quality, pricing, payment, and delivery efficiency enhances the overall customer experience. This study contributes to the literature by applying Attribution Theory and the Technological Acceptance Model (TAM), emphasizing external factors such as pricing, delivery, and payment ease as key loyalty drivers. The findings suggest that OFDS businesses should prioritize reasonable pricing, efficient payment systems, and timely delivery to foster loyalty. Combined with high-quality food and services, these strategies can enhance customer satisfaction, promote business growth, and increase revenue.

hot.title: From Asymmetry to Satisfaction: The Dynamic Role of Perceived Value and Trust to Boost Customer Satisfaction in the Tourism Industry
hot.abstract: The study investigates how information asymmetry affects customer satisfaction in the tourism industry by examining trust and perceived value as mediating factors. The research implements an integrated model to test and prove information asymmetry’s direct and mediating effects on customer satisfaction by examining the literature gap. The research used a quantitative approach based on opinion polls distributed to 408 customers of hotels, tourism companies, and travel agencies who were in Egypt. SmartPLS 3 software implemented the data analysis process using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). Previous studies have developed scales to measure information asymmetry and its related constructs, including customer trust, perceived value, and customer satisfaction. Multiple tests showed that the measurement tools possess both reliability and validity. Results strongly support all hypotheses: information asymmetry demonstrated significant direct negative effects on customer satisfaction (β = −0.187), trust (β = −0.520), and perceived value (β = −0.453). Conversely, customer satisfaction received significant positive direct effects from both trust (β = 0.273) and perceived value (β = 0.263). Importantly, trust (indirect effect β = −0.142) and perceived value (indirect effect β = −0.119) acted as powerful mediators, confirming that information asymmetry diminishes satisfaction largely by eroding these crucial factors. Crucially, the results demonstrate that the negative impact of information asymmetry on customer satisfaction is significantly mediated jointly through two parallel pathways: the erosion of customer trust and the impairment of perceived value. The research adds theoretical support to information asymmetry theory with its findings while als

hot.title: The role of robo-advisors in behavioural finance, shaping investment decisions
hot.abstract: This study focuses on using artificial intelligence-driven financial robo-advisors in the investment decision-making domain by retail investors. Based on heuristic and prospect theory, the researcher aims to examine how AI-powered financial robo-advisors (AIPFRA), through their perceived interactivity, personalisation, autonomy, algorithm interpretation and structural assurance, influence retail investors’ loss aversion and overconfidence biases, ultimately enhancing robo-advisor usage in investment decision-making. Using purposive sampling, data from 461 retail investors were collected and analysed through structural equation modelling using SmartPLS 4.0. The results indicate that, except for structural assurance, robo-advisors’ perceived personalisation, interactivity, autonomy and algorithm transparency substantially mitigated investors’ overconfidence and loss-aversion biases, enhancing robo-advisor usage for investment decision-making. The study highlights the significance of financial literacy in moderating the relationship between biases and the use of robo-advisors. The study contributed by extending Heuristic and Prospect Theories to the AI-driven robo-advisor investment ecosystem. The study comprehensively explains how AI-powered robo-advisor design features impact investor psychology and adoption by bridging behavioural biases such as loss aversion and overconfidence with technology mechanisms like interactivity, personalisation, autonomy, algorithm interpretability and structural assurance. The results can help financial institutions implement user-centric advisory tools and help fintech developers create more bias-aware robo-advisors.

hot.title: The Impact of 7Ps Green Marketing Mix on Customer Commitment and Willingness to Pay a Premium Price: Evidence from Vietnam
hot.abstract: As consumers prioritize environmental issues and sustainable development, using green elements in marketing strategy has become valuable. This research examines how the 7Ps green marketing mix influences customer commitment and willingness to pay a premium price for green products, focusing on the role of green brand loyalty, association, and perceived quality. A PLS-SEM analysis of survey data from 571 young Vietnamese consumers reveals that different green 7Ps components exert distinct effects on green consumer-based brand equity (CBBE). While prior research largely focuses on green product, price, place and promotion, limited attention has been given to green human factors, process, and physical evidence, which this study addresses. The findings of this study not only confirm the significant influence of green CBBE dimensions on consumer commitment and willingness to pay a premium price but also enriches the green marketing and consumer behavior literature. Moreover, these provide practical strategies for businesses and policymakers in emerging markets to effectively leverage green marketing, strengthen consumer commitment, implement premium pricing strategies, and contribute to advancing the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

hot.title: The push-pull-mooring model of consumer service switching: a meta-analytical review to guide future research
hot.venue: Journal of Service Theory and Practice
hot.abstract: Purpose For nearly 2 decades, the push-pull-mooring (PPM) model has been used frequently by scholars to explain consumers’ service switching intention and behavior. However, heterogeneity and incomparability between PPM model studies are prevalent issues: The chosen predictor variables, their categorization, their measurement, reported effect sizes, and effect directions vary considerably. By addressing these issues, the present meta-analytical review enables future researchers applying the PPM model to identify relevant variables and use valid measurements. Design/methodology/approach Based on 148 empirical studies employing the PPM model, the variables used to predict consumers’ service switching intention and behavior, their frequency of use, their categorization into push, pull, and mooring factors, and their measurement are assessed. The effect sizes and directions of the relationships between these variables and consumers’ service switching intention and behavior are analyzed using meta-analytic structural equation modeling. Additionally, the predictive capacity of this model and the influence of moderators are assessed. Findings Among the 148 empirical studies, 382 different independent variables were used. The three most frequently used and distinctly categorized independent variables are dissatisfaction (push), alternative attractiveness (pull), and switching costs (mooring). Overall, 152 unique sources were cited to measure these variables and the dependent variables. Dissatisfaction and alternative attractiveness increase switching intention, which positively affects switching behavior, while switching costs decrease switching intention. The model explains 30% of the variance in switching intention and 31% of the variance in switching behavior. Originality/va

hot.title: Impulsive Buying Tendencies and Personality: Cognitive and Affective Aspects
hot.abstract: Impulsive buying is a growing problem in modern society with significant financial and psychological consequences, and it is necessary to examine the mechanisms underlying it. Understanding the mechanisms driving this behavior is crucial. Impulsive buying consists of two key aspects: a cognitive aspect, characterized by a lack of planning and reflection, and an affective aspect, involving emotional responses that can occur before, during, or after a purchase. This study aims to explore the relationship between personality traits, as measured by the HEXACO model, and tendencies toward impulsive buying. Specifically, it examines how the HEXACO traits differentially predict the cognitive and affective components of impulsive buying tendencies. Data were collected from a sample of 420 students, with 32 excluded due to incomplete responses, resulting in a final sample of 388 students (155 men, 233 women) with an average age of 22.8. Hierarchical regression analyses revealed that HEXACO personality domains significantly predicted overall impulsive buying tendencies. As expected, Honesty–Humility and Conscientiousness were negatively associated with impulsive buying, while Emotionality and Extraversion positively predicted impulsive buying tendencies. Moreover, Honesty–Humility, Conscientiousness, and Extraversion significantly predicted the cognitive component of impulsive buying, while Honesty–Humility and Emotionality were significant predictors of the affective component. These findings suggest the importance of educating individuals, from an early age, on the negative consequences of impulsive buying, effective money-saving strategies, and the principles of mental accounting.

hot.title: Impulse buying in live streaming commerce: A literature review and research agenda
hot.abstract: Impulse buying in live streaming commerce (LSC) is an emerging phenomenon characterized by spontaneous, unplanned purchases driven by real-time social interactions. Despite increasing scholarly attention, the existing literature remains fragmented, lacking consensus on antecedents, theoretical perspectives, and outcomes. This fragmentation hinders theoretical development and accumulation of knowledge of this research stream. To address these issues, this study provides a systematic review of impulse buying in LSC, synthesizing key research trends, theoretical foundations, and methodological approaches. Drawing on the stimulus-organism-response (S-O-R) framework, we propose an integrative framework that consolidates antecedents, psychological mechanisms, and outcomes of impulse buying within LSC. This comprehensive synthesis clarifies existing inconsistencies and offers structured avenues for future research. For practitioners, our framework identifies critical platform features, streamer attributes, and consumer characteristics that influence impulse buying, enabling more effective strategies and responsible practices in LSC.

hot.title: Anthropomorphism in artificial intelligence: a game-changer for brand marketing
hot.abstract: Abstract The expansion of brands adopting artificial intelligence services with human characteristics, such as chatbots, has revolutionized digital marketing strategies, transforming how companies reach and engage customers. This technological innovation is reshaping digital interactions between companies and consumers, offering a more personalized and efficient experience. This study explores the influence of chatbot anthropomorphism on customer engagement and purchasing decision-making with brands that use this artificial intelligence service. Data from a questionnaire with 1319 participants was analyzed using partial least squares method. Chatbot anthropomorphism has a more positive influence on purchasing decision-making when this relationship is mediated by customer engagement. In turn, customer involvement also has a positive influence on decision-making. The results emphasize that for a greater influence of the chatbot's anthropomorphism on purchasing decision-making, the customer must first be engaged with the chatbot. This research illuminates a new path in the domain of AI-enabled brand interactions, showing the distinct influence of anthropomorphism in chatbots on customer satisfaction, trust and loyalty, thus revolutionizing traditional paradigms of consumer-brand engagement and decision-making processes. By exploring the intricate dynamics between customer engagement with anthropomorphized chatbots and purchasing decisions, this study breaks new ground, offering unprecedented insight into the transformative potential of human-like chatbot interactions in shaping consumer behavior and brand relationships.

hot.title: Drivers of Purchase Intentions of Generation Z on Eco-Products
hot.abstract: Concerns about environmental protection and sustainable consumption increased among Generation Z, as a consequence of more perceived risks emerging in the context of climate change and depletion of natural resources. The aim of the present research was to identify the main factors that influence the intention to purchase eco-products among the young generation. Quantitative marketing research was carried out on a sample of 269 Gen Z. The research results proved that purchasing intention for eco-products is strongly influenced by the perceived quality of environmentally friendly products, consumer consciousness about eco-products, perceived value of green products, and consumer trust in ecological products. Lower influences were recorded in terms of perceived price and perceived availability of eco-products, with improved total effects when considering the mediating role of eco-trust. Consequently, the provision of eco-products could lead to image benefits for organizations.

hot.title: Electroencephalography Studies on Marketing Stimuli: A Literature Review and Future Research Agenda
hot.abstract: ABSTRACT This study aims to explore the application of electroencephalography (EEG) tools in examining latent consumer behavior, emphasizing emotions, attention, preferences, memory, and decision‐making in response to various marketing stimuli (e.g., products, pricing, branding, and advertising). This study adopts a thematic review approach, employing a systematic literature review methodology (e.g., Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta‐Analyses [PRISMA] protocol). Our investigation unearthed 155 articles from the Scopus and Web of Science databases, spanning 2010–2023. The findings reveal a marked increase in EEG‐related research, underscoring its effectiveness in examining consumers' reactions to marketing stimuli. This rise reflects a growing recognition among researchers of EEG's ability to address marketing research challenges, particularly in advertising, product development, branding, and pricing. EEG research predominantly targets advertising, followed by products, branding, and pricing, and delves deeply into consumer behavior aspects such as emotional, cognitive, and decision‐making processes. The study further highlights EEG's cutting‐edge potential to predict ad success, optimize product features, and refine pricing strategies with unprecedented accuracy. Specifically, emotion‐based ads profoundly influence decision‐making, offering novel insights into consumers' emotional engagement. This study emphasizes EEG's groundbreaking role in minimizing verbal biases and revealing consumer behavior, which is increasingly recognized as critical for developing more effective marketing strategies. This review underscores EEG's theoretical and practical contributions and offers pioneering insights into marketing effectiveness and consumer engagement

hot.title: From perceived green product quality to purchase intention: the roles of price sensitivity and environmental concern
hot.abstract: Purpose This research seeks to address the existing gaps in the literature by rigorously investigating the influence of consumers’ perceived green product quality (PPQ), price sensitivity to green products (PRS) and environmental concern (ENC) on their intention to purchase green products (GPI) within the context of green circular economies. Furthermore, the study will explore the role of PRS as a mediator and ENC as a moderator by applying the price-expectancy model (PEM) and social exchange theory (SET). Design/methodology/approach The purposive sampling technique was employed to analyse 412 online survey responses from consumers, utilising partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM). Findings The findings indicate a positive relationship between PPQ and PRS and PRS and GPI, contradicting the hypothesised negative associations. This suggests that as consumers become increasingly price-sensitive, they perceive green products to possess higher quality without diminishing their purchase intentions. Additionally, PPQ is positively associated with GPI, implying that enhanced perceptions of quality directly contribute to an increased intention to purchase green products. Furthermore, the results demonstrate that while ENC moderates the relationship between PPQ and PRS, its practical significance is limited. Practical implications This research emphasises to marketers that they should prioritise quality features while addressing PRS, particularly for environmentally concerned consumers, which can effectively shape consumers’ GPI. Originality/value This study’s originality lies in its integration of PRS and ENC within green consumerism. This offers valuable insights into green marketing and provides marketers with practical strategies to tackle the challenge

hot.title: Decomposing Brand Loyalty: An Examination of Loyalty Subcomponents, Product Price Range, Consumer Personality, and Willingness to Pay
hot.abstract: Brand loyalty is widely recognized as a key driver of consumer behavior, significantly influencing their willingness to pay more for preferred brands. This study explores the relationship between brand loyalty, its components, willingness to pay, consumer personality traits, and product price range. A tailored online survey involving participants aged 18 to 60 revealed a strong positive correlation between brand loyalty and increased willingness to pay. The findings also underscore the influence of Conscientiousness and Energy on brand loyalty, alongside the moderating effect of product price range. Specifically, habit-based loyalty dominates low-priced, routine purchases, while higher-priced decisions involve deeper cognitive-affective evaluations. These insights offer valuable guidance for enhancing customer satisfaction and optimizing brand profitability.

hot.title: Unveiling the enigma of blind box impulse buying curiosity: The moderating role of price consciousness
hot.abstract: This study explores the causes of curiosity-driven impulse buying in blind boxes using the Stimulus-Organism-Response (S-O-R) model and adaptation level theory. It examines how store environment and product factors contribute to customer curiosity, incorporating price consciousness into the overall framework. Insights from an online survey of 306 Chinese respondents indicate that environmental factors and specific product characteristics positively influence consumer curiosity, while price consciousness has a negative moderate effect. The findings also show that customer curiosity stimulates impulse buying behavior and mediates the relationship between store atmosphere, surprise, and perceived novelty. This study identifies both objective and subjective factors behind blind box impulse buying and offers relevant suggestions for governments and consumers on managing impulse buying.

hot.title: Factors Influencing the Use of Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL) Payments
hot.abstract: This article focuses on the fastest-growing consumer credit segment usually associated with e-commerce, but increasingly offered for brick-and-mortar shopping too.The purpose of the study was to identify how, and the extent to which, specific aspects of consumer behaviour -particularly in terms of attitudes towards money management, and socio-demographics -influence the use of BNPL.The reasons are socio-demographic, economic, psychological and technological.The article incorporates a broad literature review of the motives behind consumers' use of BNPL as well as an original empirical survey among a representative sample of Poles, conducted using the CAWI technique.The impact and strength of individual factors for choosing BNPL were identified via a logistic regression model.The statistical significance of the selected variables was then evaluated, followed by the elimination of non-significant variables from the model.It helped select statistically significant factors for using BNPL.Among 7 statistically significant variables, 3 relate to socio-demographic features of the respondents -level of education, income and gender.Personal innovativeness, inclination towards going into debt, as well as a family history of taking various loans slightly increase the probability of opting for BNPL.It had been presumed that propensity to save would have a negative effect, and that optimism would have a positive influence, on choosing BNPL; however, this presumption was not demonstrated.Nor do consumerism and impulsiveness in making purchases affect the likelihood of using BNPL.Of all the statistically significant factors underlying decisions to choose BNPL, the consumer's use of LendTech has the greatest impact, increasing the chance of using BNPL.This suggests that similar consumer

hot.title: Trends and development in green and sustainability marketing: a bibliometrics analysis using VOSviewer
hot.abstract: The recent global environmental crisis and climate change have prompted greater interest among global citizens in sustainability issues. Consumers are demanding more to be done by product and service suppliers to ensure sustainability. This has sparked research and academic interest in understanding how various organisations position themselves from a sustainability perspective. This study emerges from the need to understand trends and developments in sustainability marketing. To this end, this study uses bibliometric data from the Scopus database to examine this development. The data were analysed using Microsoft Excel and VOSviewer. The study found significant growth in the literature on green and sustainable marketing which is indicative of the subject over the past couple of years. In many respects green marketing is seen by many enterprises as playing a central role in shaping consumer perceptions and brand loyalty in many markets. However, green marketing and sustainability face various challenges such as misleading claims and greenwashing which threaten consumer confidence in sustainability efforts. Overall, this study found that integrating sustainability into marketing strategies fosters environmental responsibility, builds consumer trust, and enhances business performance. In addition, frameworks such as the theory of planned behaviour (TPB) provide a foundation for understanding consumers’ green attitudes and adoption behaviour. Greenwashing can be addressed by transparency, education, and regulatory compliance. Finally, practical recommendations include fostering international cooperation, developing targeted capacity-building initiatives, and leveraging sustainability marketing to achieve the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
